0.content:
Ameyalco Waters (also: Ameyalco): Ameyalco Waters is a coastal stretch of Natlan's Toyac Springs, in the land of the People of the Springs. It is a body of water formed where springs meet the coast, slightly warmer than the surrounding coastal waters, a warmth the official description attributes to magma chambers beneath. It is a place of surfing, Koholasaur riding and the Spiritway.

The name is Nahuatl, meaning "natural springs" or "at the spring". Toyac Springs, its parent area, is the home of the tribe that lives alongside the Koholasaurs and is known for hot springs and relaxing music.

Geography: Warm sea-and-spring water on the Natlan coast, with islands (one in the southeast starts a world quest) and an Underground Lava River that the story quests reach through a whirlpool. Its listed points include the Upper Sanctum and the Underground Lava River.

The local specialty is the Sprayfeather Gill. Exploration features are Everflame Seeds, Flaming Seeds of Phlogiston, Jet-Set Eddies, Saurian Indwelling and the Spiritway, a course of flowing Phlogiston for Koholasaur riders, used here for sprint challenges.

People: Residents named by the wiki are Anela, Aphila, Iwai, Pania and Rongo, plus the Master Trainers Avuia and Tepache, who are listed as "People of the Springs". A Koholasaurus also appears as an NPC.

Mualani, the tribe's guide, and her teacher Nuu appear in the area's story quests. Rongo gives the world quest in which the Traveler passes a surfing test and a Spiritway test.

Dangers: Common enemies are wild Koholasaurs and Yumkasaurs with their whelps, Flowing Blade fighters (Grease-Saw, Harpoon-Thrower, Skirmisher), Swiftstep couriers, seekers and scouts, and Koholasaurus Warriors. Elites are the Anemo Hilichurl Rogue and the Flow-Inverted Wayob Manifestation.

Quests: The Tribal Chronicle "Journey to the Mysterious Island" (Where the Springs Return, Act III, version 5.0, Mualani's story) runs through the area: Someone Trustworthy, Where the Koholasaurs Gather, The Riddle of Sea and Sky and The Mysterious Island's Truth, the last entering a whirlpool into an underground cave. World quest "Stride on Rainbows, Split the Waves" (Rongo) and the daily commission "Swelling Springs" (a Spiritway sprint) are also here.

In Where the Koholasaurs Gather the party sneaks deeper into a valley and examines graffiti on a stone wall; in The Riddle of Sea and Sky, a trial Mualani activates Phlogiston Nodes to switch Spiritway paths and the party then rescues the client Viramdra and investigates the whirlpool.

Culture: The Toyac Springs tribe is called the most popular with visitors from afar, and its guides, such as the top guide Koolau, take clients to hard-to-reach places; in Someone Trustworthy Koolau passes a client, Viramdra, to Mualani, and Mualani notes that even her teacher Nuu could not reach the Mysterious Island.

Status as of 7.1: Open and unchanged as of 7.1; no appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content was found.

1.content: Ameyalco Waters is the warm-water coast of Toyac Springs, in People of the Springs territory, where Koholasaurs are ridden along the Spiritway and Mualani guides outsiders.

2.content:
Ancestral Temple (also: Temple of Ancient Forebears): The Ancestral Temple is a sacred site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan where people once communicated with the Night Kingdom. Today the tribes have a steadier link to the Night Kingdom, so the temple is unused, but it is still holy ground, guarded by the Scions of the Canopy.

Legba says only experienced Couriers who have passed three trials may enter. The in-game description evokes ancestors who made sacrifices here and prayed for a revelation that would change everything.

Geography: A subarea of Coatepec Mountain. Features include Nightsoul Totems, relay balls and ball path converters, and removable grappling hooks, so crossing it involves Nightsoul puzzles.

Several damaged stone tablets are scattered through the temple; their texts are on the wiki and are not summarised here.

People: Legba, the Scions of the Canopy's contact, is the NPC placed here. The Scions of the Canopy keep guard.

Culture: Natlan's tribes treat the Night Kingdom as a realm tied to their dead and to Nightsoul. The temple is the older way in; the tribes later set up a more stable route. In the expedition text the land is described as one that did not belong entirely to humans, whose primitive elemental forces drained the soil's vitality.

History: Natlan's ancestors offered sacrifices here to their god and sought a revelation that would alter everything, according to the expedition description. When the tribes found a steadier connection to the Night Kingdom, the temple lost its practical role.

Atmosphere: Austere, stony and ceremonial, with Nightsoul machinery and an air of restriction: a place that is respected rather than visited casually.

Travel: Entry is restricted to experienced Couriers who have passed three trials, per Legba.

The temple's quests are listed on the wiki under Ancestral Temple Quests, and a soundtrack is assigned to the area; the wiki's etymology and lore sections for it are empty, so no more can be said from sources read.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple is disused but guarded, and remains holy ground.

3.comment: Ancestral Temple: Legba and the Three Trials
3.content: Legba, a Scions of the Canopy figure, explains in To the Night, What is the Night's that only Couriers who have passed three trials may enter the temple. Further details of Legba belong to his own entry, not here.

4.content:
Ancient Mountain Path (also: Flowfire Experimentation Site): The Ancient Mountain Path is an old route on the volcano slopes of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Flowfire Experimentation Site, an ancient research station where dragon scholars worked out how to turn liquid Phlogiston into stone while the war against the powers of the heavens loomed. The station was abandoned long ago and is kept only by stone constructs.

It opens to the Traveler through a hidden exploration objective in Atocpan that begins by waking a giant stone serpent, a Secret Source Dragon Idol.

Geography: A subarea of Atocpan, on the lava-fed slopes of the Great Volcano of Tollan. The Flowfire Experimentation Site has a surface level and a deeper level, both reached by following the stone serpent into the cavern. A geothermal vent can be found among the exploration features here.

The lower floor of the site is where the readable records are left. Liquid Phlogiston and lava flow through the workings, which suits experiments on the state of Phlogiston.

Places: The Flowfire Experimentation Site, with a surface area and a lower level. The records on the lower level are two golden-lit memory traces: an experimental report and a researcher's notes.

Defence is handled by two kinds of construct named in the notes: the Secret Source Servant and the Secret Source Dragon Idol, set up as periodic defence mechanisms. The stone serpent that guides visitors is a Dragon Idol.

People: No living inhabitants are shown. The only presence is the unnamed researcher who wrote the notes, long gone, and the constructs left behind.

The researcher writes warmly of the constructs, saying they have no true emotion modules yet seem sad to see their keeper leave, and dismisses this as a researcher's folly.

History: The experimental report records Experiment 150: the Type-01 Phlogiston Converter did turn liquid Phlogiston at the site into a solid. Extracting Phlogiston from it showed that the product was not solid Phlogiston but another sort of rock, the same stone formed when gaseous Phlogiston fuses with stone, as often happens in eruptions of the Tollan volcano. The researchers judged it interesting but not practical for their needs.

The report goes on to say that time was short. To resist and prevent the descent of enemies from beyond the sky, the 'State Change' device was to turn Phlogiston into sturdier fortifications on top of Tollan Volcano. The writer ends with a line of devotion to the nation.

In the researcher's notes the war has begun and the converter research is finished. Lord Kukulkan had ordered such experiments to be done outside the Sacred Mountain, which the writer thinks may have been meant to protect dissenters like them. They hope that all factions will unite in the face of the real threat and that Kukulkan and the Chamber of Deliberation might reconcile. There was no time to retrieve most materials, so the writer returned to the Sacred City with the data only, trusting in victory and intending to carry everything back later.

The notes do not say whether the writer came back. The site still holds its materials and the constructs still keep their post.

Atmosphere: Heat and low light from the lava, ancient stone and a faint sadness: a workshop whose keeper never returned in any record, tended only by machines that keep waiting.

Dangers: The site is guarded by constructs set up as periodic defences. Lava, geothermal heat and Phlogiston currents are the other hazards.

A Pulverite barrier has to be smashed to proceed in the exploration objective.

Travel: Reached from Atocpan by completing the first step of the hidden exploration objective; a hidden teleport waypoint is unlocked inside.

Finishing the objective ends with riding the stone serpent. It also yields two Pyroculi, a furnishing blueprint and the achievement 'A Lonely Sentinel' (game rewards, not lore).

Quests: How Long Must We Wait, My Friend? (an unofficial wiki name for a hidden exploration objective). The Traveler wakes the serpent, follows it into the cavern, runs the converter mechanism, and finally rides it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the site is still abandoned and open to exploration.

Nothing in canon through 7.1 says that the researcher returned.

5.comment: Ancient Mountain Path: Flowfire Experimentation Site
5.content: An ancient research station on the Ancient Mountain Path where dragon researchers tested a device that changed liquid Phlogiston into solid form. The first successful run produced a stone rather than solid Phlogiston, a result they put aside as impractical. The researchers intended to use a 'State Change' device to build fortifications from Phlogiston atop Tollan Volcano against attackers from beyond the sky. The writer of the notes left the site guarded by a Secret Source Servant and a Secret Source Dragon Idol.

key: Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain
6.content:
Ancient Sacred Mountain (also: Sacred City of Tollan, Sacred City, Tollan, Land of Primal Flame, Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain): The Ancient Sacred Mountain is the huge hollow inside the Great Volcano of Tollan in southwestern Natlan. It holds the Sacred City of Tollan, the capital of Natlantea, the dragon civilisation that ruled Natlan before human tribes. Its creator and master, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, was killed there when the human hero Xbalanque stormed the city, and Xbalanque died with him before being reborn as the first Pyro Archon. The city was then sealed for millennia and overrun by the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler, Paimon and the young saurian Little One leapt into the crater, restarted the city's machinery and reached its Heart. There Little One refused to activate Huitzilopochtli, a dragon device that would have burned all Natlan into phlogiston.

Today it is a terraced ruin lit by artificial suns (Astral Assemblages), crossed by rivers of liquid phlogiston and tended only by Secret Source machines. The map calls it the holy city of a proud nobility older than the tribes' woven-scroll histories, of which only a lonely tomb remains.

History: Xiuhcoatl was born from the primal flame on this mountain. He shaped the Sacred City there and moulded the Dragonborn from the primal flame. After the Heavenly Principles defeated the dragon sovereigns he lay in a false death while his brother Kukulkan ruled as Regent. When Nibelung returned, Xiuhcoatl woke corrupted by the Abyss. In his short spells of clarity he rebuilt the city and created the Astral Assemblages and Huitzilopochtli. Xbalanque's army later broke into Tollan, and he killed Xiuhcoatl by striking the eye that served as the array's control hub. The two Golden Entreaties that could start the array were split between Xbalanque and Kukulkan, and the city was sealed.

The Chamber of Deliberation's records show the city's last politics. The Thirteen Sovereign Lords voted to impeach Kukulkan for giving phlogiston to humans; Awanyu says the trial collapsed into farce when Xiuhcoatl appeared during a lucid spell. A motion to burn down large human settlements failed. During the war the Lords voted to execute the Eighth Lord, who had raised the human Lianca as her daughter. Xbalanque's forces came in through the Skyfire Circlet, and he and Xiuhcoatl fell together into the volcano's depths. Xbalanque was then reborn as the Pyro Archon.

According to Awanyu, the Three Princes died fighting humanity, ten of the Thirteen Lords fell when Tollan collapsed, one remained in Chichen Uctokah, and one survives today in a form it would not have chosen. Memories in the phlogiston pools add that after the war the city went dark. Some dragons abandoned wisdom and form to survive in a land now ruled by humans, and others burned out. A lone silver-white figure kept returning to the pools to meet remembered faces there. By oath, only a human can open the city's seals. Over time the Abyss took over the volcano, and it corroded the Heart worst of all. Kukulkan later admitted that he created the legend of the Chosen of Dragons (he also calls the Jade of Return non-existent). It was meant to draw a human and a saurian with Xiuhcoatl's bloodline here, carrying both Entreaties, since Xbalanque's oath meant a human had to bring back the other Entreaty.

Geography: The city lies inside the active volcano that makes up Atocpan, which ancient scrolls already called the "Sacred Mountain". The only way in is the crater at the Skyfire Circlet, choked with gaseous phlogiston. Below lie an upper city (the map's "Dragons' Residence"), deeper districts reached by the central Celestial Axis lift, and finally the Heart of the Sacred Mountain, a great fissure beneath everything.

Liquid phlogiston fills pools and falls everywhere, and in the Heart of Force Inversion it flows upward. Secret Source Servants can lay down patches of solid phlogiston, and a Coagulation Pearl can freeze a whole fall into a pillar. Three Astral Assemblages hang over the upper city and feed beams to the pillars of the Celestial Axis. Below the cloud layer the ruins are thick with Abyssal mud.

Places: Summoning Hall (the entrance, under the crater); Sea of Shifting Sentience (phlogiston pools where dragons absorbed stored knowledge); Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds (birthplace of the first Astral Assemblage); Celestial Axis; Chamber of Deliberation (the Lords' council hall); Heart of the Sacred Mountain (the primal flame's heart and Huitzilopochtli).

Also: the Esoteric Arrays, an old calculation array; the Heart of Force Inversion; the Ruined Armament Workshop, a weapons works where dragons seem also to have experimented on humans; and the Pseudostar Pedestal, where a workshop engraving in Xiuhcoatl's voice curses Tollan's enemies and swears the city will survive both the "usurper of the sky" and the earth's "black tides". The viewpoint Court of the Dragons says the Chamber became a place where "dragon cast down dragon" once its master was gone.

People: No living people or dragons remain. Secret Source Servants maintain the city. A nameless prototype, built to help Xiuhcoatl record information, says no humans had come this far down in at least 500 years. A guiding voice speaks through dormant servants under names of the fallen (Ehecatl, Amaru, Awanyu), and the finale strongly implies it is Kukulkan's. In the Heart, dragons who gave up their bodies for phlogiston form still dream on a dead king's decree.

Amaru's namesake was an arrogant dragon who held the threshold of the Celestial Axis until he died, and a servant that once waited on him now stands there. The voice despises the Chamber's lords as power-hungry fools, and hints that they once regarded it as a criminal.

Atmosphere: Heat, silence and gold light. Phlogiston pools glow under artificial suns. Golden inscriptions replay old voices when touched, and patient machines whirr awake, speak and fall silent. The city is grand and dead at once. Lower down, black Abyssal mud covers the stone.

Dangers: The Abyss is the main threat. Floating Oozing Cores fire Abyssal bolts, black mud drains health, and Abyss Mages, Rifthounds and Mimifloras roam the ruins. Some of the city's own defences still work, including a golden purifying barrier that consumes friend and foe alike. Liquid and gaseous phlogiston are dangerous in themselves.

Oozing Cores break only to phlogiston explosions or a Tatankasaurus charge, and the mud prevents sprinting. The Heart's Astral Assemblages attack anyone without a permit, and in the finale a Source Dragon Mech guards the Heart. An Astral Assemblage that touches the Abyss either destroys itself together with it or is corrupted by it.

Travel: Climb the Skyfire Circlet, usually by riding Atocpan's Spiritways, and jump into the crater; the Traveler learned the way by watching a Qucusaur dive in carrying a stolen statue. Restarting the Celestial Axis opens the depths. The Heart needs a Permit to the Sacred Heart and three Phlogiston Units to wake its guardian Secret Source Dragon Idol.

Gameplay (labelled): a separate map whose levels unlock with quest progress. Dropping from an upper level to a lower one turns the player into a fireball that lands on nearby ground, with no loss of HP or Energy.

Quests: Path to the Flaming Peaks (the leap into the crater); Chronicler of the Crumbling City (restarting the Assemblages, winning the permit, cleansing the ruins, descending to the Heart); A Finale Emberforged (An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty, the end of Little One's story; see the finale entry).

Chapter parts: The Frozen, Rekindling Land with The Forsaken Sea of Wisdom and Sealed Site of Sacrifice; In Search of a Hidden Heart with Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment, Where Once There Was a Calculation Array, Where Once Force Was Reversed, Where Once There Were Arms Aplenty and The End of the Road; As the Burning Sun Sears Shadows.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred City is an open but ruined area. It has been unsealed, much of the Abyss has been cleared, and Huitzilopochtli was not activated. Kukulkan faded away at the Heart, and Little One, freed of the Flamelord's Blessing, is a small Tepetlisaurus again.

This research found no 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 story content that returns here. Kukulkan warned that the city no longer had the energy to sustain the dragons living on as phlogiston and that they would perish without the primal flame's authority; once the maintenance functions failed, the wiki reads them as fading with him, though no scene shows it directly.

7.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: The finale in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain
7.content: In An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (5.5), the Traveler and Little One offer the two Golden Entreaties in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. A Source Dragon Mech traps the Traveler and Paimon. Guided by Kukulkan, Little One briefly takes a "mature dragon" form with the power of speech. Kukulkan reveals himself as the Sage of the Stolen Flame and shows him the Heart. He asks Little One to start Huitzilopochtli and rule a phlogiston world as a renewed Pyro Dragon Sovereign. Little One foresees an empty, eternal white world and cancels the array. He will not put the Traveler and Paimon at risk. He breaks back to them, the Mech is defeated and the Flamelord's Blessing is lifted. Kukulkan, alone by the array, admits he made the same choice long ago and fades. The volcano shakes, but only lets out a little smoke.

8.content:
Huitzilopochtli, the "Sweeping Skyfire" or Natlan Phlogistonization Array, is the last great device of the ancient dragons. It stands in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain beneath the Great Volcano of Tollan. Kukulkan explained it to Little One. Xiuhcoatl built it to burn everything in Natlan and copy its information into phlogiston, turning the land into a realm of primal flame. Astral Assemblages would then destroy the Abyss on contact. Living things would either die or give up their bodies and become phlogiston lifeforms, and draconic ones would rule the new world. The array is started by the two Golden Entreaties, made from Xiuhcoatl's pupils, and needs three confirmations to activate or cancel. In 5.5 Little One cancelled it.

Towers placed across Natlan anchored the array's reach. Och-Kan ordered most of them destroyed, but their fragments still serve, because a single stone can carry Iridescent Inscriptions. Kukulkan describes phlogiston as matter that can store information and imitate anything through those inscriptions, which explains the phantom scenes replayed in the city.

9.content: Astral Assemblages (Tzitzimimeh) are floating balls of phlogiston, pressed together into controllable miniature suns. Xiuhcoatl made the first at the Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds of the Sacred City, and the cold voice guiding the Traveler (taken to be Kukulkan) compared the feat to "lunar reconstruction". Their purpose is to fight the Abyss by mutual annihilation, but they cannot tell friend from foe. Three hang over the upper city and power the Celestial Axis. During The Frozen, Rekindling Land the Traveler stabilised the two that had been sealed or drained.

10.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Chamber of Deliberation (Sacred City)
10.content: The Chamber of Deliberation is where the Thirteen Sovereign Lords of Natlantea met, with the First Lord as Speaker, to vote on government and judgment. Its records, written in phlogiston, survive. One is a vote to impeach Regent Kukulkan, with the Second Lord's argument erased and Kukulkan's mocking reply later surfacing over it. Another is a failed motion to burn down large human settlements. A third is the vote that condemned the Eighth Lord for her loyalty to her adopted human daughter Lianca. The Chamber still has working defences and a self-repair system. The Permit to the Sacred Heart was kept above it.

11.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Secret Source Servants of Tollan
11.content: In the Sacred City, Secret Source Servants are dragon-made machines that still guard and maintain the ruins. A voice borrowed three of them to guide the Traveler and Little One, naming each after one of the fallen. Ehecatl was a servant a Qucusaur had stolen from the Tephric Ruins. Amaru was named after an arrogant lord who held the Celestial Axis to his death. Awanyu was named after a scribe of the Chamber of Deliberation. After the quest, Ehecatl's dormant body can be returned to the Tephric Ruins. A separate nameless prototype, built to help Xiuhcoatl record information, also speaks to them.

12.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Och-Kan's origins in Tollan
12.content: Two texts in the Sacred City concern Kukulkan's son. In the "Flamestealer's" record, Kukulkan rejoices at the birth of a son with dragon blood whose looks would fool even his brother. He refuses to raise the boy as a mere dragon lord, and wonders whether to send him away rather than steer every choice he makes. The Nest Experiment Log in the Ruined Armament Workshop tells of a child-like test subject thrown among vishaps. The child grew strong, shared food with the vishaps and showed fear and empathy. After a "neutralization injection" the subject escaped, and the Regent called off the hunt, saying he had dealt with it personally. Present this as dragon records, not as a scene to dramatise.

13.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Last words of the Sovereign Lords
13.content: The Iridescent Legacy is four inscribed messages from Sovereign Lords who died as Tollan fell. The First Lord welcomed Xbalanque as a worthy foe and admitted that the dragons' civilisation had stagnated. The Seventh marvelled that humans kept coming despite their frailty. The Fifth cursed the humans' "crude misuse of phlogiston" and still believed Xiuhcoatl would burn them away. The Twelfth realised too late that a human leader had outwitted her and that her own kind had decayed. The first message is in the Skyfire Circlet, the others in the Heart of Force Inversion, the Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds and the Sea of Shifting Sentience.

14.content:
Ancient Watchtower: The Ancient Watchtower is a domain in Natlan's Coatepec Mountain area, a ruin of enormous structures built long ago by the dragons of the land. Legend says those colossal beasts, having explored all the land and sea, raised these towers to look out toward the wider world beyond the sky. The dragons are long gone, and nobody today knows the true purpose of the place.

In-game it is a Forgery domain: clearing it yields weapon ascension materials. Its flavour text says the great dragon built many peculiar structures across the land and that old legends describe its outstretched wings blotting out the sky; the text wonders whether that was literal or a metaphor for the longing to see past the sky (the Sea of Stars). Only shattered remnants of the massive structures, and the patterns on them, let present-day people glimpse the forging techniques of that vanished civilisation.

Atmosphere: Vast broken masonry and pattern-marked fragments of giant structures under the Natlan sky; a silent monument to a people who looked upward and then disappeared.

Dangers: Gameplay layer (not in-world fact): the challenge pits the party against Yumkasaurs and their whelps, Swiftstep opponents (Seekers, Armed Couriers, Storm Scouts) and, as the final target, a Secret Source Automaton: Hunter-Seeker. Its Ley Line Disorder rewards Nightsoul Burst: once triggered, all party members deal 35% more DMG for 10 seconds, and Natlan characters make this easiest.

Rewards are weapon ascension materials rotating by weekday, in the series Scrying Shadows, Attentive Observation and Estimation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is permanently accessible in Natlan. It carries no named plot; the dragons that built it are described as long vanished.

15.comment: Ancient Watchtower: Dragon builders of the Ancient Watchtower
15.content: The domain description attributes the watchtower-like structures to the ancient dragon civilisation of Natlan and says they were an attempt to see beyond the sky. This is flavour text from the domain; no quest explains the structures further, so treat the stated purpose as a legend ("Legend has it...") and not as confirmed history.

16.content:
Ashflow Street (also: The Unfinished Ashen City): Ashflow Street is a dead settlement at the foot of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams in the ruined island of Ochkanatlan, Natlan. The in-game viewpoint calls it the Unfinished Ashen City: a place where people tried to found a new country on the ruins of a city built by a forgotten race, and where only ash remains. The alliance that gathered to build it has long since scattered.

It is a Version 5.2 location in the Ochkanatlan area. What a visitor finds are fragments: scrolls, recordings and a tower, left by priests, rangers, scholars and young mystics from different ages.

Because the notes are damaged and blanked in places, treat the street as a place of half-sentences. A scene set here should never deliver a full explanation.

Geography: Ashflow Street sits at the base of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams, the castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan. Vucub Caquix Tower stands in the middle of the street. The soundtrack Ashes of Presumption plays there.

Ranger notes found in the tower say the terrain on the way is far more tangled than expected; the writer blames Abyssal erosion for ruining roads that ought to have been passable, and says they marked the way for the return trip.

Places: - **Vucub Caquix Tower:** a tower in the middle of the street, with a lower level reached by an elevator. Several scrolls and notes lie inside.
- **Cradle of Fleeting Dreams:** the castle-like structure above the street.
- **Recordkeeping Secret Source Sentinel:** an automaton used as a recorder, holding two recordings made very far apart in time.

The sentinel's older recording is an apology by someone named Manqu to Sakkuk, mentioning a feather accessory left in a stone box on a table and a promise left unkept. The newer recording is a dying adventurer's voice, aware that the Flower-Feather Clan's blockade made the trip unwise, who warns a companion to run from monsters.

History: The viewpoint text says the settlement was an attempt to found a new country on top of an older city built by a forgotten race, by an alliance that has since broken apart. The notes in the tower give a picture of its last days: a recording officer and a temple, craftspeople recruited to repair waterways, and a halt to the waterway work after a deep well was overrun by a dark calamity.

Warriors of the alliance sealed the entrance and burned the infected with flames said to be borrowed from the Holy Sovereign. Common people blamed the plague on the breaking of a taboo about offerings to the Lord of the Night, a priest tried to talk them down, and an old woman at the temple raved about the sun and the alliance's collapse. Three areas of the southwest sector were sealed by decree, yet the infected, though decayed, still walked. The last entry ends at a barricaded gate and a stained, unreadable page. All of this comes from damaged notes, not from a witnessed scene.

The notes name the recording officer Tlamachtihquetl and the craftsman Chupicua, who offered obsidian to avoid labour and was replaced by Manqu; the priest Chichiri tried to calm the public. Kamayuq warriors dragged the raving woman out, and the text hints that the alliance's laws would punish her. The alliance as a whole, and how this settlement fits within the wider story of Ochkanatlan, are covered by their own entries.

People: No living residents. The street holds the voices of the dead: the alliance-era priest and officials in the tower, and later visitors from the tribes. The visitors include a young Spiritcaller of the Masters of the Night-Wind (Liriwu), a mountain ranger and a traveling scholar, who came looking for the treasure rumoured to be aboard the Tonatiuh.

The Spiritcaller's notes say her mystic arts failed here: the voices of the Wayob could not be heard and even healing had no effect, and she wondered whether even her grand master, Sanhaj, could lift the curse. The ranger regrets bringing such a young child along. The scholar thinks an ancient scroll shows that dragon artisans once made a weapon against the Abyss, but the note breaks off at the realisation that they were deceived about what the treasure truly is.

Atmosphere: Ash, stillness and the sense of an unfinished plan. Voices from earlier ages survive in notes and recordings, but nothing answers back. The mood is melancholy rather than action-heavy: people's last words and unkept promises.

Dangers: The ruins are described as cursed and Abyss-corrupted, and a dying adventurer's recording warns of monsters. A Spiritcaller's note reports that healing and mystic arts failed here. The same recording mentions the Flower-Feather Clan's blockade.

Travel: The settlement lies within forbidden Ochkanatlan. An elevator links the levels of Vucub Caquix Tower. The ranger's note says entering the city proper requires finding a mechanism that leads toward the sky-vessel, the Tonatiuh.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and lifeless as of 7.1.

No source after 5.2 that was found revisits it.

17.comment: Ashflow Street: Vucub Caquix Tower Notes
17.content:
Tower in the middle of Ashflow Street. Its scrolls and notes contain the ranger's account, the alliance-era priest's final record, a young Spiritcaller's diary and a scholar's analysis of an old scroll about a treasure on the Tonatiuh.

The notes record that the expedition hoped to reach the sky-vessel, that the Spiritcaller was a child despite her confidence, and that the scholar's claim of a weapon against the Abyss ends with a warning of deception.

18.comment: Ashflow Street: Manqu and Sakkuk Recording
18.content: In Ashflow Street, a recording sentinel holds an old apology from Manqu to Sakkuk about an unkept promise and a feather accessory, and a much later dying adventurer's recording. A Manqu also appears in the tower's notes as the craftsman who replaced Chupicua on the waterway repair crew; the texts do not state outright that this is the same person.

19.content:
Atocpan: Atocpan is the volcanic southwest of Natlan. The Great Volcano of Tollan fills the region, an active volcano that erupts from time to time, and beside it lies the home of the Collective of Plenty (Teteocan), the tribe known for bodybuilding, wrestling and the best fruit and vegetables in Natlan. Ruins of the ancient dragons lie scattered around the slopes. The name Atocpan means "thick and fertile soil" in Nahuatl, which suits the rich volcanic farmland.

Atocpan is where Natlan's farming meets its oldest history: tribespeople grow crops beside a volcano that ancient legends call the Sacred Mountain, and the only way into the mountain's interior, the Ancient Sacred Mountain, is through the ring of floating islands above its mouth.

Geography: A region of ash-rich, fertile soil, orchards and rocky slopes around the Great Volcano of Tollan, in the southwest of Natlan. Its sub-areas are the Collective of Plenty settlement, Fallingstar Fields, the Remnants of Tetenanco, the Skyfire Circlet and the Ancient Mountain Path. The volcano encloses the whole region and periodically sends up fireballs.

Natural hot springs, a cold onsen in the west, farmland, tribal training grounds and the dig sites of ancient ruins all share the same slopes. Local specialties are Dracolite, quenepa berries, skysplit gembloom and sprayfeather gill.

Places: The Collective of Plenty settlement, with its Grand Wrestling Grounds (an elevated arena decorated with giant bull horns, also called the Resonating Arena) and training ground; Varesa's Orchard just outside the settlement; Fallingstar Fields with the Tephric Ruins; the Remnants of Tetenanco, ruins left by the ancient dragons; and the Skyfire Circlet, a ring of islands held above the volcano's mouth by Phlogiston.

The Skyfire Circlet holds the only entrance to the Ancient Sacred Mountain, which is why a quest calls it Nahuatzin's Springboard. A Fatui camp and boats sit near the Derelict Masonry Dock, and Fatui also camp west of the Tetenanco ruins. A small camp of one wandering stranger, Ixtelo, is the subject of two damaged notices: a bounty notice and a letter from Hawka, both warning that this wanderer is dangerous.

People: The Collective of Plenty live here under their chief, Acatl. Their members include the playable Iansan, a champion wrestler, and the orchard-keeper Varesa. Their saurian companions are the charging Tatankasaurs. Mposo watches over the Tetenanco dig site.

Wrestling referees, logistics managers and a flying squad are posted at the Grand Wrestling Grounds. Quest dialogue (Despair Engulfs the Heavens) notes that this tribe lives the farthest from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Culture: Physical fitness is highly prized: showing off one's muscles is a friendly gesture, adults tend to be large and heavily muscled, and fitness coaches must be very strong to be taken seriously. Warriors seek out wild Halberd-Crest Birds to see whose head is harder, hoping to temper their bodies to steel, and wrestling a Tatankasaurus is a long-standing tribal tradition; winning is considered a great honour. Their fruit and vegetables are said to be the best in Natlan because the soil beside the volcano is so rich.

A note by the cold onsen advertises 'The Book of Five Springs', a serialised bathhouse-fighting story from Yae Publishing House, a small sign that Inazuman publishing reaches even this far.

History: Legend holds that ancient dragons once dwelt in the volcano and that their palace lay somewhere beneath the magma. According to the same legends, the dragon prince Kukulkan stole the primal fire (Phlogiston) from there. The first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, is said to have fought and defeated the dragon sovereign Xiuhcoatl on the volcano, after the Abyss corrupted him. After the dragon civilisation crumbled, the Abyss is said to have taken over the volcano.

The Collective of Plenty was founded thousands of years ago by Ahpub, around the time of the Grand Alliance. The Remnants of Tetenanco are thought to be a satellite city of the dragons destroyed during the war between the dragons and Xbalanque, and the Tephric Ruins in Fallingstar Fields are a section of ruins ejected from the volcano about five hundred years ago, during the cataclysm. A report found in a hidden chamber of the Tephric Ruins describes experiments to reverse the regression of the 'Dragonborn' (saurians), and it concludes that the price would be too great. The same file carries a later comment, unsigned, wondering whether the experiment could break a 'barrier of destiny'. The commenter speaks of 'my brother' and of 'the promise I saw in humanity'; the wiki reads these lines as Kukulkan addressing Xiuhcoatl, but the text itself names neither.

Power of the two Golden Entreaties is tied to the volcano: according to the NPC Manqu, bringing both to the Great Volcano of Tollan can lift the Flamelord's Blessing from a saurian. Natlan/History also records that the dragon sovereign Xiuhcoatl carved out the Sacred City of Tollan inside the volcano, that the fungal god Bifrons was buried by an eruption here in the ancient dragon era, and that the city fell about two thousand years ago when Xbalanque invaded.

Atmosphere: Warm air, ash and orange light from the volcano, farm fields set against steaming rock and a lively, noisy tribe that wrestles, shouts and eats well. Sudden rumbling signals an eruption: fireballs rain on the ground and boulders roll down the slopes, then everything goes quiet again.

Dangers: Volcanic eruptions (fireballs and rolling boulders, which are gameplay hazards in the game), saurians, Abyssal monsters and, near the ruins, Secret Source automata. Fatui camps are scattered through the area.

Gameplay note, not lore: eruptions recur roughly every twenty minutes of play in the region, last under a minute, and are used as a puzzle element. Bosses here include the Lava Dragon Statue and the Secret Source Automaton: Overseer Device.

Travel: The Skyfire Circlet and Ancient Mountain Path lead into the Ancient Sacred Mountain. A notice at the Tetenanco tunnel says the dig site is closed to the public because of recent eruptions.

Quests: The Mushroom Realm Mystery story chapter begins here with Ardent Land of Plenty and Orchard Repose, in which Varesa and Iansan are involved. World quests include A Brief History of Rocks (at Tetenanco, with Mposo and the Avatar of Lava) and Investigator of Ancient Ruins (Fallingstar Fields), either of which counts toward The Way Into the Mountain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Atocpan is quiet, with its tribe prospering and the volcano still erupting now and then.

The Night Warden Wars ended in 5.3. The people of Natlan may now leave their homeland, and the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame has become a sports competition. Nothing in the later versions up to 7.1 changes the region's story.

The wiki lists no Atocpan changes in 6.x or 7.x beyond bug fixes. The Tetenanco dig site remains closed to the public because of eruptions.

20.comment: Atocpan: Collective of Plenty Settlement and Grand Wrestling Grounds
20.content:
The Collective of Plenty settlement sits beside the Great Volcano of Tollan. Its centre is the Grand Wrestling Grounds, an elevated arena adorned with massive bull horns where the tribe's athletic competitions are held; a quest calls it the Resonating Arena. A bulletin board, referee, logistics manager and a flying squad member work here, and a training ground lies nearby.

The tribe is led by Acatl. Their saurian companions are Tatankasaurs, and the tribe's warriors prove themselves by wrestling them.

21.content: Just outside the settlement, Varesa's Orchard belongs to the tribeswoman Varesa and is guarded by her Tatankasaur companion Vanana. It grows apples, cacahuatl, grainfruit and quenepa berries, and it is the only place red berryshrooms are found. A fruit-pressing machine on its southern side can be set off by hitting it with a Tatankasaur or a Collective of Plenty character. The orchard is the setting of the story quest Orchard Repose.

22.comment: Atocpan: Remnants of Tetenanco and Fallingstar Fields
22.content:
Two sets of ancient ruins. The Remnants of Tetenanco are the remains of what is believed to have been a dragon satellite city, destroyed in the war between the dragons and Xbalanque; today they are also called the Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site and are guarded by Mposo. Fallingstar Fields contains the Tephric Ruins, a section of ruins ejected from the volcano around five hundred years ago.

Both sites hold fragments of Secret Source machinery. At the Tephric Ruins, tribespeople placed broken pieces of Source Mechanism as if for worship, and a floating platform holds a relic, That Which Was Once Ehecatl, that opens a hidden chamber of records. The Tetenanco dig has been closed to the public because of frequent eruptions.

23.comment: Atocpan: Skyfire Circlet and Ancient Mountain Path
23.content: The Skyfire Circlet is a ring of islands suspended above the mouth of the Great Volcano of Tollan by the power of Phlogiston, and it contains the only entrance to the Ancient Sacred Mountain, hence its other name, Nahuatzin's Springboard. Secret Source Hunter-Seeker automata and sentinels are found there, and the Ancient Mountain Path leads up toward it.

24.content: Two interactable letters at Fatui camps hint at a quiet dispute. 'Letter for Anna' is from Madam Kovalevskaya, a researcher who studies ancient ruins in Natlan and also helps with kuuvahki research at the request of an unnamed 'Lord Harbinger'. 'Unsigned Letter' orders the Fatui Praporshchik Tatiana to guard Kovalevskaya on a perilous voyage in an old ship and heavily implies that nobody would blame Tatiana if something happened. Tatiana also appears as a one-time enemy near the west Tetenanco camp. The wiki infers that the Harbinger is Dottore, but the letters do not say.

25.content:
Basin of Unnumbered Flames: The Basin of Unnumbered Flames is the great bowl of land at the centre of Natlan. It holds the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, the nation's core landmark where the eternal Sacred Flame burns and the six tribes gather for the Pilgrimage, along with the fairgrounds and inns that serve it and the smoking Huitztli Hill to the north. Official text says the basin is not natural: something huge once crashed here, and no one knows what.

The Stadium is Natlan's main city and the seat of the Speaker's Chamber, so the basin is where tribal politics, tournaments and travellers meet. The surrounding land is dry and hot, with magma streams close beneath the surface.

Geography: A broad basin whose shape the Saurian Relics Association judged to be the scar of a colossal impact rather than a natural formation. The Stadium of the Sacred Flame sits within it; Huitztli Hill, a mountain the locals also call Smoke Ridge, rises to the north. Local specialty: brilliant chrysanthemum.

Magma flows from the Great Volcano of Tollan run under Huitztli Hill and send smoke between its valleys. The Stele of the Sacred Flame in the basin still burns, though no one has had an answer from its flames about the impact.

Places: The Stadium of the Sacred Flame, including three districts: Chuwen Fair (shops, food stalls and the Saurian Relics Association counter), the Temple of Pax, and the Warrior's Rest Area. Also the Weary Inn, the Speaker's Chamber, the Tablet of Tona and Huitztli Hill.

Chuwen Fair has Bounama's Grocery, Zakan's Street Bites and Xocolatl Beverages. The Salutary Furnace at the Temple of Pax is where the most skilled Children of Echoes craftspeople forge personal weapons for warriors using Liquid Phlogiston purified by the Sacred Flame; its owner is Alom. The Weary Inn, on the outskirts of the fair, is a restaurant and hotel that gives free food and lodging to warriors in the Pilgrimage. Its name was chosen in the hope that warriors would leave their weariness at the inn and enter the Stadium refreshed, and every manager of the inn is chosen and appointed by the Speaker's Chamber.

The Saurian Relics Association branch in Chuwen Fair is run by Siyah and sits in a corner of the fair. Its goods are not available when the Traveler first arrives because they have not yet been sorted. The Association's map text notes that its interests extend beyond saurians. Gameplay features: the Tablet of Tona takes Pyro Sigils as offerings, and a hidden area in the Night Kingdom, the Chamber of Night's Trial, copies the Stadium's layout and offers a battle against eight Nightsoul warriors once a Night Jade is obtained.

People: The Speaker's Chamber, the governing body of Natlan, sits in the Stadium. Tournament organisers, referees, engineers and warriors from all six tribes pass through the basin.

The Pyro Archon Mavuika is the host behind the Pilgrimage: the Weary Inn's free food and lodging for contestants is provided courtesy of the Pyro Archon. The tribes' playable warriors, such as Kinich, Mualani and Kachina, appear here in the story of Chapter V. The Weary Inn's staff member Vitusov is its listed resident NPC.

Culture: The Basin's identity is the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, a national combat tournament held at the Stadium. Official site text sums up the spirit of the place: in the name of victory and honour the fires of conflict are lit, and the fervour of all souls becomes fuel for the everlasting Sacred Flame.

Before the end of the Night Warden Wars, the Pilgrimage produced Contending Fire from fights between Natlanese, which fuelled the Sacred Flame, and chose the strongest warriors for the wars and, in time, the next Pyro Archon. Outlanders were barred because only Natlanese combat makes Contending Fire. The tournament has two phases: team contests across the countryside after a balloon drop, then one-on-one matches in the Stadium. Registration is done at the Stadium, and the Weary Inn feeds contestants the night before.

History: Chapter V of the Archon Quest begins with a Pilgrimage held at the Stadium. After it, Kachina does not come back from the Night Warden War as the Ode of Resurrection should have restored her, and Mavuika suspends the Pilgrimage and the Wars while she investigates. The Archon Quest Echoes of Life, in the Black Stone Under a White Stone act, begins at the Speaker's Chamber.

Natlan/History records that in 5.1 a nation-wide Abyssal invasion cost thousands of lives and temporarily extinguished the Sacred Flame; the Night Warden Wars ended for good in 5.3. Afterwards, Mavuika repurposed the Pilgrimage as a purely athletic tournament and asked the Traveler to serve as a special supervisor, which meant the Traveler could not compete. The first winner of the new Pilgrimage was Kinich.

With the Abyss gone and the Pilgrimage retooled as a sports contest, outsiders are able to take part. The Stadium region is the start point of the 5.3 story quests A New Pilgrimage and After the Peace (Sol Invictus chapter, As the Blazing Sun).

Atmosphere: Heat, smoke from Huitztli Hill and the steady glow of the Sacred Flame. Warriors practise, fairgoers eat and trade at Chuwen Fair, and the air is competitive but friendly.

Dangers: Wild saurians (yumkasaurs and tepetlisaurs), hilichurls, Forged Sand fighters and swiftstep couriers are the enemies listed for the hills, and Huitztli Hill is hot enough to trouble even tribespeople who handle Phlogiston. A boss, the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant, lives there.

Official text says the reclusive and unusual qucusaur has chosen the hill to live on perhaps precisely because the heat keeps people away.

Travel: The Stadium is the hub for travel between the tribes. The Pilgrimage's balloons carry teams out across the region; the Weary Inn is a place to rest.

Quests: Story and Archon quests tied to the basin include the Archon Quest Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame (5.0), Natlan! A New Adventure, Echoes of Life (Speaker's Chamber), and the Sol Invictus chapter's A New Pilgrimage and After the Peace (5.3).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the basin is at peace. The Stadium hosts the Pilgrimage as a sports competition.

The Sacred Flame was temporarily extinguished during the 5.1 invasion; the Abyss has since been purged from the Night Kingdom and the Stadium no longer sends warriors into war.

The wiki lists no changes to the basin in 6.x or 7.x.

26.comment: Basin of Unnumbered Flames: Stadium of the Sacred Flame
26.content: The Stadium of the Sacred Flame is the core landmark of Natlan and the site of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, in which members of the six tribes compete. A continually burning fire, the Sacred Flame, stands in it. The Stadium has three connected districts: Chuwen Fair, the Temple of Pax, and the Warrior's Rest Area.

27.comment: Basin of Unnumbered Flames: Huitztli Hill
27.content: A mountain north of the Stadium. Locals call it Smoke Ridge because magma streams from the Great Volcano of Tollan flow through it and send smoke up between its valleys. The heat is too much even for tribespeople used to Phlogiston, which may be why a reclusive Qucusaur lives there.

28.content:
Blazing Ruins: The Blazing Ruins are the remnants of a ring-shaped ceremonial site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan, from an era before people truly mastered flame. Sages from all corners of the world came to ponder fire and tried to perfect the rituals needed to transform phlogiston. Today it is a domain overrun by scoundrels.

Several of the heroes who later followed the "mighty one" (Xbalanque, the Pyro Archon) into the belly of the volcano (the Ancient Sacred Mountain) are said to have trained here. The domain's description invites the player to cleanse the site and perhaps gain the revelations the ancients left. In gameplay terms it is a Mastery domain that yields talent level-up materials.

History: Canon gives only the broad picture: an age when people had not yet mastered flame; sages studying fire's mysteries; a ceremonial circle used to refine phlogiston rituals; and later trainees among the heroes of Xbalanque's following. No dates, names or events are given.

Dangers: Gameplay layer: the opposition is Tepetlisaurs (whelps, Tepetlisaurus and Warrior variants), Forged Sand mercenaries (Interrogators, Shieldbreakers, Javelineers) and, at the end, two Fluid Avatars of Lava. The Ley Line Disorder gives CRIT DMG +60% for 6 seconds whenever a character's Nightsoul points rise or fall, so Natlan characters in Nightsoul's Blessing benefit most.

Rewards rotate by weekday through the talent book series Contention (Sublime Turning), Kindling (Myriad Illusions) and Conflict (Return).

Status as of 7.1: Permanently available in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot events are tied to it.

29.comment: Blazing Ruins: Ceremonial ring of Coatepec Mountain
29.content: Ring-shaped ceremonial site where ancient sages practised and refined phlogiston-transforming rituals before flame was mastered; later a training place for some of Xbalanque's followers. Described by domain flavour text only.

30.content:
Bounama's Grocery: Bounama's Grocery is a small general-goods shop in the Chuwen Fair of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames. It is run by Bounama, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind, and it sells ordinary cooking ingredients. The shop is open at all hours and restocks every day.

Bounama is protective of quiet: he asks customers to keep their voices down because noise can disturb the mixing process he carries out there. Payment is on trust. Customers take what they need and leave the money to one side, and a crafting bench in the shop may be used by anyone when it is free, without asking him first.

Places: The shop is a point of interest inside the Chuwen Fair, marked on the map as a general-goods vendor. It is not a separate district: it belongs to the fairground at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

A crafting bench stands in the shop. Bounama treats the surroundings as part of his craft, which is why he insists on quiet.

People: Bounama is the only person associated with the shop. He is curt but willing to explain himself when someone asks a thoughtful question, and he is pleased by customers who think about environmental factors in crafting.

He says that most makers know a potion changes with the amount of spinel fruit powder, or that one extra line can change a talisman, yet forget that sound can affect crafting too. When it is pointed out that the surroundings are not quiet, he replies that he has already accounted for that and bases everything on his existing environment, adding that the comings and goings of people and their stories are part of production. He quotes a saying of the Masters of the Night-Wind: "All has been understood, and the future becomes the past."

Economy: The stock is simple cooking ingredients, including mushrooms, salt, pepper, onions, milk, tomatoes, cabbage, potatoes, wheat and glabrous beans. Stock refreshes daily.

Asked whether he fears theft, Bounama says the idea of profiting from another's labour can plant a bad seed even in an honest person, but he shrugs it off: the goods are only odds and ends that the Mol Stone House sells on commission, and if something goes missing he can draw a couple of prayer talismans to make the money back.

Game note (gameplay, not lore): the shop restocks daily, and reaching Tribe Reputation Rank 4 with two of Natlan's tribes gives a permanent 10 percent discount.

Atmosphere: Hushed and slightly conspiratorial for a market stall: customers are shushed, coins are left to one side, and the owner talks about mixing. Around it the fair carries on as usual.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shop is unchanged since its introduction in 5.0, and no later story role is recorded.

31.content: Bounama keeps Bounama's Grocery in the Chuwen Fair and is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. He demands quiet because noise can disturb the mixing process, trusts customers to leave payment beside the goods, and lets anyone use the crafting bench when it is free. His only recorded idle line is a hushed "Shh!". No profile text, age or backstory is recorded.

32.content:
Brewblossom Stores: The Brewblossom Stores are an underground facility on Tete Isle, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort off Natlan's western edge, where Aphimead is refined and stored. Visitors can take part in a hands-on brewing experience called Honeydew Craftbrew.

Aphimead is Tete Isle's specialty drink. It is made with the help of aphids that tend Brewblossoms, and the Stores are the place where that process is opened up to visitors as part of the resort's offering.

Places: The facility lies underground in the Northern Cavern of Tenochtzitoc, the older name of the resort island. It holds brewing barrels, a collecting device and refining equipment for Aphimead, plus storage for the finished mead.

In the quest demonstration, brewing equipment has a suction port that takes delivered honeydew, and finished Aphimead flows from aphid-shaped and star-shaped hinges into cup-shaped structures. The area's music, "When the Mead First Ferments", is shared with the Easybreeze Market.

Culture: Brewblossoms are plants known to possess spirits, and they close their petals on anyone who strays too close. Their pollen is a key ingredient of Aphimead. Brewblossom Aphids live with them in symbiosis, tending the flowers and feeding on nectar.

Staff describe the method: aphids are guided to gather ripened honeydew from the brewing barrels; the honeydew is collected in a special device and refined using the strength of the staff's tatankasaur companions; a splash of added flavour or alcohol then turns the base into different kinds of Aphimead. Brewblossoms wither without nutrients and are revived by sending aphids to feed them.

Quests: In the Story Quest The World Is Your Canvas! (the second part of the Sunspray Summer Resort), the Traveler's party is invited to try Honeydew Craftbrew. The staff member Takhar explains the process, and the bard Venti turns it into a friendly brewing competition with the Traveler. Venti jokes that the resort's meagre mead stock means visitors are meant to help replenish it.

Later in the same quest a Whopperflower is found hiding among the Brewblossoms; Tlapalli reports that more may be lurking in a store room, and the party clears them from the lower level of the Me & Dew bar. Mualani quotes the brochure's boast about "honey-sweet Aphimead".

Elsewhere on Tete Isle, a letter from a crew member (Tecuhtli) to their captain recommends the bars Me & Dew and The Dewdrop for their good Aphimead and suggests stealing some to bring back to Nasha Town.

Atmosphere: Honey-sweet stonework, humming aphids, clinking cups and cheerful holiday patter from staff: a working brewery presented as an attraction.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the facility is open as part of the resort. No role in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content is recorded.

33.content: Honeydew Craftbrew is the visitor experience in which guests steer Brewblossom Aphids to carry collected honeydew to the brewing equipment, raising brewing progress until a lever completes the batch. The wiki describes it as hosted at the Brewblossom Stores; in the quest Takhar frames it as a way to help produce the island's Aphimead.

34.content:
Castle Joquiratto: Castle Joquiratto is the stronghold of the villain "El Capoctus Joquiratto", the main antagonist of the immersive adventure experience at Villa Guiztli. It sits in the western zone of the Guiztli Ridge caverns in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It is a comic, theatrical place full of scheming Nochtli lackeys, capybara and alpaca townsfolk, and booby-trapped chests.

Visitors play heroes defending the underground town from Joquiratto. The tone is pantomime: villains boast, barrels explode in the wrong direction, and treasure chests are rarely what they seem.

Geography: The castle lies in the Guiztli Ridge Inner Cavern, whose viewpoint is titled "Cavern of Stone and Prickly Pears". The resort island's older name, Tenochtzitoc, translates to "cavern of stone and prickly pears", though prickly pears no longer grow there in the modern day.

A teleport waypoint stands in the castle area. In the northeast a lackey guards a chest and insists there is no treasure inside; to the south of the waypoint, lackeys guard a sealed chest, threaten to send intruders to "the Night Kingdom", and detonate nearby explosive barrels, which in turn releases a lava avatar.

People: The area is occupied by Nochtli lackeys (the villain's henchmen) and by capybara and alpaca townsfolk, including an Alpaca Sheriff who speaks with a "meh" and leads the hunt for "the evil capybara". The lackeys shout "For El Capoctus Joquiratto!".

Examples of staged mischief: a lackey scowls at a capybara that has been carried to the top of a mountain on a Chroma Kite and now declares that it holds the high ground; two lackeys unearth a treasure chest, cannot split it evenly, and settle it by duel (the "Three Musketeers" challenge).

Quests: The Story Quest To Guiztli Ridge! (the Sunspray Summer Resort, part 2.2) has the party ride a cruise ship into the cavern, defeat bandits with the Sheriff, help activate a mechanism, and chase Joquiratto until his hot-air balloon is brought down and crashes on a mountaintop. The castle area is accessed partway through that quest.

A Hidden Exploration Objective that the wiki names unofficially "Joquiratto's Not-So-Great Plan" spans Guiztli Ridge and the castle: Nochtli bandits propose a fifty-fifty plan to a passer-by, then trick them with explosive barrels, and defeating them awards the achievement "A Grand Plan".

A puzzle near the castle is a liar-and-truth-teller riddle about Red-Top and Blue-Top capybaras. Picking the Blue-Top who accuses Red-Top reveals a Nochtli lackey, who flees by boat and must be shot down using a cannon.

Atmosphere: Bright, noisy and cartoonish: flat-cut villains, shouting capybaras and cheerfully sabotaged heists. Even the explosions are staged comedy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the castle remains part of the resort and has no recorded role in later story content.

35.content: "El Capoctus Joquiratto" is the villain of Villa Guiztli's adventure show. His lackeys rob the town, the Sheriff asks the heroes for help, and in the Guiztli Ridge quest the party pursues him until his hot-air balloon is brought down. Nothing is recorded of any real person behind the title.

36.content:
Catastrophe's Edge: Catastrophe's Edge is an instanced trial area in Natlan's Tequemecan Valley. It lies beyond the Hall of Parting Vows and is entered through a portal during the world quest Revelations from the Past.

In that quest the Traveler and the Little One, a saurian companion, follow Manqu's guidance to the ruins to obtain a token left by the Sage of the Stolen Flame. After crossing a lava passage, a portal to Catastrophe's Edge appears, and the party must fight off three waves of foes there.

The final wave is an Abyss-corroded Golden Wolflord, titled in the quest as a boundary-eroding beast from beyond. During this step the playable character is restricted to the Traveler.

Canon text read gives no further lore: the place is known only as a quest instance, and its name and purpose are left unexplained.

Quests: Revelations from the Past (5.0), part of the chapter Between Pledge and Forgettance, follows Rite of the Bold and precedes The Road Ahead. The Edge is the combat climax before the inscription and the token reward.

The quest steps list three waves: two of Rockfond Rifthound Whelps (Abyss-corroded variants) and a final Abyss-Corroded Golden Wolflord. Canon text read here does not explain the name Catastrophe's Edge.

Travel: Unlocked through Revelations from the Past. Afterwards it can be re-entered by returning to the Hall of Parting Vows and going down the glowing stairs.

Atmosphere: A threshold trial: a portal reached across lava and a fight against corrupted beasts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the instance remains accessible from the Hall of Parting Vows. No later developments were found.

37.content:
Chamber of Deliberation: The Chamber of Deliberation is the assembly hall in the Sacred City of Tollan, inside Natlan's Ancient Sacred Mountain, where the Thirteen Sovereign Lords of the ancient dragon civilization once gathered to settle administrative and judicial matters. It is now a gold-trimmed, self-repairing ruin, and its preserved council records show a ruling class arguing over how to deal with humanity.

A "Speaker" presided and a numbered record was kept for each session. The surviving records show votes to impeach the Regent Kukulkan, to burn large human settlements, and to execute one of the lords for supposed betrayal. The hall also holds the permit needed to reach the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Geography: Within the Ancient Sacred Mountain, the Chamber is a subarea on the dragons' level of the city. It has a second floor with a left passageway, a pool of lava, a dragon statue whose head hides one of the record boards, and a chamber of repair and purification facilities. The viewpoint here is named "Court of the Dragons".

The hall was built "to outlast the very eons", in the words of the Secret Source Servant who guides the Traveler: bristling with defences and able to repair itself. An underground room north of the Chamber holds a separate inscription, the "Record Left by the 'Flamestealer'".

Governance: The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were each styled by a title and numbered CL-01 to CL-13. CL-01, "Valiant One" Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun, acted as Speaker. Motions began with an agenda and were decided by vote; when consensus was reached, even those who abstained were bound by the decision. Any lord could bring a motion, and the Speaker invited the proposer to present the case before the vote.

The lords named in the records, with their titles, are: CL-01 "Valiant One" Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun; CL-02 "Jade Maiden" Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka'; CL-03 "Weaver of Secrets" Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox; CL-04 "Hermit of Myriad Fates" Aj Awaj K'umilal Kan; CL-05 "Bestower of Bitter Springs" Aj K'astajibal Cha'ama' Ho'o; CL-06 "He Who Shakes the Earth Like Thunder in His Wrath" Aj Tininik Oyowal Waak; CL-07 "Toxic Rain Over Boundless Forests" Aj Chojojik Kamikabal U'uk; CL-08 "Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers" Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak; CL-09 "Chronicler of the End Times" Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon; CL-10 "Undying Wings of Lofty Isolation" Aj Imuch' Paxlaq Lahun; CL-11 "Mirror of the Dawning Morn" Ix Raq'lapuj Chue'q Buluk; CL-12 "Murmuring Spring" Ix Roq'ratik'obala' Ka'alahun; CL-13 "Bonebreaker" Aj Q'uplajik Ooxlahu.

By the time of the latter records the Sixth and Tenth Lords had fallen, the Fourth Lord was absent for long periods, working on the "Phlogistonization of Life" in a citadel on the high cliffs, and the sovereign Xiuhcoatl is invoked as the lords' king whose vision they claim to serve.

History: The Chamber belonged to the era of the dragon civilization of Natlantea, whose capital was the Sacred City. The three readable records come from a time when the lords felt threatened by humanity's spread and its theft of the secrets of phlogiston.

Record B-CL-11053 is an impeachment inquiry into Regent Kukulkan, proposed by the Second Lord. Its argument was deliberately erased, but the tally is 9 in favour, none against and 4 abstentions (CL-01, CL-03, CL-04 and CL-08): consensus. Phlogiston inscriptions over the erased section later emerge: a furious tirade against cowering, change-fearing creatures that ends with the line "The Sacred City has fallen."

Record B-CL-13097, on "Neutralization of Human Settlements", was proposed by the Fifth Lord Aj K'astajibal Cha'ama' Ho'o, overseer of Ek' Pulinik, to keep human numbers down by periodically incinerating settlements above a certain size. The Second Lord voted for it but called its reasoning weak; the Eighth and Twelfth Lords opposed it, the Twelfth urging instead that humans be manipulated into policing their own numbers by backing selected tribal leaders; the Ninth Lord, associated with Chichen Uctokah, abstained with scorn for the proposal's fear of humans and was taunted in turn over that domain. The vote was 5 for (CL-02, 05, 07, 11, 13), 2 against (CL-08, 12) and 3 abstentions (CL-01, 03, 09), so consensus was not reached. Record B-CL-16130 is a motion by the Twelfth Lord, custodian of Q'umqaraq'aj, to execute the Eighth Lord, Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak, whom the Twelfth accuses of betraying their kind by tolerating a human who follows Xbalanque. The Eighth refused to defend herself; the Speaker defended respect for Xbalanque; the vote was 4 for (CL-02, 05, 07, 12), 2 against (CL-01, 08) and 1 abstention (CL-03): consensus, so the motion carried.

Atmosphere: Gold-trimmed stone beside a pool of lava, with phlogiston inscriptions and a dragon statue. The preserved voices are contemptuous and ritualised, though some lords speak with respect of the human leader Xbalanque.

Quests: Part of the World Quest Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment (inside In Search of a Hidden Heart, in the Chronicler of the Crumbling City series). The Traveler, with Paimon and the Little One, follows a Secret Source Servant that takes the name Awanyu, which once belonged to a scribe of the Chamber. A permit needed for the Heart of the Sacred Mountain was left above the Chamber, but Rifthounds have broken in and the permit receptacle is found empty. The party activates a purification device and the Chamber's self-repair, raises a phlogiston barrier, receives the permit receptacle and finally activates the Permit to the Sacred Heart.

Awanyu dislikes the place: it calls the hall a congress of arrogant fools and a den of pretenders who claimed the right to judge their own kin, and says no one regarded there as a criminal would like it either. Without the permit, Astral Assemblages inside the Heart attack unauthorised visitors.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Chamber is unchanged since 5.5: a ruined hall with its records open to the Traveler. No later story use is recorded.

38.comment: Chamber of Deliberation: Sovereign Rulers' Council Records
38.content:
Three numbered records survive: B-CL-11053 (impeachment inquiry into Regent Kukulkan, carried 9-0-4 with the argument erased), B-CL-13097 (a motion to incinerate large human settlements, failed 5-2-3) and B-CL-16130 (a motion to execute the Eighth Lord, carried 4-2-1). Each lists attendees by number and title and a vote count. They show a council divided between those who wished to cull humanity, those who preferred to manipulate it, and those who admired Xbalanque.

Quotes worth keeping in mind: the Fifth Lord claims humans have "stolen the secrets of wielding phlogiston", the Twelfth argues that humans can be "shepherded into betraying their own kin", and the Speaker declares the hero Xbalanque worthy of facing him in combat. Treat the lords' contempt for humans as characterisation, not neutral narration.

39.comment: Chamber of Deliberation: Awanyu the Scribe's Servant
39.content: Awanyu is the name a Secret Source Servant takes in the quest, saying it once belonged to a scribe of the Chamber of Deliberation who seldom touched quill or ink himself once Secret Source Servants were invented. It guides the party to the Permit to the Sacred Heart while voicing its contempt for the hall.

40.content:
Chamber of Night's Trial (also: Trial Grounds of Restive Nightsouls): The Chamber of Night's Trial is a hidden arena in Natlan, in the Night Kingdom, resembling the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It is entered by a visitor holding a Night Jade. A Nightsoul Spirit there invites the visitor to quiet the restless Nightsouls through battle.

Its in-game viewpoint is titled "Trial Grounds of Restive Nightsouls" and declares that only the blaze of battle can still these unquiet souls to slumber.

Geography: In the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, the entrance lies to the south of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. The chamber is a self-contained arena echoing the Stadium's layout rather than an open region.

Natlan legend, as the Night Jade's item text says, holds that offering the jade at a specific altar may open the path to the kingdom ruled by the night. The jade is a nearly weightless black stone wrapped in chilling flames.

People: The only inhabitant shown is the Nightsoul Spirit, a quest-only NPC who speaks in archaic, courtly phrasing. It says the Nightsouls here are like dreams of its mistress, the sleeping goddess of the night (Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night), and that when she wakes now and then they are single strains of her mind.

The spirit laments that no one living under the sun remembers the Nightsouls' names or deeds, and says it has been long since anyone found this entrance. It addresses the visitor as a beloved outlander warrior and presents the fight as a way to calm souls overcome by battle-craving.

Atmosphere: A quiet, ceremonial and slightly melancholy arena: forgotten warriors, an archaic-speaking host, and a sense of old battles that were never settled. The tone is respectful of the dead rather than menacing.

Dangers: The trial pits the visitor against eight Nightsoul warriors. Players have sixty seconds to defeat them all; success opens a set of reward chests and earns the achievement "By Battle Be Settled...". The challenge can be retried after failing (gameplay detail).

The Nightsoul Spirit reacts to the visitor's choice in character: it is amused by a bold acceptance, regretful but patient if asked to wait, and encourages another attempt after a defeat. After a win it hands over the rewards. The related achievement is hidden until completed.

Travel: Access requires the Night Jade, a quest item formed automatically once three Shattered Night Jades are gathered. The shards come from the world quests "Revelations from the Past" and "To the Night, What is the Night's", and from a chest at the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center (a hidden exploration reward).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chamber is still accessible as a permanent hidden challenge; no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 source found mentions it.

41.content:
Chamber of Weaving: The Chamber of Weaving is a minor point of interest within the Masters of the Night-Wind's Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. Its only listed occupant is the NPC Yolotli, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. Canon says very little about the place itself.

Yolotli explains that messages from Mr. Toltec often mean a new commission to investigate the Ley Lines, and that they are not ready to go out again yet.

Places: It is listed as a named point of interest inside the larger Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, itself a ceremonial site of the Masters of the Night-Wind. The altar's other listed NPCs include the tribe's chief Biram, the High Priest Caholom, a guard named Cip, the Iktomisaurus elder Tlapo and Toltec.

The altar's viewpoint is titled "Ceremonial Site Lost in Night's Dim Light".

People: Yolotli is the sole occupant. They sound anxious and apologetic, and consider many mystical arts and prepared materials necessary before travelling again. Their own Ley Line perception is mediocre, so they depend on Saurians for that task.

Yolotli explains that Iktomisaurs will not simply go out "for walkies" with humans. They despise selfish use of their abilities, cannot be bribed, see through deceit, and expect visitors to follow their etiquette and state the purpose of the request first. A gift given with nothing asked in return can also make an Iktomisaur suspicious, depending on how much it trusts the giver. Yolotli says the Iktomisaurs love a certain mushroom and gives the Traveler three Glowing Hornshrooms to try.

Culture: Yolotli is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind and says there are many mystical arts to learn and materials to prepare first. In Yolotli's words, you cannot just choose any old mystical ability: it has to be the right one for you.

According to Yolotli, Ley Line investigations are commissioned by message from Toltec, and for Yolotli the work depends on Saurian help because of their mediocre Ley Line perception.

Further details: The wiki's etymology note says Yolotli's name derives from the Nahuatl word yollohtli, which means "heart" and "to live". This is a real-world naming note, not an in-world statement.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the Chamber of Weaving is recorded, and it has no known role in later story content.

42.content: Yolotli is an open-world NPC in the Chamber of Weaving. They are nervous about a possible new Ley Line commission from Mr. Toltec, still preparing mystical arts and materials, and rely on Saurian help because their own Ley Line perception is only mediocre. They give the Traveler three Glowing Hornshrooms and a lesson in Iktomisaur etiquette. No further profile is recorded.

43.content:
Citlali's Home: Citlali's Home is the residence of Citlali, the great shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind, in the Tezcatepetonco Range. It stands far from the tribal settlement and is hard to miss: its outer walls are covered in graffiti. Inside it is a mess of wine bottles, snacks and shelves crammed with light novels.

The Traveler first enters in The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors and gains permanent access after receiving Citlali's Handkerchief and Key in The Color of Memory. Citlali gave the key so that the Traveler wouldn't wake her by banging on the door while she was drunk.

Places: The home has an exterior, an interior instance, a bedroom, a table and a bookshelf. After The Color of Memory the bedroom door carries the faint sound of Citlali snoring, and the table and shelves hold books and the Traveler's note.

The shelves are packed with light novels, and the whole home is described as a hermit's nest rather than a witch's lair. A concealed compartment in the bookshelf, protected by several layers of mystical seals, holds an obscure Inazuman light novel, New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune.

The light novel Citlali discusses most is "Mirage Warriors", perhaps the first she ever read; it is said to have changed authors three times without ever being finished, and most of its original readers are dead, with Citlali the last. Nobody can say which book is her true favourite.

People: Only Citlali lives here. She has lived here as a recluse, reluctant to go out; Character Stories note that after she reached seventy she grew unwilling to leave her home and attended only to matters that demanded her involvement. For her birthday celebration, the tribe lured her out of her home with a knock at the door.

The graffiti was a deliberate tradition: another great shaman, Huitzilin, had her students plaster Citlali's walls with taunts so that Citlali would be the stern opponent that made them improve. After Huitzilin died, her disciples and their disciples kept it up, claiming it was her dying wish. A thief once broke in claiming to have found the concealed compartment; Citlali thrashed him, handed him to the tribal guards and added another layer of defences, without denying that the compartment existed.

Mavuika remarks in the Character Stories that after two hundred years Citlali is as unenthused about going outside as ever, and that it might take a figure more fascinating than light novels to draw the genius shaman toward the real world.

History: The home is the target of a Masters of the Night-Wind tradition: shamans have their students plaster its walls with taunts, as Huitzilin once did, so that Citlali becomes the formidable opponent who pushes them to improve.

The tribe held a birthday celebration for Citlali by luring her out with a knock at the door and unveiling a cake and gifts when she stepped outside.

Quests: In the Tribal Chronicles quest series Memories Flowing With Color, the interior is first accessed during The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors. In The Color of Memory the Traveler receives the handkerchief and key. If the Traveler has the limited-deluxe "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?" and the first-edition "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power", they can be left on the table with a note from the Traveler and Paimon saying they were found while she slept.

After one daily reset the light novel sits on the table in pristine condition, the area around it wiped clean, as if its new owner cannot bring herself to read it and prefers to admire it. After a second reset two light novels are on the bookshelf, which has been tidied especially for them.

Atmosphere: Cluttered with wine bottles and snacks, with snoring behind the bedroom door and obvious pride in a few treasured books.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Citlali's Home is unchanged: a permanent instanced interior, with no later story role recorded.

44.content: Among the Masters of the Night-Wind, a great shaman sometimes chooses a strong peer as an opponent for her students.
