Huitzilin chose Citlali and had students cover her home with taunting graffiti as a direct challenge. Citlali answered by humbling each arrogant novice. After Huitzilin's death, disciples continued the practice, claiming it was her dying wish. Most of the tribe accepted this, though it departed somewhat from tradition.

45.content:
Coatepec Mountain: Coatepec Mountain is a towering peak in Natlan and the home of the Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan), the tribe of explorers, couriers and hunters who live alongside the leaf-tongued Yumkasaurs. Their village hangs from the cliff-face, and the mountain is also the seat of the Turnfire rites in memory of the ancestor Yupanqui. The Pyro Archon Mavuika comes from this tribe. The name means "at the snake hill" in Nahuatl.

The terrain is harsh, but young people still come to test themselves. The mountain also holds the old Ancestral Temple, the lake at Teticpac Peak and, south of it, Firethief's Secret Isle.

Geography: A high, rocky mountain with the Scions of the Canopy's village suspended off the cliff-face. Official text says their ancestors hung giant trees over the cliffs with ropes and grappling hooks, which gave the tribe its name. Teticpac Peak is a plateau with a small lake at the very top; Firethief's Secret Isle lies in the sea to the south. Local specialty: quenepa berries.

Tepeacac Rise slopes are said by the Expedition text to lie in the mountain's northwest, although the wiki files that subarea under Tequemecan Valley.

Places: The tribal village; the Couriers' Longhouse; the Ancestral Temple; Teticpac Peak and the Manse of Monetoo Murals; Firethief's Secret Isle; and the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center.

The Ancestral Temple is a sacred site where the people of Natlan once spoke with the Night Kingdom; the tribes have since built a more stable link, so it is out of use, but it remains holy ground guarded by the Scions of the Canopy. According to the NPC Legba, only experienced Couriers who have passed three trials may enter. Firethief's Secret Isle is hidden from the map under perpetual cloud until four time-trial challenges on it are completed, after which the weather clears. The Phlogiston Extraction Research Center is a secret underground Fatui base.

Legend has it that the tribe's warriors and one hundred Yumkasaurs spent a hundred days and a hundred ropes moving the Obsidian Totem Pole, the symbol of their faith, to its present place on the mountain.

People: The Scions of the Canopy, led by chief Wayna. They are skilled explorers, messengers and hunters, fond of extreme sports. The playable Kinich is one of their hunters, and the Pyro Archon Mavuika is of this tribe.

Natlan's Adventurers' Guild is mostly made up of Huitztlan. A tribal figure called the Mountain King (Kongamato) is a Yumkasaurus as old as the cataclysm, loved by the tribe and now ceremonially tended.

Culture: The tribe works as couriers and guides and honours its ancestors. Its great observance is Turnfire Night, held to commemorate Yupanqui, who is called the Firethief.

The tribe tends the Mountain King Flamegranates, which grow from the Mother Flamegranate Tree, and offers them to Kongamato, though rumour says Yumkasaurs sneak him some as well. Flamegranate skins are dried and made into the bags that couriers carry. To bear the Ancient Name Malipo is to carry the Turnfire.

During Turnfire Night a flame bearer, traditionally the current bearer of the Malipo name, leads a delegation that lights braziers with kindling from the Sacred Flame and takes it into the Mountain King's cave in order to cleanse the abyssal corruption within him.

History: Tradition says that in the days of the tyrant Och-Kan, the tribe's ancestor Yupanqui stole the Turnfire, a fire that burned anyone who looked back at it, and turned it on Och-Kan's army. He glanced back and was consumed. He burned for a hundred days, and the fire pierced a hole through the Ley Lines so that he fell into the Night Kingdom, where the Turnfire is said to burn still. 'Malipo' became his Ancient Name.

In the cataclysm five hundred years ago the hero Burkina, a later bearer of the Malipo name, and his Yumkasaur companion Kongamato fought the Abyss beside Tenoch and the Pyro Archon Mavuika. Abyssal energy infested Kongamato, and in a fit of rage he killed Burkina, who passed some of his power and blood to him. Kongamato lived centuries longer, a living symbol of the tribe's glory. After the cataclysm, Mavuika's sister Hine helped rebuild the Scions of the Canopy, though none of her works survive.

In the story quest series Yupanqui's Turnfire (5.0), the Turnfire ritual that drains Kongamato's energy was due again because the energy had been building faster than usual. Kinich proposed placing the Mountain King in a Beastly Rift provided by Enjou; the plan was resisted and the ritual went wrong. In the fight that followed, Kongamato begged to be put out of his misery, but Kinich told him he had to live with his shame. As of The Last Turnfire Night his corruption is permanently stabilised, a shell has grown around him, and he trains tribe members. Kongamato appeared to Kinich and the Traveler before their descent into the Night Kingdom.

Atmosphere: Vertical and exposed: a village hung from the cliffs, couriers on their rounds, Yumkasaurs on the rocks and a tribe that loves a challenge.

Dangers: Steep terrain, wild saurians and the Fatui, who run a hidden facility on the mountain.

The research center was extracting Phlogiston from captured saurians. Notes found there show the soldiers puzzling over why they must go to such lengths, with a technician, Nomokonov, understanding the science better than the rest. The Fontaine Research Institute supplied equipment, and it is unclear how much it knew about the use.

Travel: Firethief's Secret Isle appears on the map only after its four time-trial challenges are done. Only experienced Couriers who passed the three trials may enter the Ancestral Temple.

Quests: Main stories linked to the mountain are Yupanqui's Turnfire (I, Flame Bearer; The Last Turnfire Night) in the Kinich's Deal act. World quests include Ripe For Trouble (Flamegranates). Several Scions of the Canopy died in the Abyssal invasion of Chapter V, Act IV; this file leaves those individuals to their own entries.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and Kongamato's corruption is stabilised.

Natlan's war with the Abyss ended in 5.3, and the people of Natlan may now leave their homeland.

The wiki lists no story changes at Coatepec Mountain after 5.0; version 5.4 only fixed a rock near the mountain and the Ancestral Temple.

46.content:
The Turnfire is a fire from the age of the Grand Alliance that tyrant Och-Kan used as a weapon; anyone it marked felt a terrible burning behind them and would be burned to a crisp if they turned around. Yupanqui stole it and used it against Och-Kan's army, but he looked back and burned. 'Malipo' is now an Ancient Name, borne by Burkina and by Kinich. The Scions of the Canopy hold Turnfire Night to honour their ancestors.

Yupanqui was a companion of the first Pyro Archon Xbalanque in his youth and lost an eye on that journey; later he worked for the Grand Alliance seeking peace between humans and saurians, joined the Scarlet-Eyed Youth's rebellion against Och-Kan and died with the Turnfire.

47.comment: Coatepec Mountain: Kongamato, the Mountain King
47.content: Kongamato is an enormous Yumkasaurus who has lived since the cataclysm and holds a special place in the Scions of the Canopy's heart. Abyssal corruption keeps him alive but also threatens to overwhelm him, so the tribe performs a ritual to drain it. After The Last Turnfire Night the corruption is stabilised, and he offers to train the tribe's young. The Archive text jokes that he is so large because he has lived so long and eaten too much.

48.comment: Coatepec Mountain: Phlogiston Extraction Research Center
48.content: A secret underground base operated by the Fatui, where they extracted Phlogiston from captured saurians. Fontaine Research Institute equipment was used. The notes of its soldiers mention the Polychrome Tri-Stars, a group who captured saurians on behalf of Capitano's forces; the Traveler eventually stopped this effort.

49.content:
Colorfall Cave: Colorfall Cave lies just south of Colorfall Cliffs on the Easybreeze resort island. A crooked sideline used it as a hidden workshop for making fake Koholasaur dolls, and a young painter's apprentice named Zhaka was held there against his will until the Traveler freed him.

The shady arrangement belongs to Rekis, an underworld figure from Nod-Krai who is mentioned but never seen.

Geography: A cave south of Colorfall Cliffs, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Its map level is labelled as the eastern cavern of Tenochtzitoc, the island's old name.

It is a minor dead end of the resort that tourists have no reason to visit.

People: Rekis's associates ran the workshop. Zhaka, Kanei's apprentice at the paint workshop, was taken there by mistake; his Asha companion is Azhka. After his rescue he appears at Easybreeze Market.

Per the Rekis page, Rekis ordered the kidnapping of the painter Kanei. A henchman named Manou seized Zhaka instead. When Zhaka's skills proved poor, Rekis scolded Manou and ordered the weaker fakes to be foisted on unsuspecting tourists. Zhaka's own words to the Traveler later are that without the rescue his master might have thrown him out.

The wiki lists Zhaka as an open-world NPC of Natlan affiliated with the People of the Springs, and says he is Kanei's apprentice at the paint workshop.

History: The cave was used for a counterfeit scheme during the resort's opening season. The scheme made fake Koholasaur dolls for tourists to buy, using a hostage painter.

A note called Rekis's Orders found here says word came from Nasha Town that the Curatorium of Secrets had placed an informant on the island, watching Rekis's people and the crew of Radius Bone. The informant's registered name at reception is Rantiy and the note advises avoiding conflict with him.

Atmosphere: A damp, hidden hideaway behind the cheerful colours of the cliffs above: crates, half-finished dolls and the nervous air of people who expect to be found out.

Dangers: Rekis's henchmen were the threat while Zhaka was held. Nothing suggests that the cave is dangerous now.

Quests: Zhaka's rescue takes place here as part of the 5.8 Easybreeze content.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the workshop is abandoned and the cave is open.

Zhaka lives and works at the Easybreeze Market. Rekis's operations against Asha and tourists are not shown to continue.

50.content:
Colorfall Cliffs (also: Airborne Asha): Colorfall Cliffs are the sunny, colour-streaked fields of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Above them hangs the resort's star attraction, the Airborne Asha, a floating structure shaped like an Asha holding a torch, which visitors ride a hot air balloon up to and paint.

The area has an Alpaca Park run by a manager named Aloha, and an attendant named Tikraq through whom the Airborne Asha can be revisited.

Geography: Wide green fields marked with vivid swirls of paint. Colorfall Cave lies just south, and Huha Hill's lodgings overlook the cliffs, along with Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay.

The Airborne Asha floats in the sky above and is reached by balloon.

Places: The Airborne Asha, a giant floating structure resembling an Asha holding a torch, and the Alpaca Park.

The Airborne Asha is first reached during the story quest To Colorfall Cliffs! and can then be revisited by talking to Tikraq.

People: Aloha, the Alpaca Park manager, and Tikraq.

In To Colorfall Cliffs!, the Traveler is joined by Paimon, Mualani, Chasca and Bennett, and holds a spray-painting contest with Bennett at the top of the Airborne Asha.

Culture: The quest To Colorfall Cliffs! belongs to the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort event story, which asks the Traveler to colour the fields with Asha-powered paint drums.

Starblooms on Huha Hill's terraces are reminders of the cliffs; the in-game text suggests the flowers are a way of saying thank you.

Atmosphere: Bright colour, open sky and holiday cheer, with paint everywhere and tourists floating up to the sky attraction.

Dangers: Not hazardous; some Whopperflowers turn up during the paint-drum task in the quest.

Travel: Reached on foot from Easybreeze Market and Huha Hill. The Airborne Asha is reached by hot air balloon.

Quests: To Colorfall Cliffs! (part 2.1 of The World Is Your Canvas!) takes place here and at the Airborne Asha.

In the quest the Traveler first colours the Foamflower Fields while indwelling an Asha, then takes the balloon to the Airborne Asha, has a spray-painting contest with Bennett that ends in a final showdown at the top, and finishes at a scenic spot the staff recommend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Colorfall Cliffs are open as a resort attraction.

51.content:
Concealed Land of Enigmas (also: Hidden Land of Enigmas, Enigmatic Land): The Concealed Land of Enigmas is a small cave hidden behind a waterfall west of Wavey Bay, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also called Tenochtzitoc) on Natlan's western edge. A woven-scroll mystic arts implement at its end opens a portal to a temple that the wiki calls the Pyro Archon Temple. It is part of the quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc, added in 5.8.

The resort around it is a bright holiday area, but the cave is a quiet, forgotten place with something older behind it.

Geography: Behind the waterfall is a rock pile; breaking it reveals a short cave whose end holds the old implement, a woven scroll. The tourist beaches and attractions of Wavey Bay lie just east of it. Easybreeze Holiday Resort is a sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan, and its Tenochtzitoc name is said by a local to mean a 'cavern of stone and prickly pears', though prickly pears no longer grow there.

Through the portal, a temple with seven stone seats around a central structure opens out: each seat carries an inscription honouring a hero of the lost settlement of Tenochtzitoc (Tupac, Menilek, Sundjatta, Tenoch, Wanjiru, Sanhaj Kompore and Burkina). Stone tablets nearby carry fragments of warnings, including one signed Shulevitz that speaks of cloaking the Enigmatic Land and shrouding the palace so only the legacy of heroes can awaken it. Other tablets and a booklet, signed Gloharry and Cochanina, refer to blocking the Mare Jivari and holding back a Black Tide, and a more recent notebook signed Isaja records a task completed.

History: Citlali reasons that the temple was built about five hundred years ago, by the Pyro Archons of that time, to temporarily contain Bakunawa, the Abyssal monster that devoured whole villages. The cave's implement was too old to work: its spirit had long dissipated, and Citlali said every caster is a different lock needing its own key. In the quest it was revived when the Asha, benevolent souls of the Mare Jivari, were drawn to the relic of Sanhaj that the Traveler and Citlali carried.

Enjou of the Abyss Order, who had been trailing them, arrives in the temple and says he had hoped the woven scroll would take him to the Mare Jivari. Beyond the temple's central seat the quest continues in the Mare Jivari itself, where the Traveler fights a piece of Bakunawa using the Calamity of Eshu, Sanhaj's ritual sword.

Inside the Mare Jivari Enjou tells a story, which he admits is partly a distraction, about Tenochtzitoc: a lost settlement of Anemo-wielding warriors, exiled after the old kingdom's civil war, whose last defender was Tenoch; the place where their bones lie, he says, is called the 'Windless Land'. He adds that relatives who had left earlier for the 'true land of wind' became the Muratans. The quest does not confirm his account, and he used the telling to push Citlali's presence out of his body.

People: Citlali, the Masters of the Night-Wind's elder, and Enjou of the Abyss Order both appear here in the quest, which also concerns Pucli and Papar. See their own entries.

Quests: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc (World Quest, 5.8) leads here via Enjou's redrawn map. It is a prerequisite that A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night! be completed before it starts. After the quest, the player can return to touch the implement; the temple's central stone then leads to the Night Kingdom and the Mare Jivari.

Atmosphere: After the cheerful noise of the resort the cave is silent: water curtain, damp stone, and an old unsettling hush. On the far side of the portal the light is strange and the Wayob cannot be sensed.

Dangers: Little in the cave itself. Beyond the temple, in the Mare Jivari, the quest fights a fragment of Bakunawa, whose power Enjou says can corrupt even the passage of time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cave and portal are open to visitors; the Pyro Archon Temple can be reached again at will. No new development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

52.comment: Concealed Land of Enigmas: Pyro Archon Temple
52.content:
The 'Pyro Archon Temple' is the wiki's unofficial name for the sealed temple behind the Concealed Land's portal. It contains seven stone seats honouring heroes, a waterfall with tablets at its back, and two side rooms with a wind-worn booklet and a notebook. According to Citlali it was built about five hundred years ago to contain Bakunawa, and the heroes' legacy 'awakens' it. Its central structure leads to the Night Kingdom and, from there, to the Mare Jivari.

Notes there speak of sealing the borders and containing the Mare Jivari as a task for more than one generation, and one cheerful line reads 'Task complete. Now I sing!'.

53.comment: Concealed Land of Enigmas: Bakunawa and Tenoch's sacrifice
53.content: Per Citlali, Bakunawa was the most terrifying Abyssal monster to attack Natlan five hundred years ago, regrowing from any remains. It was destroyed by Tenoch's sacrifice: Sanhaj Kompore engraved border spells on his body, Tenoch let himself be swallowed, and Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom inside the monster. The explosion shattered it, though some believe it never truly died.

54.content:
Core of Chu'ulel (also: Core of Chuulel, Chu'ulel Light Core, Bloodline's Control Hub, New Core of Chu'ulel): The Core of Chu'ulel is a cavern beneath the Vision Serpent's Sanctum in Ochkanatlan, the ruined dragon city of Natlan. Inside is the Chu'ulel Light Core, a glowing orb that pulses like a heart and once powered all of Ochkanatlan. Och-Kan built this core by enslaving his own draconic half, and sealed his mind inside it to fight alongside his people. By 7.1 it has been cleansed of Abyssal energy but is spent, leaving only a piece of Pyrophosphorite.

The name echoes the Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya word 'ch'ulel', the soul or essence centred in the heart (a real-world etymology noted by the wiki). Its maker is the Sacred Lord Och-Kan, who in the present day takes the form of the dragonspirit Cocouik.

Geography: A cavern below the Vision Serpent's Sanctum, reached after the quest Adventure in the Land of Mists. The map divides it into a Secret Path, with a tower, and an Interior, with tents, pots of scrolls and a transparent barrier gate, around the Light Core. In the quest the Traveler purges Abyssal blight from the ruin, after which the core drops. An adventurer's notes say the Secret Source Automatons here, unlike those elsewhere, seem to understand speech.

Gameplay note: the Radiant Pillars and Radiant Fragments that the Traveler uses to purge the Abyssal blight are part of the area's mechanisms, introduced in the Palace of the Vision Serpent quest.

History: When Och-Kan became king of Ochkanatlan he tried to make the dragon inside the Old Core of Chu'ulel power the city for him, since its mechanisms responded only to draconic energy. She refused, and he trapped the dragon in the Old Core. Writing in the Holy Sovereign's Notes, concluded that the only way to build a core that owed allegiance to humanity alone was to enslave the 'draconic' part of himself, so that it would stay imprisoned beneath human boots even if his human parts perished. The result was the new Core of Chu'ulel, which only he could command.

At some point he placed his mind inside the core to fight beside his people, then fell inactive, leaving at least one Secret Source Automaton to guard it. Abyssal corruption slowly rotted the Light Core. According to a nameless adventurer's notes, the adventurer (identified with Bona) used Pyrophosphorite on her own body to awaken the dragonspirit slumbering in the heart of the machine, found it small, green as turquoise, and called it Cocouik. In the present day the Traveler and Paimon purge the Abyssal energy; the core falls and loses the last of its vitality, and only a piece of Pyrophosphorite remains inside.

Other notes in the interior record Och-Kan's reasoning: the Recording Officers' reports showed Abyssal corrosion in the controllable range; the city must remain permanently sealed so the Abyss cannot break through; and 'hope' alone must never be forsaken. A note in the Secret Path tower laments that its writer could not return to the flames alongside 'him' and calls the writer an unworthy beast; the wiki ties it to Och-Kan.

Quests: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, Act II: Adventure in the Land of Mists leads to the Sanctum; Palace of the Vision Serpent is set in the Core (cleansing the Abyss, protecting the fallen core from waves of monsters, and finding Pyrophosphorite wrapped in a nameless adventurer's notes). In Moment of Awakening Och-Kan names the Core as the place Bona woke him from.

Atmosphere: The heartbeat-like pulse of the Light Core, Abyssal blight eating at the structure, and tents and pots of scrolls left behind. The notes sound like a ruler reasoning his way toward ever harsher measures to keep his people safe.

Dangers: Abyssal blight, Abyssal vortices and the Tenebrous Mimesis and Thundercraven Rifthound enemies that attack the fallen core; Secret Source Automatons, though one fights beside the Traveler once the core is protected.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Core is cleansed but dead: the Light Core lost its last vitality, and what remains is a piece of Pyrophosphorite. Cocouik later regained Och-Kan's body and spoke as him before dying.

Cocouik's reawakening as Och-Kan and his death in Moment of Awakening ended his hold on the city. No later development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

55.comment: Core of Chu'ulel: Holy Sovereign's Notes
55.content: The Holy Sovereign's Notes are fragmentary writings by Och-Kan scattered through Ochkanatlan. In them he insists that only humans should decide human fate, distrusts every power greater than humanity, and decides to enslave his draconic half; later notes describe the pressure of keeping the city sealed against the Abyss and the hope he clung to. Some pages are smeared and unreadable.

56.content: Cocouik is the small, turquoise-green dragonspirit that travels with the Traveler in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm. The adventurer's notes describe waking it in the Core of Chu'ulel with Pyrophosphorite. In Moment of Awakening the dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, Och-Kan's body, is defeated; Cocouik's mind rejoins it and speaks as Och-Kan, who dies soon afterwards.

57.content:
Cradle of Fleeting Dreams (also: Cradle of Dreams): The Cradle of Fleeting Dreams is the castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan, the ruined ancient city of Natlan. It stands over Ashflow Street, the settlement at its base, and has a throne at the top of a staircase.

It is a Point of Interest in the Ochkanatlan area, added with Version 5.2. The meaning of the in-game name is not explained in the sources read.

Places: Ashflow Street lies at the foot of the building. A staircase leads up to the throne, and at its foot stands a pot of scrolls holding a Spiritcaller's note. The Vision Serpent's Sanctum is listed as a Point of Interest under the Cradle.

The building can be viewed both near the top and from lower down; no official floor plan or room names are given in the sources read.

History: Nothing in the sources read states who built the Cradle or who ruled from its throne. The surrounding city, Ochkanatlan, belonged to the ancient alliance led by the Holy Sovereign (Och-Kan), but the Cradle itself is not tied to him by name.

A note at the stair foot was written by Liriwu, a young Spiritcaller of the Masters of the Night-Wind. She records being sickened by what she saw, being told by her uncle Copan that the souls of such creatures could be freed if the Python King's treasure were found, and wondering why that king died in the Abyss if the treasure could destroy it. She resolves not to waver for everyone's sake. This is her own account and fear, not an authoritative explanation.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and abandoned; open for exploration in Ochkanatlan as of 7.1.

58.content:
Derelict Masonry Dock: The Derelict Masonry Dock is an abandoned dragon-era facility hidden deep in the heart of the mountain at Atocpan, in the Remnants of Tetenanco area of Natlan. In its day, ash-gray mechanisms (Secret Source Automatons) driven by golden runes did the labour of flesh there, bringing grand designs to life above pools of flame. It is now a desolate shell.

The flavour text says the era ended when tyrannical outsiders (linked on the wiki to the Heavenly Principles) arrived, after which the once-powerful dragon race stagnated in submission. The only visitors left are mourners of that vanished age. The text also promises treasures for those who long to reach beyond the heavens (Celestia). In gameplay terms it is a Domain of Blessing that drops artifacts.

Atmosphere: A cavernous, half-ruined shipyard-like space of dead machinery, flickering firelight and the shadow of a once-grand design.

Dangers: Gameplay layer: Tatankasaur whelps and warriors, Ferocious Warriors (Human Ram, Wrestler, Grappler) and a Furnace Shell Mountain Weasel as the boss. Its Ley Line Disorder boosts plunging attackers: a Plunging Attack hit gives +30% CRIT DMG and +20% ATK for 15 seconds.

Artifact sets offered: Long Night's Oath, Finale of the Deep Galleries, Tiny Miracle and Scholar. It was added in version 5.5.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently accessible in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot is tied to it.

59.comment: Derelict Masonry Dock: Golden-rune automatons of the dock
59.content: Flavour text: golden runes (Iridescent Inscription) drove ash-gray Secret Source Automatons that replaced manual labour in the dragons' workshops above liquid phlogiston. Not elaborated by quests; keep it as atmosphere.

60.content:
Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also: Tenochtzitoc): Easybreeze Holiday Resort is a bright, sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan. It is also called Tenochtzitoc, the old settlement where the war with the Abyss began and finally ended. The resort opened in 5.8 for a trial summer season: sandy beaches, a market, dance stages and playful Asha, colour-loving mascots that are secretly the souls of people lost in the Mare Jivari. Behind the fun lies the grave of the hero Tenoch and a temple built to hold back the Bakunawa.

Tenochtzitoc means 'cavern of stone and prickly pears' in the local tongue, though prickly pears no longer grow here. The resort is the first summer-themed map added permanently to the game.

Geography: An island west of Natlan. Its main areas are Colorfall Cliffs (green fields streaked with swirling colour and the 'Airborne Asha' attraction in the sky), Guiztli Ridge, Wavey Bay (sandy beaches, pristine water, water attractions) and Tete Isle, along with the Easybreeze Market and the Concealed Land of Enigmas.

The Concealed Land of Enigmas is a small cavern behind a waterfall west of Wavey Bay. A mystic portal there leads to the Pyro Archon Temple and, through it, to a small corner of the Mare Jivari, the westernmost part of the island that was blown off the timeline.

Places: Easybreeze Market, the resort's commercial hub and many visitors' first stop, with restaurants, specialty shops and decor by the local Asha. Tete Isle, a lively island known for the specialty drink Aphimead, with a Dance-Off Stage, Brewblossom Stores, Me & Dew and The Dewdrop. Colorfall Cliffs, Wavey Bay and Guiztli Ridge, each with attractions. The Concealed Land of Enigmas and the Pyro Archon Temple.

Easybreeze Market includes Asha's Treasure Trove, Shoal's Haven (a seafood restaurant) and the Seven-Colored Statue, a giant octopus-like statue spouting seven bubbles that visitors can paint with colour. Tete Isle is only reachable after the story quest The World Is Your Canvas! reaches its fifth step. The Pyro Archon Temple holds inscriptions for Tupac, Menilek, Sundjatta, Tenoch (whose remains are buried there), Wanjiru, Sanhaj Kompore (also buried there) and Burkina, as well as tablets signed by the Pyro Archons Shulevitz, Gloharry and Cochanina.

At check-in the quest gives the player an Easybreeze Album and a resort map. Resort staff member Ukucha describes four main areas: Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge, Wavey Bay and Tete Isle.

People: Resort staff, vendors and tourists, together with Asha. The resort staff, many Natlanese, run lodging, food and attractions. Mualani, Chasca, Bennett, and other visitors tested the new resort in 5.8.

Notable figures include Ukucha at check-in, Teuciztli of Shoal's Haven, Macuahuitl of Asha's Treasure Trove and Aloha, manager of the Alpaca Park. Enjou, an Abyss Lector, appears in The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc searching for the Mare Jivari. Citlali investigates there. Venti and Mavuika quietly work to help souls trapped in the Mare Jivari go home.

Culture: During the Sunspray Summer Resort event of 5.8 the resort's opening was marked with attractions and games, and the Natlan Adventurers' Guild sent invitations to adventurers across Teyvat to try the resort out.

Asha are the resort's mascots: special Monetoo that are more sociable and intelligent than ordinary ones because they come from human souls. The word 'Asha' in Tenochtzitoc culture has two meanings in the game, 'benevolent soul' and 'ashes', the second referring to ashes blown from the Mare Jivari. The resort's guests can wear Asha headbands.

History: Before the cataclysm the Muratan tribe settled at Tenochtzitoc. About five hundred years ago the Abyss invaded and the Bakunawa, a mountain-sized beast made by Rhinedottir, devoured villages on the west of Natlan. The hero Tenoch, a Muratan who had been exiled for his battle-mania, was the last survivor of the settlement. He gathered six allies from the tribes and led them into a battle against the Abyss at the place that became the Mare Jivari. Natlan/History marks the Abyss's invasion in that year as the start of the Night Warden Wars.

Sanhaj of the Masters of the Night-Wind engraved Tenoch's body with Phlogiston Engraving, Tenoch let the Bakunawa swallow him, and Sanhaj raised a miniature Night Kingdom inside it. The clash shattered the beast and killed both men. The Bakunawa could regrow, so Pyro Archons built the temple to contain it. Natlan/History says Cochanina, Shulevitz and Gloharry died doing so and that Isaja, the last of them, managed to contain it. To keep the Abyss from spreading across Teyvat, Barbatos blew the whole Mare Jivari off the timeline, trapping the souls of those who died there. About twenty years ago some of those souls merged with Monetoo and became the Asha. Around the same time a mountain-sized beast was reported roaming the Mare Jivari and the region vanished.

Bennett's parents, Aroni and Macani, and the rest of the Tecpatl's Flintblades adventure team were attacked by Abyssal monsters in the Mare Jivari and gave up their forms and memories to protect the infant Bennett; they lingered as Asha. In 5.8 Venti, with Mavuika's help, collected the souls who wished to return; Aroni and Macani regained their memories, were briefly reunited with their son and passed into the Night Kingdom. After the end of the Night Warden Wars, more people began settling in the area and the Easybreeze Holiday Resort was founded and began trial operations. Enjou, who sought a forgotten homeland, finished his search in the restricted Mare Jivari and decided to enter the true one.

Atmosphere: Salt air, sunlight and music, brightly coloured paint splashed on rocks and walls, Asha bobbing through the crowd, with a gentle undertone: the island's ashy western end and its monuments remind visitors that this was a battlefield not long ago.

Dangers: The resort is mostly safe, though a few hilichurls turn up in quest areas and Abyssal monsters lurk in the caves tied to the Mare Jivari. Pirates from Nasha Town, led by Radius Bone Jack, are mentioned in letters on Tete Isle.

Letters found there show a plan by Black Reef Rekis to have Radius Bone Jack's crew capture Monetoo for wealthy clients, with a man named Icahua sent to watch them. A defiant line scrawled at the end of one letter says there is to be no catching Asha. The Bakunawa still exists as a restrained fragment in the Mare Jivari, and an Abyssal simulation of the Mare Jivari exists as well.

Travel: Teleport waypoints are spread around the island. Visitors move between the market, bay and cliffs on foot, and the player can indwell an Asha to cross walls and water. Leaving the resort area ejects the player from the Asha.

Quests: The Sunspray Summer Resort story quests run: To a Carefree Vacation!, The World Is Your Canvas!, The Surprise That Awaits Us All! and A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night!. Their event was limited, but version 6.3 added an Event Quests page that lets players accept such permanent event storylines later. World quests: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc and Traces of Chroma.

Traces of Chroma introduces the Asha Zolton, created by the Masters of the Night-Wind priest Alu, who passed his memories to the Asha through the tribe's mnemonic arts; Alu lost access to those memories himself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the resort is open. Venti and Mavuika have guided the souls who wished to return home out of the Mare Jivari.

Only a small corner of the Mare Jivari is explorable. The Bakunawa is restrained but could return.

The wiki reports no later story changes to the island except bug fixes in 6.0 to 6.7.

61.content:
Asha are exploration-mechanic Monetoo exclusive to the resort and its mascots. They roam freely, and some are created from the souls of those who perished in the Mare Jivari. They are more sociable and intelligent than ordinary Monetoo. Asha can also be created by human hands: the Masters of the Night-Wind priest Alu made the Asha Zolton while researching a link between Asha and Saurian Inscriptions.

Bennett's parents Aroni and Macani lived as Asha for years, and when freed from the Mare Jivari they regained their memories and could switch between Asha and human form before passing on.

62.comment: Easybreeze Holiday Resort: Pyro Archon Temple and the Bakunawa
62.content:
The Pyro Archon Temple is reached from the Concealed Land of Enigmas. Citlali believes the Pyro Archons built it about five hundred years ago to contain the Bakunawa. It has stone tablets from several Pyro Archons and monuments for Tenoch and the heroes who fought with him.

The Bakunawa is a mountain-sized beast created by Rhinedottir whose immortality is not from Life but from a different, transcendental form of Abyssal power. It can be defeated for a time and then returns after 72 hours (a gameplay detail). A fragment of it was restrained by the Traveler and Enjou in The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc.

63.content: The Mare Jivari was the westernmost part of Tenochtzitoc. It was named after a great battle there during the cataclysm. Present-day descriptions call it an empty 'endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow', but it once held a sea of fire. It was blown off the timeline by Barbatos to stop the Abyss spreading.

64.content: Tenoch, also known by the title Tenoyollotzin, was a Muratan warrior exiled for his battle-mania yet respected by the other tribes. His giant obsidian club, the Talking Stick, got its name from his habit of using it to 'mediate' disputes. He gathered six heroes to resist the Abyss and died at the Mare Jivari with Sanhaj. He could not be revived by the Ode of Resurrection because he had already lost his Ancient Name.

65.content:
Easybreeze Market: Easybreeze Market is the commercial heart of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort and often the first place tourists see. It has restaurants, specialty shops and playful decor made by the resort's Asha.

Vendors here include the owners of Asha's Treasure Trove, Floral Whispers and Shoal's Haven, a dessert seller and a seller of 'suns'.

Geography: The market is the resort's retail district and the entrance to the island's other areas, with Colorfall Cliffs, Huha Hill and Tete Isle nearby.

Its viewpoint description is titled 'Pleasant Street'.

Places: Shops and restaurants: Asha's Treasure Trove (owner Macuahuitl), Floral Whispers (Motolinia), Shoal's Haven (owner Teuciztli, with Lawaia as an employee), Puff-Up Pauldrons (Mazatl), Street Fighting Fontainian (Tzompantli) and a dessert stall run by Fournier.

The resort's Seven-Colored Statue, a giant octopus-like figure that visitors can paint, also stands in the market area according to the resort entry.

People: A large cast of vendors, tourists and Asha. Other named residents include Challwa (Gift Egg Ambassador), Kanei, Zhaka and Zhaka's Asha Azhka, and the Ceremonial Greeter 'Teteltetl'.

Some NPCs only appear after specific quests: Tochtli, Zolin and Zolton after Traces of Chroma, and Ukucha and Nataba ('Sun' seller) after step 9 of To a Carefree Vacation!. Zhaka only appears after he has been rescued in Colorfall Cave, and is Kanei's apprentice.

Also listed are Apuaq, Ifelayo, Irqichaykuna Nui, Kapaia, Micha, Navaratra, Philpot and Tecizma. The wiki gives no more profile information for most of them.

Culture: Part of the market's story was part of the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort event; several quests start with the Traveler arriving here.

Local Asha design the decor, and the merchants sell food, drink and holiday souvenirs to tourists.

History: Opened with the resort during its trial season. Quest Traces of Chroma is set here and concerns the Asha Zolton, which the Masters of the Night-Wind priest Alu made.

Atmosphere: Busy, bright and relaxed: stalls and chatter, Asha weaving through the crowd and a feel of a holiday town.

Dangers: Safe. The only trouble linked to the market is the counterfeit Koholasaur doll scam, whose hostage worked in Colorfall Cave.

Quests: Traces of Chroma (world quest). To a Carefree Vacation! (resort story) begins with arrival and introductions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the market is open.

66.content:
Esoteric Arrays: The Esoteric Arrays are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, within the Great Volcano of Tollan in Natlan, where the ancient dragons once ran arrays that performed arithmetic calculations. Today the ruins are overgrown with Abyssal corrosion.

They lie on the way to the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. To uncover that path, the Traveler and the Little One must cleanse the corrupted ruins here, with the help of a Secret Source Servant and a Secret Source Beam Cannon.

Geography: The Arrays sit in the Dragons' Residence level of the Ancient Sacred Mountain. The ruins are ancient stonework, now fouled by Oozing Cores that carry the Abyss's corrosion.

A Secret Source Dragon Idol stands in the area; interacting with it unlocks the Secret Source Beam Cannon, a cannon that destroys Oozing Cores.

People: No named residents. Secret Source Servants move through the ruins, and one is harassed by Rockfond Rifthound Whelps, and the Traveler defends it.

The Little One accompanies the Traveler throughout, and Paimon comments on a glowing object after the cores are destroyed.

History: The arrays were built by the dragon civilization, which used them for arithmetic calculation. The wiki's source for this is the quest Where Once There Was a Calculation Array.

Beyond that, only the ruin's condition is known: the Abyss's corrosion has crept into the ancient works, and it blocks the road to the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Quests: Where Once There Was a Calculation Array is one of three sub-quests in In Search of a Hidden Heart (part of the World Quest series Chronicler of the Crumbling City). The Traveler must clear Abyssal corrosion: defeat the Rockfond Rifthound Whelps accosting a Secret Source Servant, follow the Servant, defeat more whelps near the Dragon Idol, then use the Beam Cannon to destroy the Oozing Cores. The reward is a Phlogiston Unit.

As the Traveler nears the exit a message reads "O Chosen of Dragons, the power of blazing fire now rests within you", and the cannon gains a Lava Buff. Afterwards Paimon notes that the Abyss around the place should be cleaned up and spots a glowing object after the Little One roars; it is the Phlogiston Unit.

Gameplay note: the cannon destroys Oozing Cores in an area of effect and never runs out of ammunition. The quest awards one Precious, one Exquisite and one Common Chest. Completing this quest and its two companions, Where Once Force Was Reversed and Where Once There Were Arms Aplenty, awards the achievement "Questioning the Heart of Flames".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arrays are cleared of corrosion and idle; no later story role is recorded.

67.comment: Esoteric Arrays: Secret Source Beam Cannon
67.content: The Secret Source Dragon Idol at the Arrays unlocks the Secret Source Beam Cannon, a cannon that the Traveler fires to destroy the Abyssal Oozing Cores that foul the ruins. It receives a Lava Buff when the Traveler nears the exit.

68.content:
Fallingstar Fields (also: Tephric Ruins): Fallingstar Fields is a subarea of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Tephric Ruins, a section of old ruins that the volcano threw out about five hundred years ago, around the time of the cataclysm. Inside are broken pieces of Secret Source machinery arranged as if for worship, and a hidden room with a sealed report about the dragonborn.

The ruins are the setting of the world quest Investigator of Ancient Ruins and are connected to the old Secret Source Servant Ehecatl.

Geography: Open ground below the Great Volcano of Tollan with the Tephric Ruins at its centre. A local specialty is dracolite.

The ruins are said to be a piece of a larger structure, ejected from the volcano. A floating platform in the middle of the ruins is empty at first.

Places: The Tephric Ruins. Inside are a deactivated source core, three strange Secret Source structures and a floating ruins platform.

The source core resembles the core of a Secret Source Automaton. The three structures resemble a hunter-seeker's sheath, outer shell and limbs. In-game text calls these broken parts an object of worship, perhaps placed by tribespeople. The platform once held something; a relic called That Which Was Once Ehecatl, the dormant form of a Secret Source Servant, fits there.

Returning the relic opens a hidden room with a Secret Source Sentinel and an Iridescent Inscription that holds the sealed records.

People: Nzaya and Kimosi are the tribespeople met during Investigator of Ancient Ruins, and the Traveler is joined by Little One.

The ruins' original makers are not shown. The sealed report is written by people concerned for the Dragonborn; its authors are not named.

History: The wiki says the ruins were thrown from the volcano roughly five hundred years ago, linking the date to the cataclysm.

The hidden records are titled by the in-game text as 'Items That Should Perhaps Be Deleted'. The report on reversing the regressive evolution of the Dragonborn says previous regressive events damaged the physical malleability of the Dragonborn. Those who have regressed can adapt to a stable changed environment, but the power such bodies can bear cannot be restored by the methods tried. Only selection through bloodlines and generations of modifications, using the mark known as the Flamelord's Blessing, might do it. The authors judge that the cost is too great: there is not enough time, the bodies of many regressed kin cannot take the power needed, and the experiments are too cruel, so the report should remain sealed.

A later comment of unknown date notes this might be an opportunity, if the experiment could be used to get past a barrier of destiny. The speaker, whom the wiki links to Kukulkan, mentions a brother, whom the wiki links to Xiuhcoatl, and wonders whether the promise seen in humanity was justified or a mistake. They hope any kin might reach a final choice that redeems the desolate years.

Atmosphere: Ash-grey, silent and a little eerie: old stonework dotted with dead machine parts that look as if they could twitch to life the moment the viewer looks away.

Dangers: During Investigator of Ancient Ruins, Abyssal monsters and Hilichurls are in the ruins, and a mimic chest triggers an earthquake with falling stalactites while the Traveler fights.

The enemies appear in waves: Hilichurls, a Tenebrous Mimesis, rifthounds and tepetlisauri.

Travel: Reached within Atocpan. The ruins can also be entered by dropping through a hole at the top.

Quests: Investigator of Ancient Ruins, which can stand in for A Brief History of Rocks to complete The Way Into the Mountain. The hidden room is tied to the story quest The Frozen, Rekindling Land, which yields the relic.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins stand quiet and open; the sealed report can be read.

No later change to the ruins is recorded through 7.1.

key: Items That Should Perhaps Be Deleted
69.content:
The Tephric Ruins in Fallingstar Fields are a section of ancient ruins that the volcano ejected around five hundred years ago. They hold broken Secret Source Mechanism parts, an empty platform for the relic of the Secret Source Servant Ehecatl, and a hidden room whose sealed report discusses the regressed Dragonborn and the Flamelord's Blessing.

The report concludes the proposed cure is too cruel, and a later undated comment treats it as a possible chance to break a barrier of destiny.

70.content:
Firethief's Secret Isle: Firethief's Secret Isle is a small island south of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. It is hidden on the map and under constant cloud until all four of its time-trial challenges are completed. It was an ancient trial site and training ground, and only Saurians live there now.

The island is shaped a little like a dragon, and the wiki guesses it was named for the Dragon Prince who stole the flame of Phlogiston.

Geography: An island in the water south of Coatepec Mountain, with a central spot where the fourth challenge appears after the first three.

Once the challenges are complete the island is added to the map and the perpetual overcast weather lifts. A teleport waypoint on it earns the achievement 'Only the Training Grounds Are Left?'.

Places: Four time trial challenges: three that can be done in any order, and a fourth at the island's centre that appears afterwards. Unusually, none of them has a countdown timer.

Manmade structures, decorations and graffiti on the island suggest humans re-used it at some point.

People: Only Saurians live on the isle now.

History: The island was once an ancient trial site and training ground, presumably set up by Natlan's ancient dragons. Later humans seem to have repurposed it, judging by the buildings and graffiti.

The guess that its name comes from Kukulkan fits a tale that he stole the flame of Phlogiston from his kin and gave it to humanity, but another Firethief appears in the tribal tale of Turnfire Night, so the name is unresolved.

The achievement 'Only the Training Grounds Are Left?' is the main in-game statement of its past as a trial site and training ground. That the island is shaped somewhat like a dragon is a wiki observation, not in-game text.

Atmosphere: Before the challenges are cleared, a gloomy, cloud-covered island of old stone. After that it brightens.

Dangers: The challenges are puzzles, not combat; wild Saurians are the main living creatures.

Travel: Not on the map at first; the area is found by travelling south of Coatepec Mountain.

Quests: A set of four time trial challenges, with no storyline quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the isle is a quiet training ground with only Saurian residents.

71.content:
Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds: The Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan. According to the World Quest Sealed Site of Sacrifice it is where Xiuhcoatl created the first Astral Assemblage, a feat comparable to forging a star. The altar was sealed, and the Traveler unseals it.

Activating the Astral Assemblage replays a vision of the ritual: the dragons' success, a quarrel between its creator, identified as Xiuhcoatl, and Kukulkan, who addresses him as his king and elder brother, and a warning of a looming catastrophe. The place also holds the third "Iridescent Legacy" inscription, the last words of one of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords.

Geography: The site has an upper altar where the sealed Astral Assemblage stands, high above, and lower levels with pulverite and a furnace-shell mountain weasel guarding one inscription. The viewpoint here is called "Condensed Altar" and opens only after the quest.

Reaching the sealed device involves pushing stone steps into place to form a path and, optionally, pulling levers. Breaking the seal restores the Assemblage to normal operation and lets it fire a beam of light at the Celestial Axis at the centre of the Sacred City, activating one of the Axis's pillars.

History: The Ritual Grounds are where Xiuhcoatl created the first Astral Assemblage. Phlogiston was compressed under great pressure into a floating, controllable ball of heat, a miniature celestial body.

The creator's brethren cheer "We've done it!" while he stands apart, as if unrelated to the deed. In the vision, Kukulkan congratulates him coldly, saying the achievement is comparable to lunar reconstruction, and says that "that one" (whom the wiki identifies as Nibelung) would have nodded in approval if still alive.

The creator says that if Kukulkan had helped, it might have been finished long ago. Kukulkan answers that he has no interest. The creator urges Kukulkan to help: the All-Plunderer's herald has been driven into the deepest of mountain valleys, but its master's awakening would bring another catastrophe. Kukulkan sneers at the idea of protecting their "pitiable brethren"; the creator says his days are numbered and he must forge a new path for the Dragonborn before the pitch-black shadow smothers them. Kukulkan suggests the Dragonborn find their own way, warning the path may be too narrow, but the creator insists "the narrow way must be walked". Kukulkan finishes by saying that on this alone he cannot concede, or in another version, that the creator once said he would understand the desire in his final moments.

Quests: Sealed Site of Sacrifice is part of The Frozen, Rekindling Land (Chronicler of the Crumbling City). The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One find the Astral Assemblage locked high up, push stone platforms to form a path, break the seal and activate the device, triggering the vision.

Paimon realises that the figures surrounding the platform were the dragons who lived here. The quest awards a Luxurious Chest and two Exquisite Chests, and unlocks the Condensed Altar viewpoint.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grounds are unsealed and unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

72.comment: Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds: Iridescent Legacy Part III
72.content: Found in the lower levels after destroying pulverite and defeating a furnace-shell mountain weasel, this inscription holds the last words of the Fifth Lord, Aj K'astajibal Cha'ama' Ho'o. He rages at humanity's crude misuse of phlogiston, laments that his proposal was rejected by "traitors", taunts humans to sing while they can before the Lord of Light and Heat burns them all, and breaks off addressing Xiuhcoatl: "you alone must not...".

73.content:
Furnace of Fiery Embers (also: Furnaces of Fiery Embers): The Furnace of Fiery Embers names five Source Mechanism sites in Ochkanatlan, Natlan: three in underground caverns (west, southwest and north) and two on small islands (east and southeast).

They are the focus of the hidden exploration objective Stoking the Ancient Flames (5.2). Each furnace has a matching Iridescent Inscription near an old sword, and the inscription reports whether the furnace has been rekindled.

Once all five are rekindled the player can draw the ancient sword, which takes them to a small floating island. Until then the old sword seems bound to the space itself and will not budge.

The wiki marks the objective's name as unofficial, and the sources read leave the furnaces' original function unexplained.

Places: The wiki numbers the sites I to V, though the in-game map labels only some. Furnace I is reached by touching an Iridescent Inscription, II by entering a tower, and III after the achievement Clear the Area, Please! The eastern and southeastern furnaces sit on small islands and are not labelled with numbers.

Furnaces I and II each have an upper and a lower level; furnace III has an entrance, a cave path and an area of ancient ruins.

Quests: Stoking the Ancient Flames is a quest-like exploration objective: activate all five furnaces, then draw the ancient sword. The first step grants the achievement Embers Rekindled and the second grants a copy of the Flute of Ezpitzal. These rewards are a gameplay detail.

History: Canon text read does not say who built the Source Mechanisms or when; they belong to the ancient Ochkanatlan civilisation's technology.

Atmosphere: Old mechanisms coaxed back to life: glowing inscriptions in caves and on small islands.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the five furnaces remain sites to be rekindled by players. No later changes were found.

74.content:
Golden Dusk: Golden Dusk is a restaurant and lodge in the People of the Springs' settlement at Toyac Springs in Natlan, owned by Kupo Nui, the matriarch of the Nui family. It serves chilled drinks, has beautiful scenery and a convenient beach location, and has an in-house singer, Tirda.

It is an old Nui family home that was turned into a restaurant at Chief Amina's suggestion. Business is steady, but the family is frequently short-staffed. Guests may use the kitchen and sleep in tents near the water.

Places: A beachside house turned restaurant, with lodging and a bulletin board. The Hot Spring Retreat: Secret Menu furnishing is designed to resemble it.

Services listed on the bulletin board include use of the kitchen facilities and tents for guests who want to sleep near the water. Kupo Nui lets people help themselves or bring their own ingredients and cook, at no extra charge.

People: Kupo Nui owns the place and greets visitors warmly; Mahina Nui staffs reception; Tirda sings; Wakea Nui appears at night.

At night Wakea Nui asks Kupo Nui whether the family might unite to expand the business instead of each working separately, and she replies that everyone is gainfully employed. Wakea admits to being a little sad that no relative will give them the time of day; at this rate they will never get a second employee for their international travel agency.

History: Originally an old Nui family home, it was converted after Chief Amina noted the wonderful scenery and suggested a restaurant. It has been steadily busy ever since, with both locals and tourists enjoying drinks by the beach.

Kupo Nui says her biggest problem has always been securing staff: she has a big family, but few of them are interested in helping.

The Golden Dusk has held 242 iterations of the regional eating contest Inferno Stomach Supremo. The current champion is Varesa of the Collective of Plenty.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Golden Dusk remains open and steady, with no recorded story role after 5.0.

75.content: Inferno Stomach Supremo is a regional eating competition that has been held 242 times at Golden Dusk, according to its bulletin board. The current champion is Varesa of the Collective of Plenty.

76.content:
Grand Wrestling Grounds (also: Resonating Arena): The Grand Wrestling Grounds is an elevated arena decorated with massive bull horns in Atocpan, Natlan. It is the central hub of the Collective of Plenty tribe, where its many athletic competitions are held, and is also called the Resonating Arena.

Staff listed here include Macacoz, a professional wrestling referee, Muuziyaa of the Flying Squad and Tonaca, the logistics manager. Cuaxilo is also listed among the NPCs, and a Collective of Plenty Bulletin Board stands nearby.

The arena appeared in version 5.5 with the Collective of Plenty content. The alternate name Resonating Arena is attested in the quest Ardent Land of Plenty.

Sources read give no founding history or rules of the contests; keep those unstated in scenes unless a Collective of Plenty entry supplies them.

Places: A raised arena crowned with bull horns, forming the central hub of the tribe in Atocpan.

People: Referees, runners and logistics staff of the Collective of Plenty work here. Their individual stories belong to their own entries.

Culture: Competition is a public pastime for the tribe: the arena hosts its many athletic contests.

Atmosphere: Loud and lively: contests, referees and logistics bustle under giant horns.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an active arena in Atocpan. No later changes were found.

77.content:
Great Volcano of Tollan (also: Volcano of Tollan, Sacred Mountain, Tollan Volcano): The Great Volcano of Tollan is the enormous active volcano that covers Atocpan in the southwest of Natlan. Ancient scrolls call it the Sacred Mountain. It still erupts from time to time and is said to have been far more active in darker ages. It was once the dwelling of the ancient dragons, and the legends of Natlan keep returning to it.

Legend says the dragons' palace lies beneath the magma, that the sage Kukulkan stole the primal fire from it in the form of Pyrophosphorite, and that Xbalanque fought and defeated the Abyss-corrupted Xiuhcoatl here. Inside the volcano lies the Ancient Sacred Mountain, an ancient city that the Traveler enters during the quest chain Path to the Flaming Peaks.

It is also where the legend of the Golden Entreaties leads: bringing both discs to the volcano is said to lift the Flamelord's Blessing from a Saurian. The 5.5 finale shows that this legend hid a far darker purpose.

Geography: The volcano encompasses the whole of Atocpan in the southwest of Natlan, the same area that holds the home of the Collective of Plenty. The Skyfire Circlet crowns it, and the way into the mountain opens from there. The tribal legend of the Volcano Lord places a Shadow Pin above the Sulfurous Veins, a locale linked to the Children of Echoes.

Atocpan's own description names the volcano as the area's defining feature. Spiritways let travellers reach the Skyfire Circlet; the quest Nahuatzin's Leap triggers on arrival there.

Atmosphere: Heat, sulfur, ash and the rumble of a mountain that is never fully asleep. Eruptions rain burning rocks across the area and send boulders rolling in places, so people and creatures take cover until it passes and then carry on.

Documents left around Atocpan speak darkly of people who returned from the volcano changed. Treat these as in-world rumour rather than established fact.

Dangers: The volcano erupts periodically. During an eruption fireballs of Pyro fall across Atocpan and hurt anything they hit, and enemies seek shelter too. Phlogiston inside the mountain is harmful to those who linger. In story terms, the pilgrimage to the volcano is deadly.

In Manqu's questline, Pacal of the Children of Echoes at first refuses to allow the pilgrimage because many who attempted it failed the trials and died; he relents after a brief duel with the Traveler.

History: In ancient times the volcano was the dwelling of the Pyro dragons, and Xiuhcoatl shaped the city of Tollan inside it. When the dragon civilisation crumbled, the Abyss is said to have taken the mountain. Later, Xbalanque, not yet the Pyro Archon, fought and killed the corrupted Xiuhcoatl here.

Item and book texts add that Kukulkan, Xiuhcoatl's younger brother, is said to have stolen the primal fire from the palace under the magma as Pyrophosphorite. A fable in the Records of Hanan Pacha, which historians judge unhistorical, calls Xiuhcoatl the great lord of the volcano and has a vain winged dragon claim his treasures while he sleeps.

The tribal legend The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins describes a time when the great beasts withdrew and a dark Volcano Lord, a black-and-purple salamander-like giant, occupied the empty volcano and tormented the tribes. The hero Traore of the Children of Echoes tricked and pinned it with help from the Wayob and four phlogiston nails. It is a children's story and should not be read as literal chronology.

Lore: Tradition says that bringing both Golden Entreaties to the volcano can wash the Flamelord's Blessing from a Saurian. The blessing is a mark tied to Xiuhcoatl that grows into uncontrollable power and madness. The tribes gave up the custom since no warrior ever succeeded, and now simply care for afflicted Saurians until they die.

The Golden Entreaties were made when Xbalanque split Xiuhcoatl's eye; one went to Xbalanque and the other to Kukulkan. The Saurian Relics Association researcher Manqu believed they were only legend until the Traveler showed him one. Mposo adds that the mark appears every dozen or several dozen years, and that Saurians who walk into the volcano alone are never heard from again.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the volcano is still active, still erupts, and remains an open-world landmark of Atocpan. Its interior can be entered after Nahuatzin's Leap. After the Traveler and Little One declined to activate Huitzilopochtli, the Tollan systems ceased maintenance and the draconic remnants faded; the array is obsolete.

The wiki pages read show no role for the volcano in Nod-Krai (6.x) or the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya content. Do not invent later involvement.

Quests: Key quests: Nahuatzin's Leap (the first part of Path to the Flaming Peaks), where the party reaches the Skyfire Circlet and leaps into the crater, and An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (the only part of A Finale Emberforged), set in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Earlier, Revelations from the Past and The Road Ahead in Tequemecan Valley introduce the Golden Entreaties and the idea of a pilgrimage to the volcano.

78.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: Xbalanque and Xiuhcoatl's battle
78.content:
Long before the present, Xbalanque, not yet the Pyro Archon, fought the corrupted Xiuhcoatl at the volcano. He pierced the weak spots in the dragon's eyes, one of which split into two disc-like fragments, and both fell from a great height. Xiuhcoatl stayed dead while Xbalanque was wreathed in flame and revived. Whether anything of Xiuhcoatl remains is disputed.

According to Kukulkan, Xiuhcoatl was beaten because one of his eyes served as the control hub of Huitzilopochtli. The wiki notes that Xiuhcoatl's remains can be seen at the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

79.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: Golden Entreaties and the Flamelord's Blessing
79.content:
The Golden Entreaties are two identical white discs with golden patterns, said to have been made from Xiuhcoatl's eyes. Legend claims that a strongly bonded human and Saurian can bring them to the volcano to cleanse the Saurian of the Flamelord's Blessing.

Kukulkan, the Sage of the Stolen Flame, reveals in 5.5 that he created the legend so a human would bring both discs and a blessed Saurian to Huitzilopochtli. He and Och-Kan both hoped Little One would make the right choice. Och-Kan had hidden his disc on the Tonatiuh because he feared its power.

80.content:
Huitzilopochtli is a device built by Xiuhcoatl in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain to turn Natlan into phlogiston and so destroy the Abyss, at the cost of nearly everything alive there. It is activated by reuniting the two Golden Entreaties.

In A Finale Emberforged, Kukulkan urged Little One to activate it. Little One declined and the Primeval Source Dragon Mech guarding it was defeated; the Tollan systems and Kukulkan then faded. The wiki records a non-canonical alternative ending for the other choice; ignore it.

81.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins
81.content:
A tribal story told to Children of Echoes children. A giant black-and-purple salamander-like lord took the empty volcano, bathed in the springs, at its worst swallowed the Collective of Plenty, and finally coveted the gems of the Children of Echoes' valleys. Traore tricked it with a stone chamber, and the Wayob's four pins turned into phlogiston nails to pin it.

The tale ties several tribes together: Tatankasaurs help free the Collective of Plenty, the People of the Springs suffer from its smog, and the Scions of the Canopy from its sparks. It is a legend, so keep it as folklore.

82.content:
Guiztli Path: Guiztli Path is a winding cavern linking Villa Guiztli to Castle Joquiratto on the Easybreeze resort island. It is a stretch of the resort's immersive adventure in which visitors play heroes defending a town from the villain El Capoctus Joquiratto.

Nochtli lackeys, the play-acting 'bandits', mill about the path in staged skirmishes.

Geography: A cavern under Guiztli Ridge. Villa Guiztli is the underground town at one end and Castle Joquiratto, the villain's stronghold, at the other.

The map names the zone as the northern part of the ridge's inner cavern.

People: Nochtli lackeys and the cardboard cutouts and Nochtlins of the villa.

One lackey shoots red paint at a chest and shouts 'Enemies ahead!', then announces himself as the enemy and surrenders when the Traveler does not fall for it.

Villa Guiztli at one end is an underground town inhabited by cardboard cutouts and Nochtlins, and it is fully unlocked only by progressing the quest To Guiztli Ridge!. Before the quest ends its capybaras and alpacas grumble that the lackeys keep robbing the place.

Culture: The path belongs to a staged role-play adventure for tourists, not a real conflict.

Atmosphere: A theatrical cave: painted stage props, cheerful 'villains' and a sense of play.

Dangers: Mock ambushes; the chest in the exchange summons an Eroding Avatar of Lava, a gameplay challenge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the path remains open as part of the attraction.

83.content:
Guiztli Ridge: Guiztli Ridge is a small island of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort, topped by a single rocky ridge. Beneath it lies Villa Guiztli, an underground town that offers a role-play adventure against a make-believe villain.

Its residents include a fruit farmer, a guard and a character named Achu.

Geography: A rock ridge on its own island. Visitors can see it from the Huha Hill lodgings. The caverns beneath hold Villa Guiztli, and Guiztli Path connects the villa to Castle Joquiratto.

In the story quest the Traveler rides a cruise ship through the cavern.

People: "Achupalla", the Fruit Farmer, "Willapi", the Guard, and Achu.

In To Guiztli Ridge! the Traveler works with Bennett, Chasca, Mualani and the Asha form of Macani, and meets characters named "El Capoctus Joquiratto" and "Nanasian".

Culture: Part of the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort story, in which a robbery in Villa Guiztli leads to a chase and a hunt for the culprits through the cavern, ending with the Traveler confronting the Nochtli ruffians.

History: Opened with the resort in 5.8.

Atmosphere: A rocky islet with a play-world below: quirky alpacas, capybaras and costumed villains.

Travel: The cavern below is entered from the ridge, and the quest has the Traveler ride a cruise ship through it.

Quests: To Guiztli Ridge! (part 2.2 of The World Is Your Canvas!).

Steps in the quest include following the sheriff to the bar, defeating the bandits, helping the sheriff activate a mechanism, then riding the cruise ship in pursuit of the Nochtli ruffians, finding a way to lift a barrier and investigating the cavern. The enemy labels are jokes, naming the culprits as Butch Churldy and Slushdance Kid.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ridge remains open as part of the resort.

84.content:
Hall of Parting Vows (also: Sacred Path Trial Ruins): The Hall of Parting Vows is an underground ruin in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, said to be where Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, and the Sage of the Stolen Flame swore a sacred oath. Players enter it during the world quest Revelations from the Past, seeking the token the Sage left.

Below it, glowing stairs lead down to Catastrophe's Edge, and an inscription there transports the player to the Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame. Its map has two levels, an entrance hall and the place of parting vows. A viewpoint inscription in the hall is titled Mural of Sworn Pledges.

Geography: Underground, with an entrance guarded by a barrier, corridors, a lava crossing and mechanisms. The ruin lies near the Children of Echoes in Tequemecan Valley.

History: Within the quest, Manqu explains from ancient tribal scrolls that the Sage believed humans could guide and lead Saurians to a better future than the age of the giant dragons. Feeling guilty for stealing phlogiston from dragonkind, the Sage hoped humans and Saurians could live as equals, and he left a token here; the scrolls say humans and Saurians each have their places.

The Sage of the Stolen Flame is the human legend of the dragon prince Kukulkan, who once formed an alliance with Xbalanque (the wiki describes it as aimed at preventing the Huitzilopochtli array's activation). The oath sworn here fits that alliance, but the sources read do not spell out its terms.

The trial reflects the Sage's design: the barrier opens only when a human and a Saurian stand in their respective positions, a test of understanding between the two. The reward, a Golden Entreaty, later becomes central to the plot at the Great Volcano of Tollan; Kukulkan, speaking as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, steered the rite for his own aims.

Dangers: Abyss-corroded Rockfond Rifthounds guard the entrance, and a corroded Golden Wolflord appears in the final fight at Catastrophe's Edge.

Quests: Revelations from the Past (world quest, Tequemecan Valley, chapter 'Between Pledge and Forgettance'), played with Manqu, Paimon, the Traveler and the Little One Saurian; the player has the Traveler only for part of it.

Atmosphere: Sealed, ceremonial and slow: ancient trial machinery, murals and glowing lava, built to be opened only by a pair who cooperate.

Status as of 7.1: Completed ruin as of 7.1; can be revisited after the quest, with the lower sites reachable by the glowing stairs.

85.comment: Hall of Parting Vows: Mural of Sworn Pledges
85.content: A mural viewpoint in the hall, which the wiki connects to Xiuhcoatl's defeat and to a black dragon through gallery images. The wiki gives no transcript.

86.content:
Heart of Force Inversion: The Heart of Force Inversion is a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan, filled with pools of liquid phlogiston that flow upwards into the sky. Abyssal corrosion clogs its waterfalls until the Traveler clears it.

The World Quest Where Once Force Was Reversed sends the Traveler and the Little One here to destroy Oozing Cores and solidify the waterfalls with a Coagulation Pearl, opening the way toward the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Geography: Liquid phlogiston cascades through channels and pools; one waterfall flows upwards towards the sky. Waterfalls of liquid phlogiston can be solidified into platforms and pillars, and corrosion has blocked some of the channels.

The final solidified pillar connects to the lava pool just north of the Sea of Shifting Sentience, one map layer higher, with a Pyroculus part-way up. In places a see-saw of stone slabs lowers one while raising another, and a Secret Source Servant is stranded until a Tepetlisaurus is indwelled to add weight.

People: Secret Source Servants appear, and the Little One digs one out. Pyro Abyss Mages first accost the Servants, and Oozing Cores pelt the party with mud from above.

The Little One and Paimon are the only named companions. Paimon is dismayed that the Abyss's influence has reached the Sacred Mountain.

Quests: Where Once Force Was Reversed (World Quest, part of In Search of a Hidden Heart) can start by progressing In Search of a Hidden Heart or by defeating the Pyro Abyss Mages. The Traveler destroys the Oozing Cores and follows the Little One as the Servants turn waterfalls solid. At the top a new waterfall flows up from the pool's centre and is solidified into a tall pillar with the Coagulation Pearl, revealing a Phlogiston Unit.

The quest awards a Luxurious, an Exquisite and a Common Chest, and a Phlogiston Unit. It is one of three companion quests with Where Once There Was a Calculation Array and Where Once There Were Arms Aplenty.

The quest's stated aim is to uncover a path to the Heart of the Sacred Mountain by cleansing the Abyss that is corrupting the ancient ruins. Completing it together with its two companions awards the achievement "Questioning the Heart of Flames".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area has been cleansed and is unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

87.comment: Heart of Force Inversion: Iridescent Legacy Part II
87.content: Found by destroying the Oozing Cores beneath a rock arch, this inscription holds the last words of the Seventh Lord, Aj Chojojik Kamikabal U'uk. He marvels at humans who keep coming though weak enough to fall to a single blow, even as their skin sloughs off corroding corpses and more of their kin rise to take their place. Mortally wounded, he asks whether the bright light in their eyes once shone in dragon eyes too, and tells Xiuhcoatl that was a time before they abandoned their glory.

key: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain
88.content:
Heart of the Sacred Mountain (also: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain, Sacred Mountain's Heart): The Heart of the Sacred Mountain is the innermost chamber of the Great Volcano of Tollan, far below the ruined Sacred City in Natlan. It holds the heart of the primal flame (Phlogiston) and the last legacy of the ancient dragons: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, a device made to burn Natlan into pure phlogiston and so destroy the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler and the saurian Little One reached it, and Little One chose not to run the machine. As of 7.1 it lies dormant and obsolete.

Entry requires both halves of the Golden Entreaty and a permit from the dragons' old records, and it is the destination of the Chronicler of the Crumbling City quest chapter. The Sage of the Stolen Flame, who stage-managed the journey, turns out to be the dragon Kukulkan.

Geography: The Heart lies under the Sacred City of Tollan, inside the volcano that dominates Atocpan. The way down is a fissure in the city centre that the dragon Xiuhcoatl excavated when he rebuilt the city, to give himself a stable place to experiment. A guardian Secret Source Dragon Idol seals the entrance and needs power from three Phlogiston Units. Inside, the story unfolds along a series of platforms, where Kukulkan recounts the history of the dragons, passes the dragons who gave up their bodies, and finally reaches the great array and its activation mechanism.

Kukulkan describes the place as the home of the blueprints of the old world, and as the spot where the first Pyro Sovereign was born from the primal flame and shaped Tollan and the first Dragonborn. Towers once spread over Natlan were meant to let the array cover the whole land; most were later smashed on Och-Kan's orders, though Kukulkan says their fragments serve the same purpose.

History: By Kukulkan's account, Xiuhcoatl was frozen in lava by the Heavenly Principles after their victory, and woke when the Dragon King Nibelung returned from beyond the sky. When the Heavenly Principles killed Nibelung, the Abyss-soaked Xiuhcoatl briefly regained clarity, saw how corrupted the world and his own mind had become, and spent his remaining lucid time building Huitzilopochtli. The device would turn Natlan into a land of only phlogiston, whose burning would be recorded and replicated, and the Abyss would be annihilated on contact. Kukulkan says every Dragonborn but himself accepted the plan; he walked away to look for another path.

Xiuhcoatl made one of his pupils the control hub of the array, which became his only weakness: Xbalanque exploited it to kill him, and both died, though Xbalanque was reborn as the first Pyro Archon. Xbalanque and Kukulkan then split the hub into two Golden Entreaties and swore that Huitzilopochtli would never be activated. Xbalanque's half passed to Och-Kan, who hid it on the Tonatiuh; Kukulkan hid his in the Hall of Parting Vows. Disappointed in the human tribes after Och-Kan's fall, Kukulkan lost his faith in humanity, spread rumours of the second Entreaty, and waited for someone to join the halves and carry them to the volcano; he says he deliberately sent a dragon (Little One) to walk beside a human.

The nameless servant says that sealing the city left the device itself with the deepest Abyssal corrosion, after which the city was taken over; Kukulkan adds that the dragons who had discarded their bodies to become phlogiston lifeforms were held in a dream-like state at great cost in resources. Kukulkan says that by the time of the Traveler's visit the city's reserves were nearly spent and the sleepers would die unless someone took authority over the primal flame.

Quests: The route is the two final parts of the Natlan wandering-saurian storyline. In Search of a Hidden Heart (Chronicler of the Crumbling City, part 2) sends the Traveler through the Sacred City: a nameless Secret Source Servant, a prototype built to help Xiuhcoatl keep records, explains that entry needs a permit from the Chamber of Deliberation and power for the guardian idol, obtained by clearing Abyssal corruption from several sites. An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (A Finale Emberforged) is the ending.

In the finale the two Golden Entreaties are offered at the central mechanism, and a golden voice (the Sage of the Stolen Flame) invites the Chosen of Dragons in. The Traveler fights the Primeval Source Dragon Mech, is caged by its laser, and Little One, forced to act alone, is guided by an unnamed voice into a temporary mature-dragon form. That voice is Kukulkan, who shows Little One the history of the array and asks it to activate Huitzilopochtli, requiring three rounds of confirmation. Little One, remembering the Traveler and Paimon, cancels, breaks the Traveler out, and the pair defeat the Mech together.

Kukulkan admits the removal of the Flamelord's Blessing was a lie of omission: the Blessing would have killed most saurians if mishandled, and he planned to use a human to open the volcano and bring back the second Entreaty. Little One answers his claim that Natlan's people will never forge their own defences with an explicit trust in humanity.

People: Kukulkan, the dragon behind the Sage of the Stolen Flame and the voice in the Secret Source Servants, appears here in many borrowed forms (including Manqu and Bona's shapes). A nameless Secret Source Servant, a prototype built for Xiuhcoatl's record-keeping, guards the way in. Little One, a young Tepetlisaurus that carried the Flamelord's Blessing, is the protagonist of the choice. Paimon and the Traveler are present throughout.
