Atmosphere: Vast, quiet and mechanical rather than infernal: white light, golden script appearing as words in the air, and a ceremonial voice that speaks of cleansing creation. The mood shifts between scholarly calm and growing pressure as Kukulkan warns that the energy reserves are running down.

Dangers: Abyssal corruption in the Sacred City above; the Secret Source Dragon Idol guardian; the Primeval Source Dragon Mech, with a laser cage and charged beam attacks; and the uncontrolled power of the Flamelord's Blessing if a saurian is unguided.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heart is dormant. Huitzilopochtli has not been activated and is obsolete; Little One keeps a dimmed mark and has returned to his small saurian size.

The Flamelord's Blessing is gone. The volcano did not erupt in response, only releasing a little smoke. Kukulkan and the phlogistonised dragons faded away, and Tollan's maintenance functions ended. No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here.

89.comment: Heart of the Sacred Mountain: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array
89.content:
Huitzilopochtli, also called the Sunquake or Sweeping Skyfire, was the dragons' final weapon, kept in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. It was built to turn all Natlan, and eventually the world, into phlogiston and matter made only of phlogiston. Everything burned would be transcribed and copied as phlogiston units, and the Abyss would be destroyed when astral assemblages from the primal flame attached to it. Dragons who gave up their bodies would become the rulers of the new world; ordinary life would die or be converted. It needs the two Golden Entreaties and three confirmations to start or stop.

Kukulkan calls phlogiston an atom on which information can be written, a kind of computronium shaped by Iridescent Inscriptions, which is why it can imitate any form. He says nobody can predict what it would do to the Traveler. The player is allowed to confirm activation; the wiki treats the resulting vision, of a single lonely consciousness in a white world, as a non-canonical branch.

90.comment: Heart of the Sacred Mountain: Golden Entreaties
90.content: The Golden Entreaties are two stone inscriptions that together form the control hub of Huitzilopochtli. They were created when Xbalanque and Kukulkan split the hub to guarantee the array would never run. One was kept by Och-Kan on the Tonatiuh (the legendary 'Jade of Return') and the other in the Hall of Parting Vows. Joined and offered in the Heart, they open the way to the array.

91.comment: Heart of the Sacred Mountain: Kukulkan in the Heart
91.content: Inside the Heart the Sage of the Stolen Flame reveals himself as Kukulkan, saying that 'Kukulkan' was his first name and Waxaklahun Ubah Kan only one of many he invented. He wore the forms of Manqu and Bona to explain things and calls himself Xiuhcoatl's younger brother and Och-Kan's father. He admits that his invented legends, the secret-servant voice and the trial path were all designed to bring a dragon to this room, and that he wanted the Dragonborn to choose the array freely and was still moved when it chose otherwise.

92.content:
Huha Hill: Huha Hill is the resort's lodging district: a cluster of villas and other places to stay, with rooftop pools, outdoor dining and a fine view of Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay. A loading screen calls it a great area for tourists and says its name comes from the 'hooh... hah...' sounds often heard nearby.

Souvenirs from other resort areas decorate it once certain quests are done.

Geography: A hill above the resort looking over the cliffs, the ridge and the bay. Tete Isle is another part of the resort.

The viewpoint is part of why the lodgings are popular.

Places: Villas and lodging, rooftop pools and outdoor dining areas.

Display items appear after quests: Starblooms from Colorfall Cliffs after To Colorfall Cliffs!, guests from Villa Guiztli with a Soothing Salve after To Guiztli Ridge!, a baby-koholasaurus wave machine from Wavey Bay after To Wavey Bay!, and a Joypop Bottle of Aphimead from Tete Isle after The Surprise That Awaits Us All!.

People: Tourists and resort staff.

The wave machine's text says Mualani in particular wants one for her own house.

Culture: Accommodation is expensive. According to Pumayna, some rooms cost 20,000 Mora per person per night, with fees for attractions elsewhere in the resort included.

Aphimead, the festive drink, can be brewed in many flavours, and the in-game text says the glass shared with friends is the one that you never forget.

The wiki notes that huha means thigh or flank in Maori, which it lists as the name's etymology, but the loading-screen explanation is the sounds nearby. The two accounts are not reconciled.

Atmosphere: Comfortable and relaxed: an upmarket stay with views of the cliffs, the ridge and the bay.

Quests: Hosts reward decorations unlocked by the Sunspray Summer Resort story quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Huha Hill is open as the resort's lodging area.

93.content:
Huitztli Hill (also: Smoke Ridge): Huitztli Hill is a mountain north of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames. Local tribespeople call it Smoke Ridge because magma streams from the Great Volcano of Tollan run beneath it and send smoke up through its valleys. It is too hot even for people used to Phlogiston, which may be why a reclusive Qucusaur lives there.

Huitztli is a Nahuatl word meaning 'thorn' or 'spine'.

Geography: A mountainside with valleys that smoke. The base of the southern cliff face is strewn with the bones of a huge, unknown creature.

It lies north of the Stadium, within the basin.

Places: Exploration features include a Coilgrass Sigil, an Everflame Seed, Flamegranate, Monetoo, Phlogiston Piles and Saurian Indwelling spots. A local specialty is brilliant chrysanthemum.

People: No settlement. The Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant is its notable resident.

The bone field at the cliff's base has no known origin.

Dangers: Extreme heat. Enemies are hilichurls, tepetlisauri, yumkasaurs and their whelps, Forged Sand fighters and Swiftstep couriers, plus the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant as the boss.

The full list of common enemies is Hilichurls (plain, shooter, fighter, wooden-shield guard, berserker, Pyro shooter), tepetlisauri, yumkasaurs and whelps, Forged Sand interrogators, javelineers and shieldbreakers, and Swiftstep armed couriers.

Travel: Found north of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hill is still smoking wilderness.

94.content:
Isle of Tozoz (also: Isle of Night, The Isle of Night): The Isle of Tozoz, also called the Isle of Night, is a small island in the northeastern corner of Ochkanatlan in Natlan. It was once guarded by people who watched over saurian hatchlings and is now a quiet ruin of mechanisms and logs.

The world quest The Lone Isle Named Night (5.2) begins when the player activates three switches and the main Ancient Inscribed Ring. In a hidden chamber the Traveler and Paimon find a guard's diary and a Saurian egg, which the guard had named Aguara and which becomes a companion.

Secret Source Sentinels still patrol, warning intruders to leave or be expelled by lethal force.

The wiki notes that the name echoes Tozoztli, a Nahuatl word for vigil. This is an etymology note, not stated in game.

Geography: A small island at the northeast edge of Ochkanatlan, with switches placed high up, a summit the player climbs and a hidden underground chamber.

People: An unnamed guard kept the island under Lord Milchi. The diary also mentions Lord Atlatl and warriors from Cinder City who attacked the island.

History: Maintenance logs show a lax, low-budget watch: security was repeatedly judged too weak, but the approving party ruled that intruders should merely be driven off rather than harmed. A newer guard complained that the Saurians ate better than the staff, citing Lord Och-Kan's view that they were enemies.

In the diary, messengers from Cinder City describe the island's creatures as pests whose contact brings sickness and personality change, and say Lord Milchi himself was transformed after meeting them. The guard rejects this, saying the Saurians are clean and that attackers kept trying to burn the island. Later entries mention orders to execute the little ones, rumours of tribal rebellions, and Lord Milchi freeing the hatchlings and staying to face Och-Kan.

In the last entry the guard writes that the egg could not be moved, hid it in the underground chamber and named it Aguara, while warriors searched the island and food ran out. A stone tablet at the island has its inscription partly chiselled away, and a damaged Sentinel reports failed initialisation.

Dangers: Secret Source Sentinels guard the island, and a Tenebrous Mimesis variant of an Iktomisaurus Warrior appears in the quest's combat step.

Quests: The Lone Isle Named Night belongs to the chapter In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons. Completing it unlocks an achievement and sends the Unhatched Saurian Egg to the Rest Area.

Atmosphere: Quiet and melancholy: tidy logs, grappling hooks and a hidden room that preserve one guard's worries long after the hatchlings left.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is abandoned, with Sentinels still active. No later developments were found.

95.comment: Isle of Tozoz: Isle of Tozoz Maintenance Logs
95.content: Logs and the diary on the island record a guard's complaints about budget, ladders and the lax care of the Saurians, as well as the officials' repeated order to avoid harming intruders. They are one guard's account and should be treated as partial.

96.content:
Land of Myriad Megaliths: The Land of Myriad Megaliths is a point of interest in the Sulfurous Veins area of Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. Its in-game viewpoint is titled Stone Chamber of Shifting Crystal Pillars.

The name and viewpoint title point to a stone chamber of crystal pillars. No lore, inhabitants or quest are documented for it in the sources read.

It first appeared with Natlan in version 5.0 and has a map level of its own.

No quest, character or text is tied to it in the sources read, so its origin and the cause of the shifting pillars stay unknown.

Geography: A chamber in the Sulfurous Veins section of Tequemecan Valley with its own map level.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

97.content:
Legendary Tonatiuh (also: Tonatiuh, Skyserpent Ship, Sky Serpent Ship, Legendary Skyserpent Ship): The Tonatiuh, also called the Skyserpent Ship, is a floating, dragon-built vessel high above the clouds over Ochkanatlan in Natlan. Legend made it Och-Kan's treasure ship, full of riches and containing a Jade of Return that could quell the Abyss, and adventurers chased it for generations. In fact it is a bleak, wind-scoured structure of islands and tangled lines, and the 'Jade' is a Golden Entreaty that Och-Kan hid there; Kukulkan invented the legend as a lure. As of 7.1 it is empty.

It is reached by placing Pyrophosphorite on the Altar of Primal Flame in Ochkanatlan, which raises a guiding wind. The ship is a spoiler-heavy location for the Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm quest chapter (5.2).

Geography: The Tonatiuh hangs above the sea of clouds over Ochkanatlan. From below it looks to Paimon like a vast ball of yarn or tangled snakes rather than a ship; on arrival it is a desolate scatter of floating islands and sand-covered structures, with Pyrophosphorite everywhere and an old mural on the north-western island. A mechanism like an Altar of Primal Flame stands on the ship; special flame-infused Pyrophosphorite ('Firestones') found around it activates the mechanism.

Gameplay note: before the quest chapter is finished the area can already be approached by characters able to gain great height through Nightsoul Transmission, and its name shows as '???' on approach.

History: According to the wiki's reading of An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty, the dragons built the ship, originally to anchor the sky-cable ('stairway') that was to climb from Chichen Uctokah into space beyond Teyvat. Och-Kan, who took Ochkanatlan, turned it on its side and used it to hide a Golden Entreaty, one half of the control hub for Huitzilopochtli. Over the years countless adventurers from Natlan went looking for the ship, and none proved it existed. Bona's father Taika, with Copan, Titu and Legba, set out on the same search and never returned; the one survivor of that squad, a young mystic called Liriwu, came back from the city alone.

In Och-Kan's memories Taika's group, the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team, hopes the Jade of Return can quell the Abyss, and is later shown to have fallen victim to the trap. The trap was the work of the Sage of the Stolen Flame, Kukulkan, who made the legend part of an 'experiment'. Years later Bona reached the Tonatiuh herself with Cocouik, saw through the legend, and set out to break the trap.

Kukulkan says he donned masks, collecting the souls his son Och-Kan devoured, to test how humans respond to a legend. In Och-Kan's memory Kukulkan presses him to join the Golden Entreaties and activate Huitzilopochtli; Och-Kan answers that the Entreaty is no longer where Kukulkan expects it, and Kukulkan guesses he left it on his 'toy ship'.

Quests: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (Act II: A Dream of Gazing Upon the Distant Sky; Act III: The Tonatiuh Quivers). In To the Sky-Road, the Traveler, Paimon, Little One, Bona and Cocouik offer two chunks of Pyrophosphorite on the Altar and fly up. In The Other Side of the Sky they use Firestones to open a sealed rock and take out the 'Jade of Return', which turns out to be a Golden Entreaty; Bona becomes agitated and tries to warn them of a trap before the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash seizes it.

The Traveler learns the nature of the trap in Och-Kan's memories (Moment of Awakening) and later takes both Entreaties to the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. After the chapter, Bona's goggles and woven notes can be found on the north-western floating island.

Atmosphere: Silence, wind and altitude: a lonely, sand-strewn structure among clouds, with the 'desolate' feel of a place that once held a mastermind's dream. A nameless adventurer's notes say it is nothing like they imagined, and that they could understand what the Python King felt at the end.

Dangers: Falling from the floating islands; the lingering trap, now destroyed; and, in the story, the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, which snatches the Entreaty from those who take it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tonatiuh is empty and quiet. The trap set there by the Sage of the Stolen Flame has been destroyed, and the Golden Entreaty has been recovered by the Traveler.

The goggles left behind are the only testament to the adventurer who fought the maker of the trap, and an achievement awards the interaction. No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here.

98.comment: Legendary Tonatiuh: The Jade of Return legend
98.content: The Jade of Return is said to be a treasure aboard the Tonatiuh that would 'cleanse filth' and quiet the Abyss in Natlan. Many adventurers, including Bona's father, died or vanished looking for it. It is a fiction: the object is the Golden Entreaty that Kukulkan tells the Traveler he made into a legend, calling it a trap for the 'lions of Natlan', and the inscriptions on it say it is hazardous and should not be touched.

99.comment: Legendary Tonatiuh: A Nameless Adventurer's Notes
99.content: A woven-scroll diary appears in pieces across Ochkanatlan and ends on the Tonatiuh. Its author describes awakening a dragonspirit from the heart of a machine and naming it Cocouik for its turquoise-green colour, following Aunt Liriwu's markings to the Altar, noticing that the legend of the Jade conceals the machine that could save Natlan, and resolving to deny the Sage's plan. Goggles beside it testify that she once existed.

100.content:
Leisurely Puffer: A watersports shop in Toyac Springs, in the People of the Springs' area of Natlan, owned by the family of the surfer Mualani.

It sells a wide range of gear, from swimsuits to waterskis, and its custom surfboards are said to be especially popular. A message board stands at the shop.

Places: The shop sits in the Toyac Springs area under the People of the Springs' name on the map. Its Leisurely Puffer Message Board is the shop's interactable.

People: Ownership by Mualani's family comes from the quest Home of the Hot Springs. For Mualani herself see her own entry; the shop's other staff are not named in the sources read.

Culture: The prize for the planned First All-Tribe Surfing Championship is currently kept at the shop, which hints that it may host or sponsor the event. This is the wiki's inference, not a stated fact.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

Nothing in the sources read changes the shop's status after its introduction in 5.0.

101.content:
Malinalco Grotto: Malinalco Grotto is an underground cavern in Quahuacan Cliff, Natlan. It contains a mural depicting the legend of Kuntur and Rumi, and is reached by taking the right-hand tunnel at the entrance of the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave.

Notes found there suggest the mural is being repaired by people who use paints produced on the spot. Two viewpoints are named Cavern of Tranquil Light and The Story Recorded. Hued Monetoo and Brilliant Chrysanthemum can be found in the cave.

The notes ask whether the story could really end with three tribal warriors defeated by Rumi the wicked sorcerer, and wonder whether another mural showing Kuntur lies elsewhere and whether its path has been buried or needs a mechanism.

The wiki's etymology note says the name echoes Malinalco in Mexico; this is a real-world reference, not an in-game statement.

Places: The cavern has several levels and the wiki names the area the Cavern of the Legendary Mural.

Culture: The notes treat creating murals near where paint is produced as a good idea, since missing colour can be refilled with material gathered on the spot.

Dangers: The tunnel lies beside the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grotto remains accessible. No later developments were found.

102.comment: Malinalco Grotto: Kuntur and Rumi mural
102.content: The grotto's mural depicts the legend of Kuntur and Rumi, with Rumi called a wicked sorcerer in the restorers' notes. For the tale itself, see the item The Tale of Kuntur.

103.content:
Manse of Monetoo Murals: The Manse of Monetoo Murals is a point of interest on Teticpac Peak in Coatepec Mountain, Natlan. Its viewpoint is titled Where the Painted Realm Unfolds.

The name and viewpoint suggest a building with murals, but no inhabitants, history or quest are documented for it in the sources read.

It was added with Natlan in version 5.0 and has a map level of its own.

No quest, character or text is tied to it in the sources read, so who built the manse and what the murals show stay unknown.

Geography: Located on Teticpac Peak in the Coatepec Mountain area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

104.content:
Mare Jivari (also: Silent Sea of Ashes, Ashen Sea): The Mare Jivari ('Silent Sea of Ashes') was a region at the far west of Tenochtzitoc in Natlan, once a sea of fire and now described as an endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow. It earned its name in a great battle of the cataclysm, when Tenoch and Sanhaj Kompore destroyed the Bakunawa there. Barbatos later blew it off the timeline, so it is cut off from the world.

Since version 5.8 a small corner is reachable through the Pyro Archon Temple, as a restricted story-mode area in which the Bakunawa can be fought. The rest is promised for later versions. As of 7.1 no further expansion is recorded on the pages read.

Geography: The westernmost part of Tenochtzitoc (now the Easybreeze Holiday Resort area). Loading text calls it an endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow. The playable portion is reached by touching the central structure in the Pyro Archon Temple and entering a portal in a Night Kingdom-like area, and is affected by Smoldering Ashes; it can be left only through the portal that appears when the Bakunawa is defeated, or by exiting the story mode.

An ancient shield near the Bakunawa's arena carries fading etchings about faint outlines of structures in the distance, familiar shapes and a plea to remember everything that happened.

People: No living inhabitants. Souls of people who died there, local Monetoo, and Abyssal monsters remain. Traces of earlier visitors include the Mondstadt adventurer Stanley and Tecpatl's Flintblades.

Because of the temporal disruption, the souls of those who perished there were bound to the land, and foreign souls could not return home. Some of these souls merged with Monetoo; about twenty years ago Asha began to be sighted around Tenochtzitoc.

History: Legend says a phoenix lived in the sea of fire, worshipped as a totem and read by kings as a sign of nobility. A sage, the Lavawalker, made a circlet that could withstand the flames; his teacher and peers called this blasphemy and ordered him in, and he survived, wandering in and out for another hundred years until the fire burned him to ash. About a thousand years ago the Wanderer's Troupe came here while performing for foes, and its flautist met the Bakunawa, from which the troupe carved the Runestone.

In the cataclysm the Abyss invaded Natlan and the Bakunawa, west of Tenochtzitoc, devoured entire villages. The settlement of Tenochtzitoc fought it until only Tenoch remained. He rallied the quarrelling tribes against the black tide and gathered six allies, forming the coalition, and began a campaign at the Mare Jivari. Legend says Sanhaj, a Border Master of the Masters of the Night-Wind, summoned a miniature Night Kingdom to destroy the calamity. In reality he engraved phlogiston onto Tenoch's body, Tenoch let the Bakunawa swallow him, and when Sanhaj triggered the array the clash of the Abyss, the Lord of the Night and Tenoch's spirit fractured the Bakunawa into countless pieces, killing both men.

The Bakunawa could still be revived and its power could corrupt the passage of time, so Barbatos, before his long hibernation, blew the entire Mare Jivari off the timeline to stop Abyssal corruption spreading. This explains why the region was created 500 years ago yet recorded for a thousand. Twenty to thirty years before the story, travellers reported a mountain-sized dark creature roaming it, after which the whole region vanished; settlement then increased around it, and the Easybreeze Holiday Resort was set up soon after the Night Warden Wars. Stanley of Mondstadt crossed it with a novice, Hans Archibald, and was killed protecting him; Hans took the name Stanley to keep the man's tales alive. The infant Bennett survived an Abyssal ambush on Tecpatl's Flintblades there.

Dangers: The Bakunawa, a huge permeated body with Anemo, Cryo and Geo attacks that ignores dash i-frames; Abyssal monsters in the simulated version; and smouldering ash. Many adventurers who tried to prove themselves here fell. After a defeat the Bakunawa is sealed only temporarily.

Quests: In the Sunspray Summer Resort event (limited-time) Mavuika and Barbatos (now Venti) open a rift between an Abyssal simulation of the Mare Jivari and the real one so that Venti can guide lost Mondstadter souls home; Bennett is targeted by the Abyss for escaping as an infant. In The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc the Traveler, Paimon and Citlali stop Enjou and enter the restricted real area, where they restrain the Bakunawa's permeation. Enjou then goes into the true Mare Jivari, which cannot be entered without the Bakunawa's power, looking for a forgotten homeland.

Atmosphere: Grey, windless, silent: a plain of ash under a stilled timeline, with the faint outlines of vanished structures at the edge of sight.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, a small area is open and the rest of the true Mare Jivari remains unexplored. Nahida calls it one of the places beyond her reach, implying Irminsul keeps no record of it.

105.content: A vast Abyssal calamity of the cataclysm era that devoured villages west of Tenochtzitoc. Its body was fractured by Tenoch, Sanhaj and the Night Kingdom's power, yet it keeps the potential to revive and to corrupt time. The Wanderer's Troupe had earlier carved a Runestone from its body, according to the account in The Festering Fang.

106.comment: Mare Jivari: Enjou and the Mare Jivari
106.content: Enjou researches the region's history and access routes. In Yupanqui's Turnfire he meets Kinich and the Traveler; in the Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls event (limited-time) he uses Leyla as bait to make Citlali work out its location. In The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc he pacts with Citlali, helps restrain the Bakunawa, and then goes into the true Mare Jivari, because none of the civilisations he had learned about was the forgotten homeland he sought.

107.content:
Mother Flamegranate Tree: The Mother Flamegranate Tree is a great tree in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, and the source of the Scions of the Canopy tribe's Flamegranates. Its roots, in a cave warmed by lava, grow the Mountain King Flamegranates.

Only Scions of the Canopy holding a special entry pass, the Green-Edged Paper Slip, may enter the root cave. Each pass bears its holder's name and cannot be traded. Tisoc has long served as guard at the cave entrance.

The tree bears two special kinds of fruit: larger Flamegranates on the cliffside, and the Mountain King Flamegranates near the roots. The latter are named for the Mountain King, Kongamato, to whom they are offered.

Before the world quest Ripe For Trouble the tree and its fruit are blue and unripe; afterwards they are orange and ripe.

Geography: A tree on a cliff in Tequemecan Valley, with a cave of roots below. The roots have three map levels: a cool damp cave (before the quest), a warm cave (after it) and a geothermal surge.

The roots' special fibres thrive when immersed in Liquid Phlogiston rather than burning. That contact is needed for the fruit to mature and acquire its Phlogiston content.

People: Tisoc, the cave guard, calls himself an excellent one. The tribe guards the tree because it supplies its Flamegranates.

Culture: Flamegranate skins can be dried to make bags, such as those carried by couriers. Mountain King Flamegranates are an offering to Kongamato.

Quests: Ripe For Trouble (5.0): the Traveler and Paimon enter the cavern to find Tisoc, who has gone missing, explore the roots, break solidified magma and raise the Liquid Phlogiston levels, then flee before speaking to Tisoc again.

Dangers: Lava and solidified magma fill the root cave.

Atmosphere: Hot, orange and carefully guarded: a tree whose fruit is a tribal treasure.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tree is ripe and still guarded by the Scions of the Canopy. No later changes were found.

108.content:
Muhuru's Gemporium: A gem shop in the Children of Echoes' settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, run by Cheven.

Cheven's apprentice is Imix, and the NPC Iknal is also listed there. The shop sells gems and similar goods; the in-game vendor is Imix.

People: Cheven is the owner and Imix the apprentice. Iknal is listed at the shop without a stated role.

Culture: Muhuru was also the name of a stegosaur Saurian, the companion of the Nanatzcayan hero Sundjatta. Weapon text says it fought alongside Sundjatta and the other heroes led by Tenoch against the Abyss. Stegosaurs are no longer found in Natlan today. The wiki connects the shop's name to this figure, but no text explains the choice of name.

The furnishing Tequemecan Treasures is designed to resemble the shop.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

109.content:
Natlan (also: Nation of War, Land of Saurians): Natlan is the nation of Pyro and of war in western Teyvat, beyond Sumeru's desert, a hot land of volcanoes, canyons, mesas and hot springs. Its people are the Natlanese, organised into six tribes, each bonded with one kind of Saurian, the evolved descendants of Natlan's ancient dragons. The Pyro Archon and God of War, currently Mavuika, is unlike other Archons: every Pyro Archon is a mortal human who won the throne through battle. For 500 years Natlan fought an unending war against the Abyss, until it was won in Archon Quest Chapter V.

Its heart is the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, where the ever-burning Sacred Flame stands; under Natlan lies the Night Kingdom, a realm of ancestral spirits (the Wayob) and the dead that serves as the nation's ley lines. Prized titles called Ancient Names, inherited through the generations, carry the deeds of past heroes.

Geography: Natlan lies west of the Great Red Sand, past the Desert of Hadramaveth. It is hot and volcanic, with canyons, mesas and hot springs. Each of the six tribes holds its own territory (Tequemecan Valley, Coatepec Mountain, Toyac Springs, Quahuacan Cliff, the Tezcatepetonco Range and Atocpan under the Great Volcano of Tollan) around the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames.

Further areas: the ruined Eternal Empire of Ochkanatlan, the Ancient Sacred Mountain (whose interior holds Abyss-like dark mud), and Easybreeze Holiday Resort, an island off the westernmost edge of Natlan once called Tenochtzitoc, "where the war had begun and met its end". The Great Volcano of Tollan erupts periodically, raining fireballs over Atocpan. Saurian species hold their own territories, whose borders largely define the tribal lands. Phlogiston occurs naturally as crystals, rivers of liquid and hot gas, and Pale Mist drains the colour from some areas.

Government: The Pyro Archon leads Natlan from the Speaker's Chamber at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame; each tribe has its own chief.

By ancient tradition the six chiefs gather by the flame in the Speaker's Chamber at regular intervals and negotiate openly under the Archon's eye; the Chamber coordinates the Stadium's and the tribes' affairs and also appears to act as Natlan's highest court.

Pyro Archons bear the divine name Haborym. Xbalanque, the first, borrowed the power of Ronova, the Ruler of Death, to set the rules by which ordinary people can rise to the throne; traditionally the Pilgrimage was also how the Natlanese chose their Archon, judging battle the truest test. A new Archon's "inner flame" awakens and the Sacred Flame grants them knowledge and memories of the land. Pyro Archons age and die like anyone else, so Natlan has had many. In formal settings Mavuika is a stern ruler; in private she is a friendly, big-sister figure who parties at the Weary Inn on the eve of a Pilgrimage.

Known Pyro Archons: Xbalanque (about 2,000 years ago; an outlander with no tribe); the unnamed scarlet-eyed youth of the Flower-Feather Clan who overthrew Och-Kan and later asked that his name be erased from history; an unnamed female Archon of the Muratans, acquainted with Venti and reigning more than 1,600 years ago, who held martial tournaments between the tribes; Ndenge and Xumucul (known only as Archons Gosoythoth imitated); Cochanina of the People of the Springs, who drove the "Volcano Lord" from their land, and Gloharry, Shulevitz and Isaja, who worked to contain the Bakunawa in the Mare Jivari; and Mavuika of the Scions of the Canopy, who reigned during the cataclysm and reigns again today. According to a note by the first Cryo Archon, the Heavenly Principles had fated the half-dragon Och-Kan to rule Natlan, and Xbalanque's seizure of that destiny was the culmination of millennia of rebellion against Celestia.

Religion: The tribes revere their ancestors and the Wayob: formless spirits, "will without form or thought", that dwell in the Night Kingdom, see past and future, protect their tribe and choose who receives Ancient Names. The dead go to the Night Kingdom, slowly merge into its sea of souls and are eventually reborn in Natlan in another form. Warriors draw power from these souls, the Nightsouls (Nightsoul's Blessing). The Sacred Flame, also called K'ahk', is the conduit to the Night Kingdom and the foundation of Natlan's defence.

A tribe's Wayob is believed to speak through its chief's dreams, and the Wayob can manifest in Natlan through obsidian totems and Nightsouls. The Night Kingdom was built about 6,000 years ago by Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, from fragments of the ley lines shattered in the war of funerary flame, under Ronova's guidance; Xbalanque later strengthened it. Because it is not like ley lines elsewhere, it records only Natlanese deeds and long refused foreign souls; since the war ended and Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night, it accepts people from other nations. The Masters of the Night-Wind are the tribe closest to it: their shamans commune with the Wayob, watch the ley lines and Phlogiston, and weave scrolls recording major events.

Culture: The official description calls Natlan "the nation of oaths"; it prizes strength and competition, and "war" is part of everyday life. Visitors describe the Natlanese as energetic people whose "souls are forged for battle from birth", fond of graffiti, music, dancing and showing off. Warriors dress in imitation of their Saurian partners, whom people treat as family. Until the war ended, Natlanese could not safely leave the nation: outside its borders the Wayob's protection weakened and leavers suffered memory loss and emotional problems, so a chief had to seek the Wayob's approval before anyone departed.

Economy: Because its people could not leave, Natlan's economy was long closed, and tourism was effectively its only export. Each tribe has a niche: the Children of Echoes mine, smith and appraise gems, are Natlan's only source of ritual obsidian, and train the Name Engravers who forge Ancient Names; the People of the Springs live from hot-spring tourism; the Scions of the Canopy take delivery and hunting commissions and host extreme sports; the Masters of the Night-Wind offer fortune-telling, blessings of tools and weapons, and artisan goods believed to carry special effects; the Collective of Plenty grows Natlan's best produce on volcanic soil and shares the surplus with other tribes; the Flower-Feather Clan is known for elite warriors and the saurian vet Ifa. The Pyro Archon pays for free food and lodging at the Weary Inn for Pilgrimage contestants and their families.

Natlanese ores are all associated with Phlogiston; Vennessa already praised their quality over Mondstadt's. Varesa's family orchard has sold produce abroad to Escoffier in Fontaine and Dori in Sumeru. Inazuma's fondness for Natlan's hot springs led it to commission Snezhnayan boilers to build artificial ones at home.

History: Before humans ruled, Natlan was Natlantea, a dragon civilisation under Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, and the artificial Thirteen Sovereign Lords. About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque slew Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon; the tribes then founded the Eternal Empire of Ochkanatlan under Kukulkan's half-dragon son Och-Kan, who became a tyrant until a scarlet-eyed youth, the second Pyro Archon, overthrew him. Five hundred years ago the Abyss struck Natlan harder than any other nation. The exiled warrior Tenoch and six heroes, one per tribe, fought beside the newly ascended Mavuika and drove it back, but it rooted itself in the Night Kingdom.

Natlan took no part in the Archon War, as the dragons were fighting each other, and the dragon Kukulkan gave humans Phlogiston to revive their civilisation. Mavuika's plan: the tribes would rebuild for 500 years, the Wayob would then each choose a hero bearing one of the six heroic Ancient Names, and with them the Archon would drive the Abyss out for good. To lead it in person she placed her life in the Sacred Flame and woke again in the present; she refused every suggestion to use the Pyro Gnosis, which would have rewritten the ley lines and erased Natlan's history and culture. Her sister Hine helped rebuild the Scions of the Canopy. Soon after the cataclysm the Khaenri'ahn knight Thrain, later the Fatui Harbinger Capitano, fled to Natlan with his platoon and fought the Abyss alongside the tribes. Over the centuries the Abyss corrupted the Wayob, so when the Traveler arrived only three heroes (Kinich, Iansan, Xilonen) had been acknowledged.

Earlier, a civil war split a seventh tribe: one branch, the Muratans, wandered abroad and settled in Mondstadt (Vennessa was one of them); the rest were confined to Tenochtzitoc. In the cataclysm Rhinedottir's Bakunawa killed all of Tenochtzitoc but the exiled Tenoch, and several Archons spent themselves containing it in what became the Mare Jivari. Among the heroes, Burkina was slain by his Abyss-tainted Yumkasaur Kongamato, Sanhaj and Tenoch died detonating a miniature Night Kingdom at the Mare Jivari, Menilek and Sundjatta fell in the final battle, and Tupac carried the unconscious Mavuika to the Stadium for her sacrifice and died on his feet. Beneath the Children of Echoes, Traore and two Khaenri'ahn warriors pinned an Abyssal invasion underground with the Shadow Pins. After the cataclysm an adventure team led by Taika, and later his daughter Bona, sought the Legendary Tonatiuh at Ochkanatlan and were lured to their deaths by Kukulkan.

Foreign relations: Mondstadt: Vennessa, founder of the Knights of Favonius, descended from Natlan's exiled Muratans, and Bennett, born in Natlan and carried to Mondstadt as a baby, owes his chronic bad luck to being cut off from Natlan's ley lines. Snezhnaya: Capitano came to take the Pyro Gnosis around 3.1, and his subordinates captured Saurians for Phlogiston experiments; he ended as one of Natlan's honoured heroes. Inazuma: Natlan's hot springs inspired artificial ones there. Sumeru: in 6.6 Mavuika gave the Pyro Gnosis to Nahida through the Traveler, and Nahida later visited Natlan to thank her. Khaenri'ah: its refugees fought for Natlan after the cataclysm, and the Traveler's sibling wove New Khaenri'ah's ley lines over Natlan. Nod-Krai: visitors from Nod-Krai reached Natlan in 5.8, and in the 6.0 prelude the automaton Ineffa washed ashore there.

Natlan was the last nation to have any of its people appear in-game: before 5.0 it was known only through foreigners such as Inazuman bathhouse keepers, a Fontainian sailor who hoped to settle there, and a Sumeru merchant who called it "colorful, contradictory and charming". The sailor feared its many tribes and rules would make it hard to fit in.

Festivals: The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame is Natlan's great national contest; since the war it has been an athletic competition, whose first winner was Kinich. The Scions of the Canopy hold an annual Turnfire Night using small flames split from the Sacred Flame.

Dangers: Liquid and gaseous Phlogiston scald and burn, unstable Phlogiston crystals explode, and the Great Volcano of Tollan hurls fireballs. Secret Source automatons and dragon cannons still guard ancient ruins and went haywire in 6.0. Abyss Order cells struck every tribe in 5.7. Ochkanatlan was long a cursed, Abyss-infested ruin under Flower-Feather Clan blockade, and those who slipped past the patrols died there. Wild Saurians, tribal warrior bosses and survivors of Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome are reminders of the war.

Atmosphere: Blazing sun, red rock and volcanic haze; huge graffiti murals and hip, colourful street style; Saurians everywhere, from small whelps riding on shoulders to towering Tatankasaurs; hot springs and surf on the coast, dance-offs and drills in the mining gorge, balloon platforms on the cliffs, and a roaring crowd at the Stadium whose flame can be seen from far off. The Weary Inn is the place to celebrate.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Natlan is at peace. The Abyss was purged from the Night Kingdom in 5.3 and the Night Warden Wars are over. Mavuika lives and still rules, because Capitano took her fated death upon himself. Natlanese may now leave the nation without harm, though they still need their chief's permission. Natlan no longer has its Pyro Gnosis.

Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night, making her undying so she can keep repairing the ley lines; his body sits dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire atop Ochkanatlan. The Pilgrimage is now a sports competition. In 6.6 Mavuika gave the Pyro Gnosis away for good to help burn the corrupted Irminsul, and it vanished. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1). At its close, after Ronova destroyed a Celestial Nail in Snezhnaya with Eitr, the other Nails began emitting pillars of light, including the one near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, right beside where people live. Mavuika, who blames the Heavenly Principles for most of Natlan's past disasters, is warning the population to watch for danger; what the phenomenon means is not yet known.

Capitano is commemorated on a monument to the fallen near the Masters of the Night-Wind. In 7.1 the Traveler tells Anastasya that, according to Mavuika, the Gnosis has returned to the ley lines; Nahida earlier said no trace of its destruction was found. In 7.0 Pierro revealed Capitano's will, which gave most of his subordinates and all his key personnel to Tartaglia, along with his seat as a councillor of the Snezhnograd Veche.

110.comment: Natlan: Bloomflower Trials (Tournament of Glory in Bloom)
110.content: During the limited-time 5.5 event Tournament of Glory in Bloom, held in a peaceful Natlan after the war, the six tribes competed in friendly war games, the Bloomflower Trials, testing attack and defence.

key: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
111.comment: Natlan: The Pilgrimage and the Night Warden Wars
111.content:
Every tribe fields warriors who fight alongside their Saurians, and the Flower-Feather Clan's Qucusaur Riders once patrolled all of Natlan. Until the war ended, the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame chose the strongest Ancient Name bearers to fight the Abyss in the Night Kingdom in the Night Warden Wars; fallen bearers could be revived by the Ode of Resurrection if at least one teammate came back victorious.

The Pilgrimage was a two-phase tournament at the Stadium: teams, usually led by a bearer, were dropped by balloon around the country to fight for Contending Sparks, then winners fought one-on-one. Battles between Natlanese produce Contending Fire, the only fuel for the Sacred Flame, so outlanders could not compete. If a whole team fell, its members stayed lost and their Ancient Names were forgotten: "the victors shall burn bright, while the losers must turn to ash". Since the war, the Pilgrimage is a purely athletic contest open to outsiders.

112.comment: Natlan: Natlanese Daily Life and Technology
112.content:
Grainfruit is the staple food (in tatacos and soups); cacahuatl, bitter and complex, flavours sweets and drinks, and Embercore Flower nectar, sweet with a burning aftertaste, is popular. Food is hearty, heavy on starch and meat. In the Collective of Plenty, masked wrestlers keep a tradition that the loser of a duel between two masked fighters must unmask. Natlanese boxers train by "shadow boxing", which an Inazuman visitor carried home. Since the Abyss was purged, Natlanese can travel abroad without harm, but they still need their chief's permission.

Technology builds on the dragons' "Secret Source": Phlogiston engravings imitate the dragons' iridescent inscriptions to store information and create Spiritways. Phlogiston-powered vehicles are rare and almost all built by Xilonen (Kachina's drill, Chasca's flying cannon, Mavuika's motorcycle, the Flamestrider); the Phlogiston Wings jetpack was designed by Tepal, who died testing it, and finished by his mother Allpa. The Flower-Feather Clan keeps platforms aloft on hot-air balloons, and the People of the Springs press music records that also play on Fontainian players.

113.content:
Six major tribes have existed since Och-Kan's era. Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan, Tequemecan Valley): miners, excavators and gem appraisers, Geo, bonded with Tepetlisaurs. Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan, Coatepec Mountain): couriers, hunters and explorers, Dendro, Yumkasaurs; Mavuika's birth tribe. People of the Springs (Meztli, Toyac Springs): guides and hot-spring keepers, Hydro, Koholasaurs. Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan, Quahuacan Cliff): rangers and riders, Pyro, Qucusaurs. Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan, Tezcatepetonco Range): shamans who monitor ley lines and Phlogiston, Cryo, Iktomisaurs. Collective of Plenty (Teteocan, Atocpan): farmers, bodybuilders and wrestlers, Electro, Tatankasaurs. Current chiefs: Pacal (Children of Echoes), Wayna (Scions), Amina (People of the Springs), Mutota (Flower-Feather), Biram (Night-Wind) and Acatl (Collective of Plenty).

Each tribe's Wayob can manifest as a guardian spirit. The Children of Echoes and Collective of Plenty were founded by the twins Ixquieh and Ahpub; the Flower-Feather Clan by Lianca; the Masters of the Night-Wind by the Priest-King Maghan. A defunct seventh tribe of Anemo warriors split after a civil war into the wandering Muratans and the Tenochtzitoc, who all but perished in the cataclysm.

114.content:
Saurians are Natlan's dragons: Pyro vishaps that, after the Heavenly Principles cast down nails against Natlan's Phlogiston-rich soil, adapted by losing their intelligence (a "devolution" in the eyes of old dragons such as Kukulkan and Och-Kan). They now live closely with humans, choose their own partners and cannot speak human language, though tribe members read their moods. Phlogiston is an advanced form of Pyro, a programmable matter once used by the dragons, that powers Nightsoul's Blessing, Saurian abilities and Natlanese devices, and symbolises the people's indomitable spirit. Ancient dragon "Secret Source" machines still dot the land.

Yumkasaurs normally live under a century, and Kongamato's far longer life is blamed on Abyssal contamination; the Iktomisaur Elder Tlapo has lived for several centuries. Qucusaurs refuse riders who show the slightest hesitation. Cacucu, Ifa's Qucusaur, is the only Saurian able to say a few human phrases.

115.comment: Natlan: Ancient Names and the Heroes of Natlan
115.content:
An Ancient Name (tocaitl) is a title embodying a virtue and an obsidian stone engraved with it, carrying the deeds of all its past bearers. The Wayob grant them to tribe members whose lives exemplify the Name; the Pyro Archon can also commission a new one, forged by a Name Engraver at the cost of part of their lifespan. Six Names belong to the Heroes of Natlan, first borne by Xbalanque's companions and then by Tenoch's six during the cataclysm. The modern heroes: Xilonen (Baraka), Kinich (Malipo), Mualani (Umoja), Chasca (Vuka), Ororon (Bidii) and Iansan (Uwezo). The Traveler is the first outlander to hold one, Tumaini, chosen by the Lord of the Night and forged by Xilonen.

Past bearers: Baraka – Ixquieh, Sundjatta; Malipo – Yupanqui, Burkina; Umoja – Uenuku, Tupac; Vuka – Lianca, Menilek; Bidii – Maghan, Sanhaj; Uwezo – Ahpub, Wanjiru. A newly acknowledged hero receives the memories of the cataclysm-era bearer. Mavuika, Tenoch, Capitano and the Traveler with Paimon are also counted among the Heroes of Natlan. Kachina bears Uthabiti and Citlali Ukumbuko. Mavuika's Ancient Name is Kiongozi ("leader"); the wiki infers that all Pyro Archons share it. Tenoch lost his Ancient Name while still alive, probably because he was an exile.

116.content:
Xiuhcoatl, born from the primal flame, split off part of it to create his brother Kukulkan, carved the Sacred City of Tollan inside the Great Volcano, and made the Thirteen Sovereign Lords to govern Natlantea. The Heavenly Principles stole his Pyro authority and left him in a false death. As Natlantea declined, Kukulkan secretly gave humans Phlogiston and fathered the half-dragon Och-Kan to unite both peoples. About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque, an outsider who had forced the warring tribes into peace and was crowned by the Lord of the Night, stormed Tollan and slew Xiuhcoatl; the Three Princes and ten of the Lords also died. Xbalanque and Kukulkan each took one of Xiuhcoatl's eyes as an oath of peace. Xbalanque's followers founded Ochkanatlan on the ruins of the Ninth Lord's realm, and when Xbalanque "entered the Sacred Flame" the seven tribes put their authority in Och-Kan's hands as the Grand Alliance.

Och-Kan betrayed Xbalanque's commandments: he tried to exterminate dragons and Saurians, mistreated his people, banned worship of the ancestors and the Night Kingdom, and imprisoned the Ninth Lord Ixlel to power his city. The scarlet-eyed youth, banished for protecting Saurians, became the second Pyro Archon and overthrew him. Och-Kan survived split into a mind sealed in the Core of Chu'ulel and a body that became the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash; sovereignty returned to the tribes, who reconnected with the Night Kingdom and mended ties with the Saurians. Ochkanatlan became a cursed ruin. In 5.2 the Traveler met Och-Kan's mind ("Cocouik"), defeated his reunited self and freed Ixlel's spirit.

117.comment: Natlan: The Night Kingdom and the Lord of the Night
117.content:
The Night Kingdom is a realm deep underground, "a liminal space between body and mind, life and death", that functions as Natlan's ley lines. The Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, built it about 6,000 years ago under Ronova's guidance and slumbered until Capitano and Ororon's attempt to rewrite the ley lines with a Source Mechanism woke her in 5.1. When the Abyss struck in the cataclysm it rooted itself in the Night Kingdom; over five centuries the Wayob wore themselves down fighting it, and by the Traveler's arrival Mavuika estimated the realm would fall within a year.

After the war the Lord of the Night returned to the Night Kingdom to maintain the ley lines, made undying by Capitano's sacrifice. The Weaver of Secrets, one of the Sovereign Lords, merged her consciousness into the realm to create a "dream labyrinth" where dead dragons and humans find peace.

118.content:
In 5.0 Kachina fell in a victorious Night Warden War but the Ode of Resurrection failed to bring her back, because the Abyss had corrupted the Wayob. The Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan pulled her out of the Night Kingdom, and Mavuika burned the keepsakes her people had given her over the centuries, each holding Contending Fire, to rescue them. Mualani, then Ororon, then Chasca (after her adoptive sister Chuychu died of Abyssal contamination during a nationwide invasion) were acknowledged as heroes. With all six, Mavuika channelled Ronova's borrowed power to break the invasion. In 5.3 the Traveler, granted Pyro by the Lord of the Night, descended with Mavuika into the Night Kingdom, helped by the souls of the fallen, and destroyed Gosoythoth, the heart of the Abyss there, ending the war.

The invasion cost thousands of lives, overran the Scions of the Canopy and hit the Flower-Feather Clan hardest, as the last tribe without a hero; Gosoythoth even extinguished the Sacred Flame for a time. In the final battle it took the form of the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire, built from Xiuhcoatl's memories, and imitated past Archons.

119.comment: Natlan: Ronova's Price and Capitano's Sacrifice
119.content: Using Ronova's power once was Mavuika's unique right, at the cost of her fated death. After Gosoythoth fell, Ronova demanded payment, and Mavuika prepared to give her life to repair the Night Kingdom. Capitano stepped in instead: a Khaenri'ahn cursed with undying life by Ronova herself, he offered his own "death", which would create a paradox unless she lifted the curse on his people. Ronova upheld the curse; Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night, making her immortal, and his body remains seated on the Throne of the Primal Fire atop Ochkanatlan. Mavuika lived, and one of his soldiers, Rotchev, attended the memorial.

120.content: When he struck his bargain, Xbalanque bet Ronova that humanity would win and asked, if it did, to see the new world for one day. After the war she kept the bet. Warned by the Wayob through Citlali, Mavuika and the Traveler welcomed him; he possessed a boy, Mausau, entered the new athletic Pilgrimage and was quickly eliminated in that small body, then dueled Mavuika in a spirit realm and narrowly lost. She declined his offer to briefly bring back someone from the Night Kingdom, took him around Natlan on her Flamestrider, and he returned to the Night Kingdom at day's end.

key: A Space and Time for You
121.content: After the war the Abyss Order attacked every tribe at once, starting with the Collective of Plenty, from a base at Ochkanatlan. Dainsleif arrived and tore through it. The attack was a diversion: the Traveler's sibling slipped into the Night Kingdom and struck a deal with the Lord of the Night, using the Loom of Fate to weave New Khaenri'ah's ley lines superimposed on Natlan, which briefly overlaid parts of Khaenri'ah and caused a time loop. The finished ley lines are stored in an Atlas, waiting for a place to lay them down. The Traveler also met Direidyth, a pure-blooded Khaenri'ahn woman seeking the "Savior", who came from another point in time.

122.content: Mavuika kept the Pyro Gnosis only as a last resort, refusing to use it because rewriting the ley lines would erase Natlan's history; Capitano came for it but, after losing his duel with her, declined to take it while she was weakened and later abandoned his mission. During the 5.x invasion its power kept the Sacred Flame burning. In 6.6 Mavuika tossed it to the Traveler "to do with as you see fit", and Nahida used its flames to burn the corrupted Irminsul; the Gnosis then vanished. Mavuika sensed the loss and accepted it, saying this time there was to be no "returning", only giving.

123.content:
Natlantea (also: Natlantean civilization, Natlantean era): Natlantea was the civilisation that came before Natlan: an age when Pyro dragons ruled and humans lived in primitive tribes. Its lord was the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, served by the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, and its greatest city was the Sacred City of Tollan. The era ended when Xbalanque united an army, defeated Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon.

Natlantea is not a place a traveller can visit as such; it is the ancient layer under today's Natlan. Its ruins, mechanisms and records are scattered across the nation, and the dragons of that age eventually devolved into the Saurians.

Geography: The land that is now Natlan, divided among the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, each of whom was given a territory to rule. Tollan was carved out by Xiuhcoatl himself and was said to be rivalled only by Chichen Uctokah. The wiki lists known sub-civilisations: Chichen Uctokah (the later Ochkanatlan, under the Lord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon), Ch'upikaq Tajin (now the Flower-Feather Clan's land, under Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak), Ek' Pulinik and Q'umqaraq'aj (unplaced), and the Tezcatepetonco Range (under Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox).

The 'cable' in Chichen Uctokah that leads beyond Teyvat's skies was anchored by the construct Tonatiuh. A Celestial Nail struck what is now the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, ruining Natlantea's phlogiston-rich soil.

People: Xiuhcoatl, born from the Primal Flame as the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, and his younger brother Kukulkan, whom he made from a portion of that flame on the day of his own birth. The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were artificial intelligences made by Xiuhcoatl, regarded as his descendants and as the peak of Secret Source Mechanism technology. Below them stood the Three Princes. Humans lived in tribes under the dragons' brutal rule.

The Lords held differing views of humans. The Third Lord made a pact with the humans of her region. The Eighth adopted a human daughter, Lianca, and gave her a bow made by the Second Lord. The Eleventh loathed humans more than any peer. The Fifth recommended culling the human population at a Sovereign Council. The First regarded Xbalanque as an enemy worthy of respect, and the Twelfth recognised his worth just before she died.

Kukulkan, who later became the human legend of the Sage of the Stolen Flame, gave a seed of phlogiston to the human Chaac after losing faith in dragonkind, which the sources describe as the re-establishment of human civilisation in Natlantea.

Governance: Rule by dragons over humans. Xiuhcoatl sat at the top; the Thirteen Sovereign Lords governed territories; councils of the Lords recorded debates, including over how to treat humans. Kukulkan served as Regent while Xiuhcoatl was incapacitated.

History: Xiuhcoatl was born from the Primal Flame and shaped the Pyro vishaps from it. The Heavenly Principles then arrived in Teyvat and defeated the Seven Sovereigns; Xiuhcoatl was frozen in lava and fell into a false death. Natlantea is thought to have come under Heavenly Principles control, overseen by Angels, with Kukulkan as Regent. When the Nibelung returned bearing the Abyss' power, its call woke Xiuhcoatl, who halted the Sovereign Lords' attempts to explore the stars and replicate moon-forging, retook control and devoured the Angels, an act that drove part of the unified civilisation into savagery.

As a result of the War of Funerary Flame, the ley lines of Natlantea, which the Heavenly Principles had made, were destroyed, and a Celestial Nail struck the future Basin of Unnumbered Flames. The ruined soil caused the dragonborn of Natlantea to regress. Xiuhcoatl, infested by the Abyss and losing his lucidity, built the Huitzilopochtli array, using his own eye as its control hub, and the Astral Assemblages in a last attempt to banish the Abyss from Teyvat, experimenting on himself in the process. Watching this, Kukulkan gave up on dragonkind and passed phlogiston to humans.

Xiuhcoatl's final plan was never completed before Xbalanque's siege. The dragons of Natlan later degenerated into the Saurians.

Status as of 7.1: Natlantea is long gone. Its legacy survives as ruins, Secret Source machinery, the Great Volcano of Tollan and the Saurians, and the older layers of Natlan's history keep surfacing in the Archon Quests and world quests. Nothing newer than 7.1 changes this.

124.content: Before Xiuhcoatl could carry out his last plan, Xbalanque and the army he had united invaded Tollan, killing ten of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords and the Three Princes. He then fought Xiuhcoatl; as they fell from a great height Xbalanque came out of Xiuhcoatl's chest, reborn as the first Pyro Archon. His victory and a treaty with Kukulkan ended dragon rule.

125.content: Xiuhcoatl's artificial 'descendants', each given a territory. Their attitudes to humans ranged from pacts and adoption to a recommendation to cull them. Ten of them died when Tollan fell. Other council records are preserved in the Chamber of Deliberation.

key: Kingdom of the Lord of the Night
126.content:
Night Kingdom (also: Realm of the Wayob, Kingdom of the Lord of the Night, Land of Night): The Night Kingdom is a realm of souls deep beneath Natlan, described as "a liminal space between the body and mind, life and death". Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, built it from the fragments of Natlan's ancient ley lines, which were shattered in the war of funerary flame. Since then it has worked as Natlan's ley lines. The tribes' ancestral spirits, the Wayob, live there, and so do the souls of Natlan's dead. Natlanese warriors draw their "Nightsoul" power from those souls. For five hundred years after the cataclysm the Abyss occupied the realm. The Traveler and Mavuika purged it in 5.3.

The dead of Natlan go there and slowly lose themselves in a "sea of souls". In time they are reborn in Natlan in a different form. Ancient Name bearers who fell in the Night Warden Wars could be brought back out through the Ode of Resurrection, provided their team won. Because the realm is not like the ley lines elsewhere in Teyvat, it holds only memories made in Natlan, and for millennia it accepted only Natlanese souls.

Geography: The Night Kingdom is not a place on the map. It lies "deep underground", and visitors reach it as souls or through ritual rather than on foot. Inside, Chasca warns, real-world knowledge no longer applies: the group falls a huge distance unharmed, and to leave they only need to stand under a shaft of light from above and pray. It is misty and easy to get lost in. Obsidian totem poles stand throughout it, and a Celestial Nail can be seen hanging far above.

Mavuika calls it "a realm of souls and memories, where mental fortitude outweighs physical strength". Six main totem poles act as the bodies of the six tribes' Wayob, and countless smaller proxy totems let the Wayob spread their awareness across the whole realm. The deepest part, where the Abyss had dug in, was the most contaminated. Gosoythoth retreated there, and the final battle of the war was fought there. When Mavuika's divine power washed through it during the war, the souls and memories inside took on the forms of their past selves for a while.

The Weaver of Secrets, one of the ancient Thirteen Sovereign Lords, merged her consciousness into the realm long ago and wove a "dream labyrinth" in it. It was meant to give the souls of dead dragons and humans peace and comfort. The Masters of the Night-Wind count the realm as familiar ground. Ororon tells the Traveler that he could never have caught them off guard anywhere else.

People: - **The Lord of the Night (Yohualtecuhtin)**: the realm's creator and ruler. She is an angel, a kind of being whose devolved descendants are the Seelies. Natlan's people worship her as a god.
- **The Wayob**: formless ancestral spirits, "will without form or thought". Each tribe has its own Wayob, which protects it, chooses who inherits Ancient Names and speaks through the chief's dreams.
- **The dead**: Natlanese souls, also called Nightsouls, who gradually merge into the sea of souls.

During the war the Traveler met many souls there. Mallko, a fallen Ancient Name bearer of the Scions of the Canopy, guided the rescuers through the mist. Tupac, a hero of five hundred years ago, spoke to them through Mualani's Ancient Name. In the final descent, the spirits of Atea, Mallko, Vichama, Chuychu and Guthred helped, along with the heroes of the old war. Mavuika says the heroes they saw were not true souls but "snapshots" left by Ancient Name engravers; their real souls had long since been reborn. Abyssal servants such as the Abyss Lector Comonqui also hunted there while the realm was corrupted.

Governance: The Lord of the Night keeps the realm and its rules. Mavuika says Natlan's rules "are founded in the Night Kingdom", so if the Lord of the Night vanished, they would vanish too. The rules that make the Ode of Resurrection possible come from Ronova, the Ruler of Death. She wrote them into the realm for the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, and lent him her power. Mavuika later used that power in the war against the Abyss, and its price under Ronova's rules was her own death.

The tribes' bond to their Wayob is the link between the surface and the realm. A tribe's strength showed in its Wayob's strength, and the Wayob chose a hero only when the tribe was ready for war. Before the war ended, the Wayob protected Natlanese everywhere inside Natlan, visitors included. They were very strict about letting anyone leave, because protecting people beyond the border used power they needed for the fight against the Abyss. Leaving needed the chief to ask the Wayob for approval.

History: In the war of funerary flame between the Descender and the dragons, Natlan's ley lines took the worst damage, and that opened a way for the Abyss. Guided by Ronova, the Lord of the Night rebuilt a similar network from what was left, and that network is the Night Kingdom. Xbalanque later strengthened it. In the cataclysm five hundred years ago, the Abyss was driven off the surface but rooted itself in the realm. That began the Night Warden Wars, which lasted five centuries and steadily wore the Wayob down. In 5.3 Mavuika and the Traveler destroyed Gosoythoth in its depths, and the Abyss was gone.

Ancient legend credits the first Wayob to Chaac, the first human to receive Phlogiston. At the end of his life, alone, he lit a flame on a mountain and called to his lost companions, and the god of the night realm answered. The tribes then worshipped their ancestors, the Wayob and the Night Kingdom. They spoke to it through obsidian and, in ancient times, through living sacrifices, often prisoners of war. Och-Kan, tyrant of Ochkanatlan, banned that worship. After his overthrow the tribes reconnected with the realm.

The Lord of the Night says the Heavenly Principles altered ley lines everywhere to counter the Abyss, and that stability came first. After Natlan's network was rebuilt, the rules needed for the Ode of Resurrection meant it could not be reconnected to other nations' ley lines. Mavuika adds that the Ruler of Death probably limited it to Natlan's souls so that the Ode could not be abused. Damage to the realm scatters souls that cannot find their way back, and those losses damage it further. Citlali gives this as the reason the Masters of the Night-Wind once planned to use Ororon as a vessel to carry lost souls home.

Atmosphere: Visitors describe mist, endless dark, glowing totems and voices. Under the Abyss's corruption, black manifestations of its power drift everywhere. Kachina kept hearing a voice tell her to give up on the Wayob and leave. In the depths, the Traveler sensed souls that had suffered for a very long time. After the purge, the Lord of the Night describes it as a place of rest, where souls lose themselves peacefully in the sea of souls.

Dangers: While the Abyss held it, visitors were contaminated even by a short stay, and a soul could be lost if a nearby proxy totem was badly corrupted. That is how Kachina went missing in 5.0. The Abyss could also seal the exits. Anyone whose soul is damaged or incomplete is especially vulnerable: the Lord of the Night's waking cry nearly shattered Ororon's soul.

Natlanese who left the realm's protection paid for it. Mavuika links memory loss, stress and even bad luck to life without the Wayob's protection. Souls that cannot reach the realm drift on the surface as ghosts and slowly, painfully disperse, unless a Night-Wind shaman such as Citlali "opens the gate" for them.

Travel: There is no road in. Known ways include the Pyro Archon stepping into the Sacred Flame during the Ode of Resurrection, and the Masters of the Night-Wind's rites (the Spiritspeaker Stone sent Kachina's rescuers). Capitano and Ororon also used a Masters' ritual to draw the Traveler's soul there. Obsidian totems scattered over Natlan act as contact points, and the Wayob can manifest on the surface through them and through Nightsouls.

Gameplay (not in-world lore): the Night Kingdom is not part of the open world. Touching Nightsoul Totems sends the player there for Local Legend trials, and Archon Quest scenes use the quest domain "Realm of the Night Kingdom" and the Chamber of Night's Trial. Nightsoul's Blessing, Nightsoul Bursts and Nightsoul Transmission are the combat and movement mechanics named after its souls.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter V: Black Stone Under a White Stone (5.0, Into Eternal Night), Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (5.1, To Whence the Smoke Drifts) and Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3, the final descent). World quests include Peace to the Slumbering, The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach and To the Night, What is the Night's. Act VI, A Space and Time for You (5.7), reveals what the Traveler's sibling did there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Night Kingdom is free of the Abyss and is being restored. The Lord of the Night is back inside it, maintaining Natlan's ley lines, and the Night Warden Wars are over.

Capitano gave his life in Mavuika's place and merged with the Lord of the Night. That made her undying and changed the realm's rules: the Night Kingdom now also takes in the souls of outlanders who die in Natlan, and Capitano led the souls he carried into it. Natlanese can now leave the country as often as they like, as long as their chief gives permission.

The Traveler's sibling later used part of the realm to weave New Khaenri'ah's ley lines (5.7). Citlali sensed only some "noise" and no real effect on Natlan. In 6.6, Mavuika's link to the Night Kingdom meant she could not be recorded in the Irminsul-linked ley lines that Dottore was watching while she was in Natlan.

127.comment: Night Kingdom: Wayob Totems and Proxies
127.content: Mallko explained the realm's layout to Kachina's rescuers. Six main totem poles in the Night Kingdom are the "bodies" of the six tribes' Wayob, and countless proxy totems let each Wayob extend its awareness over the realm and track souls wherever they wander. A badly contaminated proxy can let a soul go missing. In 5.0 the rescuers cleansed one corrupted totem, and Mavuika said that otherwise that part of the realm would have been lost to the Abyss for good.

128.comment: Night Kingdom: Ode of Resurrection and the Night Kingdom
128.content:
During the Ode, the Pyro Archon steps into the Sacred Flame and searches the Night Kingdom for the fallen warrior and their Ancient Name. If at least one of the warrior's team came back victorious, they could be brought back. A whole team that fell could not be. Souls left behind stay in the realm, and their Names are eventually lost. The Ode heals only the fatal wound. In 5.0 Mavuika came back without Kachina, finding neither her nor her Name, because the Abyss had cut the Wayob off.

With all six heroes gathered, Mavuika briefly extended the Ode's protection to every Natlanese warrior, Name or no Name, which brought casualties in the war to effectively nothing. After the war Mavuika declared the Night Warden Wars over and said she hoped the Ode would never again be needed to bring back the fallen.

129.comment: Night Kingdom: The Abyss in the Night Kingdom
129.content:
After the cataclysm the Abyss took root in the Night Kingdom, and for five centuries Natlan sent its best Ancient Name bearers into the realm to fight it. The Wayob grew weaker and their tie to the tribes nearly broke. In 5.0 Mavuika judged that the realm would be lost in under a year. In 5.3, Mavuika and the Traveler descended to the deepest, most corrupted layer, where Gosoythoth, the "heart of the Abyss", had fled. It took the form of the fallen Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl, drawing on his memories in the ley lines, and taunted them in the voices of past Pyro Archons. They destroyed it, and the realm was purged.

In the battle the Sacred Flame faltered. Kachina started the Ode on her own, the stadium crowd sang to send their support into the depths, and that revived the Flame and awakened the Nightsoul's Blessing of the Traveler's Ancient Name, Tumaini.

130.comment: Night Kingdom: Capitano's Sacrifice and the New Rules
130.content:
Mavuika had borrowed Ronova's power, and the price was her death. She meant to give her life to restore the Night Kingdom. The Lord of the Night waited for another who wished to take part: Capitano. He merged his existence with her, which turned his curse of undying life into her immortality and let him rewrite the realm's rules. Ronova withdrew her demand for Mavuika's death. Capitano led the souls he had carried, Khaenri'ahn and Natlanese alike, into the realm. From then on it also accepts outlanders who die in Natlan.

The Lord of the Night admitted that she had once thought little of how long a life lasts. She thanked humanity for her new endless life and called her responsibility the purpose of her existence, not a burden. Before Capitano's sacrifice, Mavuika had told the Traveler that the realm accepted only Natlan's souls. Capitano had come to Natlan because it was the one land where the souls he bore might find rest.

131.comment: Night Kingdom: The Sibling's Ley Line Weaving
131.content:
The Traveler's sibling believed the Heavenly Principles had locked Teyvat's ley lines, but saw the Night Kingdom as an exception. After the war they had the Abyss Order fake an attack on Natlan's tribes to buy time. Meanwhile they entered the realm and negotiated with the Lord of the Night. Even the Night Kingdom could not host new ley lines, but she granted them room to run the Loom of Fate. Through it they wove the ley lines of New Khaenri'ah, which they now hold.

Citlali later learned the story from the Lord of the Night in a dream. The Lord of the Night was intrigued by a third path besides Mavuika's defence of memory and Capitano's preference for the ley lines, and agreed once she was satisfied that the Loom would have no real effect on Natlan. She set a condition that Citlali was not told. The weaving briefly overlaid parts of Khaenri'ah onto Natlan, which caused a time loop.

132.comment: Night Kingdom: Origins of the Wayob and the Dream Labyrinth
132.content:
Two legends describe how the realm became bound to its people. The artifact Myths of the Night Realm says that Chaac, the first holder of Phlogiston, lived to be the last survivor of his band. On his final night he lit a flame on a mountain and called out to his lost companions. The god of the night realm answered, and that was the birth-cry of the first Wayob. Weapon texts and a Dragonlord priestess's records tell of the Weaver of Secrets, the Third of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords. She pitied her devolving dragons and made a pact with the human ancestors of the Masters of the Night-Wind, then merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom to weave a "dream labyrinth" where dragon and human souls could rest.

Her pact demanded a "Holy Sovereign" with a soul approved by the Lord of the Night, and the role was a cruel one. Kukulkan tried to wreck the arrangement by leading the last Holy Sovereign, the girl later called Maghan's master, astray. The Weaver foresaw it and guided her into the realm. There she showed the girl a future of peace between humans and dragons and told her to record memories on tapestries so that the labyrinth would endure. The labyrinth's pact with the Masters of the Night-Wind is said to hold to this day.

133.content:
Nursery of Nightmares: The Nursery of Nightmares is a space resembling the Night Kingdom in Ochkanatlan, Natlan. It is where the Traveler finished the chase for the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash in Moment of Awakening, where the dragon's corruption was purged and Och-Kan's soul was freed, and where Och-Kan's remains now lie.

The wiki lists it as a Point of Interest unlocked during the quest; the interactable remains describe him as the Python King, the Sacred Lord and the fell dragon, fully dragon and fully human, sleeping in silence until the end of time.

History: Cocouik's laser opens a gap in the fleeing dragon's defences, and the Traveler follows it into this space. A voice then introduces itself as Och-Kan, once ruler of Natlan, whose mind was infused into the city and whose soul had been devoured by the Abyss poison and turned into a furious dragon. The voice asks to be helped to purge the poison, and the dragon is defeated. Och-Kan speaks, now with his own mind, as the survivor of the Abyss's taint and as the one who in the past sealed his mind inside the Core of Chu'ulel.

Och-Kan lets the Traveler walk through his memories, since everything that happened in Ochkanatlan was recorded by his 'two tainted eyes'. They include the arrival of Taika's expedition and a confrontation in which Kukulkan tells Och-Kan he has betrayed Xbalanque's oath, that his dragon blood marks him as the last dragon-heir, and that he must join the two Golden Entreaties to activate Huitzilopochtli. Och-Kan refuses, saying a world without humans has no meaning, and Kukulkan warns that he will come to collect Och-Kan's soul. After the memories, a Golden Entreaty is recovered.

Och-Kan says that the Golden Entreaty can cleanse Natlan's Abyssal filth but not in the way the Traveler imagines, which is why he hid it. His memory is fragmented and he cannot recall what the Entreaty is for 'when taken to the sacred mountain', suspecting that Kukulkan is tampering with his thoughts. He also tells the Traveler that Little One carries the same Flamelord's Blessing as he does.

Quests: Moment of Awakening, the second part of The Tonatiuh Quivers, in the Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm quest chapter (5.2). The steps are tracking the dragon, defeating it, speaking to the 'evil dragon', looking for answers in Och-Kan's memories, and collecting the Golden Entreaty.

Atmosphere: The place is dream-like and quiet; the quest's black-screen narration and golden text give it the feel of a recollection rather than a location.

Dangers: In the story, the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash fights with Golden Flame attacks. Nothing else hostile is listed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Nursery is calm. Och-Kan's remains rest there; the dragon body and Cocouik's mind were reunited as Och-Kan, who died as the quest ended.

The Golden Entreaty found here was later joined with the other and used in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain (5.5). No development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

134.content: After Moment of Awakening the Nursery contains Och-Kan's remains as an interactable. Its text calls him the Python King, the Sacred Lord and the fell dragon, fully dragon and fully human, who now slumbers in silence until the end of time.

key: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
135.comment: Nursery of Nightmares: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
135.content: The Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash was the 'evil dragon' that haunted Ochkanatlan for decades and whom Bona's tribe feared. It was Och-Kan's Abyss-corrupted body, the half he had split from his mind. Kukulkan used it, the wiki says, to devour human souls for his masks. A nameless adventurer's notes say it attacked her but that she might owe it thanks for leading her to the Core of Chu'ulel.

136.content:
Ochkanatlan (also: Cinder City): Ochkanatlan, the Cinder City, is a ruined island city in Natlan, north of Quahuacan Cliff. It was built thousands of years ago by followers of Xbalanque on the remains of an older dragon city, and was ruled by the tyrant Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord, in the era of the Grand Alliance. Today it is thick with Abyssal corruption, shrouded in mist, and forbidden to the tribes. Any human found inside is either a memory of the past or a trespasser.

It is the setting of the world quest series Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (Version 5.2), in which the Traveler follows a legend of a "Jade of Return" and learns that the legend was a lure laid by the dragon Kukulkan. At the end of that series Och-Kan's tainted body is put to rest and his mind, which the adventurer Bona had freed from the Core of Chu'ulel and named Cocouik, passes on.

The wiki distinguishes the area (this entry) from the ancient civilisation of the same name. Use this entry for the place: how it looks, what is in it, and what a visitor would meet.

Geography: A mist-covered island north of Quahuacan Cliff, with a castle-like structure, the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams, at its centre. Waterfalls and underground ruins lie below it. Above it, drifting over a sea of clouds, hangs the Tonatiuh.

Local plants include Withering Purpurbloom, Brilliant Chrysanthemum, Saurian Claw Succulent, Glowing Hornshroom and Quenepa Berry, and different wildlife and Saurian species occupy different parts of the island. The base of the city is the old dragon city Chichen Uctokah (the "Land of Seven Flames"), which was built as the foot of a "stairway" or "cable" leading beyond Teyvat, working with the Tonatiuh as a satellite.
