196.comment: Temple of Cascading Colors: Ch'upikaq Tajin: Priestess's Records
196.content: Three interactable documents in the temple: dragon rulers argue over how to handle humans' theft of phlogiston, Kemonel plans a dream-realm, the writer plans a sealed domain called Xibalba, and a forged bow reaches the writer's daughter through Je'lal's secret gift.

197.content:
Tepeacac Rise (also: Genesis of the Mountains): Tepeacac Rise is a stretch of slopes in the northwest of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. The lower ground is unusually good for plant growth, so Saurians often rest there; Natlan also calls the slopes the "Genesis of the Mountains".

Its Nahuatl-style name is thought to relate to words for a settlement on a ridge or hilltop.

Geography: Green, sloping ground on the edge of the mountain, richer in vegetation than most of the surrounding rock. The local specialty is the Saurian Claw Succulent.

Next to the Local Legend "Sappho Amidst the Waves" lies an interactable notebook holding an unfinished musical score.

People: No permanent settlement is listed. Saurians are the usual visitors, resting on the gentler ground.

Culture: The score's note thanks someone for suggestions, says the music became livelier after adjustments, remarks that the writer and friend have not met since the last Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and proposes fruit wine and new songs next time. The writer is unnamed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary explorable subarea. Nothing about the score's author or recipient is established, so avoid naming them.

198.content:
Tequemecan Valley: Tequemecan Valley is the mining country of eastern Natlan and the home of the Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan), the tribe of miners, gem appraisers and craftspeople who live in a gorge with their burrowing Tepetlisaur companions. Clanging hammers and tapping gem-hunters echo through the canyon, and dance battles are held daily. Beneath the valley the Shadow Pins keep the Abyss sealed, and the ruins of an ancient oath lie below its hills.

The name is Nahuatl: tetl is stone, quemitl a ritual chest garment, and -can marks a place. The valley's rock walls are canvases for graffiti, a tradition said to start with a sage who engraved Phlogiston into flowing lines.

Geography: A canyon and gorge region in eastern Natlan with a settlement inside the gorge, mining tunnels, rocky slopes and underground ruins. Subareas include Sulfurous Veins (with the Land of Myriad Megaliths) and Tepeacac Rise. Local specialties are quenepa berries and saurian claw succulent.

The Children of Echoes have dug so deep into the mountains that sunlight is scarce in places. The Sulfurous Veins are described in-game as pins of rock entwined with golden runes, and the Land of Myriad Megaliths as a stone chamber of shifting crystal pillars.

Places: The Children of Echoes' settlement; Stage Tepetl, the grand dance-battle stage; Muhuru's Gemporium; the Mother Flamegranate Tree; Sulfurous Veins and the Land of Myriad Megaliths; the Hall of Parting Vows; Catastrophe's Edge; and the Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame.

Stage Tepetl has a DJ booth, fire-spewing props and a very sturdy frame. The Hall of Parting Vows is an underground ruin where Xbalanque and the Sage of the Stolen Flame swore a sacred oath. Glowing stairs below the hall lead to Catastrophe's Edge, and touching the inscription there takes the player to the Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame. Tlazolli's Home on the settlement's outskirts can be entered only during the quest Melodious Chant.

Tepeacac Rise is described as lower slopes surprisingly good for plants and a frequent resting place for saurians, called the 'Genesis of the Mountains'. Its Local Legend (Sappho Amidst the Waves) leaves an unfinished musical score with a note about meeting after the last Pilgrimage.

People: Chief Pacal, whose Tepetlisaur companion is Uchu, leads the Children of Echoes. The playable Xilonen has her workshop at the tribe's settlement.

Titu is the tribe's old storyteller. Traore, an elder and storyteller, is a former acting chief. The tribe fields 19 mining teams. The Scions of the Canopy post a guard at the Mother Flamegranate Tree, and Muhuru's Gemporium sells gems.

Culture: Stone is one of the tribe's symbols. The Children of Echoes value gemstones highly, some calling them a second layer of skin, and decorate tools, weapons and accessories with them as a sign of skill and status. The tribe is the sole producer of obsidian, an important ceremonial material. They love rhythmic music and dance, especially breakdance.

Dance competitions are constant: the Drillbit Dance Dance-Off has run daily for over 350 years, its tally standing at 127,751 rounds. The Salutary Furnace in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame is staffed by the tribe's best craftspeople.

The tribe was founded before the Grand Alliance by Ixquieh, the first bearer of the Ancient Name Baraka. Its chiefs are counted by number; Sundjatta was the 52nd and fell in the last battle against the Abyss five hundred years ago.

History: Natlan/History says that during the cataclysm, five hundred years ago, the Children of Echoes' acting chief Traore led the tribe against an Abyssal invasion in their territory. With help from two Khaenri'ahn warriors, Zephaniah and Irizar, they trapped the Abyss deep underground using the Shadow Pins. The Land of Myriad Megaliths is given as that underground place.

The Shadow Pins are large stone pillars with smaller Lesser Shadow Pins nearby, and the old storyteller Titu says the giant pin once plunged beneath the earth in an earthquake. In the world quest Beneath the Crystal Rock, two of three Lesser Shadow Pins had recently floated up, a sign the seal was weakening. The Traveler and Titu repaired the pins and reinforced the seal on the Abyss.

In Revelations from the Past the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One enter the Hall of Parting Vows; a mural shows Xiuhcoatl's defeat, and visions show the annihilation of the Sacred City of Tollan and a giant dragon with pierced pupils falling with a tiny human. The trial leads down to Catastrophe's Edge and to a Golden Entreaty token left by the Sage of the Stolen Flame. The NPC Manqu says the Sage believed humans could guide and lead saurians toward a future brighter than the age of the giant dragons.

Atmosphere: Hammers ringing off the canyon walls, dust in the tunnels, glittering crystals, thumping beats from Stage Tepetl and bright graffiti on the cliffs. The mood is rowdy and warm.

Dangers: Rockfond Rifthounds and Abyss-corrupted Nightsoul variants of Forged Sand fighters and Tepetlisaurus warriors turn up in the underground ruins, and swiftstep couriers roam above. The boss is the Gluttonous Yumkasaur Mountain King, Kongamato.

A boundary-eroding Abyss-corroded Golden Wolflord is the final trial at Catastrophe's Edge. Unstable Phlogiston crystals can be sensed by Tepetlisaurs and the tribe's playable characters, which makes tunnelling safer.

Travel: Tepetlisaurs can burrow through certain surfaces and enter Molten Fissures. A tribe member or Tepetlisaur indwelling lets one ascend Phlogiston crystals.

Quests: World quests include Beneath the Crystal Rock (the Shadows of the Mountains chapter, begun with Titu), Peace to the Slumbering, Ripe For Trouble (the Mother Flamegranate Tree and its Mountain King Flamegranates) and Revelations from the Past (Between Pledge and Forgettance chapter).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is quiet; the Shadow Pins hold, and the tribe's music and mining carry on.

The Abyss's assault on Natlan ended in 5.3. The Children of Echoes lost members in the earlier invasion, including Batz and Nechca.

The wiki lists no story changes at Tequemecan Valley in 6.x or 7.x.

199.comment: Tequemecan Valley: Shadow Pins and the Land of Myriad Megaliths
199.content:
Huge stone pillars in the Land of Myriad Megaliths, below Tequemecan Valley, hold the Abyss beneath the earth. Tribal tales say the Wayob hung them to pin the shadow of the 'Volcano Lord'; the storyteller Titu says what lies beneath is truly the Abyss. The Children of Echoes, with Khaenri'ahn help, set the seal five hundred years ago.

The Lesser Shadow Pins have floated before, and the old way to deal with it is to repair the engraved inscriptions with their power.

200.content:
The source of the Scions of the Canopy's Flamegranates. A guard, Tisoc, stands at the entrance to the cave holding its roots and admits only Scions with special named passes. Its special roots thrive in lava rather than burning, and the fruit must grow near liquid Phlogiston to mature. Larger Flamegranates grow in the open on the cliffs; Mountain King Flamegranates, grown in the cave, are offered to Kongamato.

Initially the tree is blue and its fruit unripe; after the quest Ripe For Trouble it turns orange and the fruit ripens.

201.comment: Tequemecan Valley: Hall of Parting Vows
201.content: An underground ruin unlocked in Revelations from the Past. It is where Xbalanque and the Sage of the Stolen Flame swore their oath. Murals show Xiuhcoatl's defeat. Below the hall, Catastrophe's Edge holds a trial and the token the Sage left.

202.content:
Tete Isle (also: Tete Island): Tete Isle is a subarea of Easybreeze Holiday Resort, the summer resort island off Natlan's far west. It is known for a lively atmosphere and its specialty drink, Aphimead, and becomes accessible at step 5 of the story quest The World Is Your Canvas! (Sunspray Summer Resort, Part II).

Three points of interest are listed: the Dance-Off Stage, and two competing Aphimead bars, Me & Dew and The Dewdrop.

Places: The Dance-Off Stage is an elaborate performance stage with dynamic music mixing, lighting and stage effects; it resembles a giant eye with the DJ booth as its pupil. Me & Dew is owned by Tlapalli (from step 22 of The World Is Your Canvas!); The Dewdrop is its rival. Both specialise in Aphimead.

A lone islet to the north holds a Precious Chest guarded by Flowing Blade pirates and a Koholasaurus; defeating them brings in reinforcements led by Radius Bone Jack and her crew, who sing as they arrive.

People: The wiki lists many residents and visitors, including Ca'asho, Chira, Elmi, Feiming, Ho'oliu, Icahua, Kapak, Malinche, Oquichi, Papar, Pumayna, Q'ellu, Q'utuj, Taye, Tecuhtli, Tlapalli, Uhane, Vara and Wayner. Detail about each belongs in their own entries.

History: Two letters found on the isle show a pirate plot. One, signed Black Reef Rekis and addressed to Captain Radius, says powerful figures want a Monetoo captured from Tenochtzitoc and offers relief on a spine-ownership dispute and personal debts, adding that he had sent Icahua ahead to the resort as insurance. The other, from the crewman Tecuhtli, reports that Icahua took one of his eyes, that he poisoned Icahua, that he went to the Asha's home and removed Rekis's men who were caging Asha, and that the two bars sell good Aphimead and juice. Both letters carry sung, scribbled lines from the captain's side.

Atmosphere: Music, drink and crowds: a holiday island's nightlife hub rather than a place of danger, with a pirate subplot at its edges.

Quests: World quests listed here are Dreamy Paititi and Strange Encounter of the Tete Isle Kind. They are part of the permanent resort content.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a permanent, explorable part of Easybreeze Holiday Resort, added in 5.8.

203.content:
Teticpac Peak: Teticpac Peak is a plateau with a small lake at the highest point of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. It contains the Manse of Monetoo Murals.

The name comes from Nahuatl roots meaning roughly "large rock" and "the building above".

Places: The one listed point of interest is the Manse of Monetoo Murals, whose viewpoint text, "Where the Painted Realm Unfolds", wonders whether a world was born from wall graffiti or merely hidden by expressive writing.

The manse has its own entry. Its music track is "Whistles of Monetoo", shared with Spiritwall Cave.

Quests: Linked quests: the world quests In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons, Lies and Promises and Weighty Wings, and the Hidden Exploration Objective The Secret Gate of Graffiti.

Atmosphere: A high, open summit above the mountain, with a lake and a sense of looking down on Natlan. Do not invent inhabitants.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary explorable subarea.

204.content:
Tezcatepetonco Range: The Tezcatepetonco Range is the highland home of the Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan), Natlan's shamans and mystics, who speak with the Wayob, watch over the ley lines and Phlogiston, read futures and heal. The tribe is reclusive and eccentric and has the deepest bond with the Night Kingdom of any Natlan tribe. A fog-covered island, Tecoloapan Bay, lies off the range. In Nahuatl, Tezcatepetonco means 'mirror on the hill'.

Visitors from other tribes come here for fortune-telling, blessings on tools and weapons, and the old arts of Phlogiston engraving. The best-known shaman, Citlali, lives in the range.

Geography: Rocky highlands in Natlan where the tribe's settlement sits around the Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land. Tecoloapan Bay is an island lying to the west of the range. Xalac Vale, a river valley, runs from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to the Flower-Feather Clan, passing north of the shamans' settlement. Local specialties: glowing hornshroom and sprayfeather gill.

Parts of the range are muted into grey by Pale Mist, which strips colour from the land until nearby stone monuments are painted correctly and activated. A cave southwest holds the Trial of Disembodiment.

Places: The settlement of the Masters of the Night-Wind and its Chamber of Weaving; the Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land; Citlali's Home; Idukan's Trove, a bookstore run by Amazolli; Scorchwind Trial Grounds; Xalac Vale; and Tecoloapan Bay.

The Scorchwind Trial Grounds south of the settlement host the Pakpaka Flying School, which teaches flying with Qucusaurs and seems to be run by the Flower-Feather Clan. A notice in Xalac Vale advertises the school. Tecoloapan Bay's island is initially hidden in dense fog and listed on the map only as '???'.

Three damaged stone tablets, 'Stone Tablet Amidst Gray Ash' I to III, lie in the range: one northeast of the Statue of the Seven, one west of the settlement and one in a cave above the Trial of Disembodiment. The first two can only be read once the Pale Mist is lifted.

People: Chief Biram presides at the Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land. Caholom is the High Priest, Tlapo the Iktomisaurus elder and Cip a guard; Toltec and Yolotli also work at the altar and the Chamber of Weaving. Citlali is the tribe's most experienced shaman and has created many spells of her own.

Their saurian companions are Iktomisaurs. Most Mictlan members seen outside are travelling doctors. Some tribe members have no spiritual sensitivity at all and are called 'spirit-duffers'. The playable Citlali has her home here.

Culture: Their main role is as shamans who conduct rituals to talk with the Wayob for knowledge and guidance, and they are also storytellers, record-keepers, doctors and Phlogiston engravers. The Mictlan can perceive Phlogiston and souls, and they cast spells for healing, telekinesis, concealment and extracting memories.

Their spells depend on skill and training. Citlali explains that all of the tribe's spells and problem-solving methods are based on dealing with spirits, so some spiritual sensitivity is required. Unlike other Natlanese, shamans can sense their connection to the Wayob and the Night Kingdom, and whether they are far enough from home to sever it.

The Mictlan tribe was founded shortly after the Archon War through the joint efforts of the Priest-King Maghan and his master, a young mystic.

History: Five hundred years ago the Border Master Sanhaj of this tribe joined Tenoch's coalition and died with him at the Mare Jivari, when the two used the engraved body of Tenoch to raise a miniature Night Kingdom inside the Bakunawa. A former chief, Ayizu, fell in the cataclysm; with his last words he told the ally he had fought beside, 'the Captain', the secret of the Gnosis.

Damaged stone tablets in the range tell of an older disaster: the Sacred Flame burned away the 'pitch-black foe', but its embers floated like clouds, and a canyon in the sea, Ochkanatlan, was covered by flowing ashes that destroyed colour. Not even the High Priests of the tribe could fix this 'purging of color'. In a later tablet the sages in white engraved golden inscriptions like rings upon a stone dragon, and priests who venerated it each day kept Cinder City from being covered again, though the ash was never fully removed.

Version 5.3 added a new waypoint in the range along with a new boss, the Wayward Hermetic Spiritspeaker.

Atmosphere: Hushed and uncanny: rocky heights, grey stone where the Pale Mist lies, glowing hornshrooms, and shamans who work with spirits. Tecoloapan's fog adds to the mood.

Dangers: The boss is the Wayward Hermetic Spiritspeaker. The Pale Mist hides inscriptions and drains colour. Tecoloapan Bay holds Abyss-corrupted Nightsoul enemies.

In The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach two voices speak: a weak one asks the Traveler to break four seals on the island and a menacing whisper warns against it. The weak voice is the true, weakened Wayob manifestation; the whisper belongs to an Abyss-corrupted mimic trying to take over the spirit within this 'puppet'. The central seal had cut the Nightsouls off from the Lord of the Night's realm, and breaking it lets them return to rest.

Travel: The NPC Sakaw is posted near the waypoint on the range's western end. Tecoloapan Bay is reached by crossing the water.

Quests: World quest: The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach (clearing the fog and the seals), started by approaching the fogbound island. See also the entry on the limited-time event Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace, and Tecoloapan Bay is free of fog and seals.

Natlan's war with the Abyss ended in 5.3, and the tribe can leave Natlan without loss of memory. Four Masters of the Night-Wind were potential casualties of the earlier invasion depending on player choice: Iyoba, Mayahuel, Osawe and Waqar.

The wiki lists no changes to the range in 6.x or 7.x.

205.comment: Tezcatepetonco Range: Masters of the Night-Wind
205.content: The Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan) are one of Natlan's six tribes, shamans who talk with the Wayob and tend Natlan's ley lines and Phlogiston. Their chief is Biram, and their saurian companions are Iktomisaurs.

206.content: Initially covered in fog and marked '???' on the map, Tecoloapan Bay is a forbidden ceremonial site. A damaged record tells visitors to leave quickly, to beware deceptive bewitchment and never to look, and shows the half-sane carvings of the writer, who wanted to seal something. A Nightsoul totem there says the long-lost Obsidian Totem Pole cannot respond. Completing the World Quest The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach disperses the fog, and the true name of the island is shown.

207.content: The limited-time event Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls begins with the story quest Night-Wind Letter at the Masters of the Night-Wind settlement. It features Citlali, Ororon and Leyla, and it is the source of the account that Sanhaj died in the Mare Jivari explosion that destroyed the Bakunawa. Because it was an event, not every Natlanese or visitor will know its contents.

208.content:
The Mysterious Island's Truth: The Mysterious Island's Truth is a quest domain in Ameyalco Waters, Toyac Springs, Natlan: an underground lava cave the party enters through a giant whirlpool during Mualani's story quest of the same name. The name is the wiki's unofficial label.

It is the fourth part of Mualani's "Journey to the Mysterious Island" (chapter "Where the Springs Return", Act III), also linked to the Underground Lava River. Characters involved include Mualani, Karya, Koolau, Nuu and Viramdra. Mualani is the trial character. The party explores the cave, discusses what to do, fights, rescues Viramdra, then escapes and accompanies Mualani to return a talisman.

Dangers: Gameplay layer: Pyro Slimes and Large Pyro Slimes, then a Fluid Avatar of Lava together with Large Pyro Slimes in two waves. Viramdra must be caught within a 54-second time limit. The cave holds two Common Chests and one Exquisite Chest.

Quests: Story quest "The Mysterious Island's Truth" (version 5.0), part 4 of "Journey to the Mysterious Island"; it ends with a commemorative photo with Mualani.

Completing it grants 200 reputation with the 'People of the Springs' (the reputation entry is titled 'Journey to the Mysterious Island'), among other rewards.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain as of 7.1; the wiki entry is a stub.

209.comment: The Mysterious Island's Truth: Whirlpool into the lava cave
209.content: The giant whirlpool sends the party to the quest domain, a lava-filled underground cave where Viramdra must be rescued.

210.content:
The Salutary Furnace: A blacksmith's stall in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, owned by Alom, built around a giant furnace at one side of the Temple of Pax.

Per its map description, the Children of Echoes' most skilled craftspeople use Liquid Phlogiston purified by the Sacred Flame to forge unique personal weapons for warriors from across the land. Alom is its vendor.

Places: It stands on one side of the Temple of Pax section, in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames.

Culture: The map description presents it as a place where fighters get weapons made specifically for them rather than standard issue, using phlogiston refined by the Sacred Flame, which fits the Stadium's role as a venue for tournaments.

Do not assume Alom is the only smith there; the description speaks of the most skilled craftspeople of the Children of Echoes in general.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

211.content:
The Upper Sanctum (also: Upper Sanctum, Hanan Pacha): The Upper Sanctum, also called Hanan Pacha, is a ring of floating islands above the lake at Ameyalco Waters in Toyac Springs, Natlan. Legend says the Sage of the Stolen Flame and his companion Chaac raised it into the sky, and that people who passed his trials were taught to use phlogiston there and formed the first human tribe. The islands are said to be held together by Phlogiston. A trial ends at a hidden hot spring in the centre.

It is called the Upper Sanctum because neither humans nor saurians can ordinarily reach it. A Spiritway is needed.

Geography: Today the Upper Sanctum is not one island but a ring of smaller islands, visible from the lake below. It can only be entered by activating a Spiritway, and the ancient trial mechanisms (Spiritways and Iridescent Inscriptions) still work. In Seeker No Finding the Traveler follows a sequence of Spiritways and inscriptions to a hidden centre island with a hot spring full of phlogiston. Phlogiston also supports grass and flowers and warms cold ground, Chikya says.

Gameplay note: besides the quest route, the islands can also be reached with a geyser pillar south of Toyac Springs, with a flying character followed by a Natlan character such as Kinich. The Phlogiston Chiselith found all over Natlan are said, in the scrolls, to have been modelled on the mechanisms here.

History: By the legend in Records of Hanan Pacha, the Sage of the Stolen Flame, Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, brought back the 'kindling' of phlogiston from the red and black lands by tricking a vain winged dragon out of its Pyrophosphorite. Because nobody wanted to learn from him, he first taught the 'fool' Chaac, and the two raised a tract of land into the air: Hanan Pacha. Chaac guarded the lake and helped people ascend; those who passed the Sage's trials learned phlogiston, and they formed the first permanent tribe there. The book says historians regard this as a fable with no historical basis.

The same fable says the people built a city of gems, feathers and flowers on the islands, and the Sage decided to raise them higher still, forbidding any food produced by the land. The Lord of the Night, fearing humanity's departure, tricked Chaac with an intoxicating drink, and when the Sage returned and found everyone drunk he expelled the tribe, which carried phlogiston across Natlan. The Sage then set out for home, and the fable says he will one day return.

In Tracer No Tracing, Chikya says some call the Sage a madman or lunatic, which she takes as a compliment, and that he stole the flaming phlogiston seed from the giant dragon. Some of her tribe doubt a human could do it. Quest 5.5 later reveals that 'Waxaklahun Ubah Kan' is one of many names invented by Kukulkan, the dragon behind the Sage of the Stolen Flame, which complicates the legend's claim that the Sage was human.

People: Chikya, listed by the wiki as a member of the Masters of the Night-Wind, who cannot wield phlogiston because of an Abyss-related injury in her youth, is the quest's guide; she looks after her tribe's ancient woven scrolls. The Traveler, Paimon and Little One travel with her.

Quests: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire (5.0): Tracer No Tracing starts in the Underground Lava River, where a Spiritdoor trial asks for Unveiling Scripts and opens a Spiritway to the Upper Sanctum. Seeker No Finding then takes the party up to the islands, where they follow Iridescent Inscriptions along Spiritways to the hot spring.

Chikya had told the Traveler the spring might be a 'legendary elixir that cures all injuries'. She knew from the start it was a hot spring and confesses she tricked them; her injuries are not cured, but she stays to soak.

Atmosphere: From below it looks grey and empty, but the islands hold grass and flowers and warm ground. The final trial is a fight with Avatars of Lava awakened by a stone tablet, after which the water level rises and the spring fills with phlogiston.

Dangers: Falling from the floating islands, and the Eroding Avatars of Lava that the final trial's stone tablet awakens.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Upper Sanctum remains a broken ring of islands whose trials and hot spring still function. Chikya soaks in the spring and returns to her scrolls.

No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here. The Records of Hanan Pacha can be found in Natlan's Scions of the Canopy and the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

212.comment: The Upper Sanctum: Hanan Pacha hot spring
212.content: The hot spring at the centre of the Upper Sanctum is the 'gift' the Sage of the Stolen Flame leaves for those who pass his trial. After the final fight its water level rises and the spring becomes full of phlogiston. Chikya says a chosen hero who bathes in it receives the power to wield phlogiston; for the Traveler, who could already use phlogiston, nothing changed.

213.comment: The Upper Sanctum: Records of Hanan Pacha
213.content: Records of Hanan Pacha is a three-volume fable in Natlan collected from the Scions of the Canopy and the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It tells first how the Sage and Chaac stole phlogiston from a vain winged dragon that had claimed Xiuhcoatl's treasures, then how phlogiston was passed to people and Hanan Pacha was raised, and finally (volume 3) how the tribe broke the Sage's taboo and was expelled. The book carries a note that scholars consider it unrelated to historical fact.

214.content:
Throne of the Primal Fire: The Throne of the Primal Fire is a site in Ochkanatlan where the throne of the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, once stood. The map text says he borrowed the Ruler of Death's power here to establish Natlan's rules.

A thousand years later, the same place is described as where another human hero has "frozen" life and death, to remain there forever.

History: In the map description, the throne belonged to Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon. At this spot he borrowed the power of the Ruler of Death, understood to be Ronova, to establish Natlan's rules of death and rebirth.

The text then says a thousand years have passed and another human hero has frozen life and death here. The wiki connects this figure to Capitano. The throne's own voice line says a noble figure coats the sun with frost and that two eras grant salvation to Natlan not once but twice.

The wiki also notes the scene resembles a scene from another franchise, a trivia point and not canon.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the Pyro-aligned Traveler can offer Blazing Flint Ore to the throne to raise Primal Flame Resonance. Six ores are the maximum and each unlocks bonus effects at a constellation level. Offering requires the Traveler as the active character and attuned to Pyro. The offering system unlocks after completing "Incandescent Ode of Resurrection".

Atmosphere: Austere and sombre, a seat of power gone cold and frosted, with death and rebirth hanging over it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the location is a point of interest in Ochkanatlan; it appears after the quest "When All Becomes a Monument". Before that quest the throne is part of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams.

215.comment: Throne of the Primal Fire: Throne of the Primal Fire
215.content: The Throne of the Primal Fire in Ochkanatlan was the seat of the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, who borrowed the Ruler of Death's power there to set Natlan's rules. A human hero is now said to have frozen life and death there.

216.content:
Tlazolli's Forge (also: Tlazolli's Workshop): Tlazolli's Forge is a workshop belonging to Tlazolli, a forger of Ancient Names among the Children of Echoes in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. She had given it out as closed down after leaving her position in the tribe. In the Tribal Chronicles quest Wailing Cacophony it turns out to be a ritual site, guarded by hired Forged Sand fighters, where she tries to imprint her dead daughter Nechca's memories onto the adopted girl Nepecha.

It exists in the game as a quest domain, entered during Wailing Cacophony, the third part of the act Melodious Chant (5.1). After the ritual failed, the tribe closed the workshop officially.

Geography: The entrance is blocked by mud and rocks and carries a sign saying the workshop is closed and no entry is allowed. Inside, the workshop is a series of industrial chambers joined by working transport carriages, with controller levers that open gates and move carts to deeper areas. Solid Phlogiston walls and Molten Fissures are part of the layout; Children of Echoes can use their abilities to climb on solid Phlogiston. At the centre is the ritual chamber where the Central Inscription is set up.

Doors are shut along the way, so Xilonen and the Traveler have to find the controls to restart the transport system and ride it further in. The carts run on a timer, so the party has to reach the next gate before it closes.

Places: Entrance: the sealed front, with the closure sign. Outer halls: where the hired fighters wait. Transport depots: carriages and levers that connect the chambers. Central chamber: the ritual space where Nepecha lay while the engraving diagram ran and the Blazegem Inscriptions were linked to the Central Inscription.

People: Tlazolli, a forger who stepped down from her tribal position and was also Xilonen's mentor, is the owner. Nepecha, an orphan she raised, is brought here against her will. Xilonen and the Traveler follow them in. The workshop is guarded by Forged Sand fighters and, in the last stretch, Tepetlisaurus warriors.

Xilonen calls Tlazolli "Auntie". Nechca, Tlazolli's real daughter, died in an Abyss attack years earlier but is present in the story through a cinematic in which she speaks, her spirit having remained within Tlazolli's own Ancient Name.

History: Several years before the Traveler arrived, an Abyss attack killed Tlazolli's daughter Nechca and orphaned another child, Nepecha, who shared Nechca's birthday and was about the same age. Tlazolli took Nepecha in, then gradually came to treat her as the lost Nechca. She forged and sold Blazegem Inscriptions, decorative pieces made by methods similar to Ancient Name forging, that quietly drew memories of Nechca from their owners. These were meant to be gathered through a Central Inscription and pressed onto Nepecha. When Xilonen discovered the memory theft, Tlazolli fled with Nepecha to her workshop.

In the forge, Tlazolli said she meant the Central Inscription to become Nechca's Ancient Name and that she had set up all the inscriptions. Xilonen found a flaw in the engraving diagram and, on her countdown, the ritual was turned against itself. What poured out of the inscriptions was mostly the grief and pain of everyone who had seen Nechca dying, not clean memories. Newly kindled flames purified those thoughts and awakened the real Nechca, who had remained in Tlazolli's Ancient Name, Undugu (Kinship). Nechca spoke with her mother and blessed Nepecha before fading. Tlazolli, broken, was tied up by Xilonen and taken into tribal custody. Per the wiki profile, the workshop was then officially closed, Xilonen took Nepecha to her own workshop, and the Blazegem Inscriptions were deactivated and destroyed. Later, in Journey of Stars and Flames, Tlazolli is said to have met Nechca in a dream and lent her power against the Abyss.

Tlazolli denied lying, claiming she only wanted to save her daughter, and described the dead Nechca as having stayed too long in a "Night Kingdom". Per the wiki profile, she had told the tribe that Nechca was only injured and that Abyssal energy had caused the memory loss, and had kept Nepecha isolated and given her "medicine" that made her sleepy. Nepecha's attempts to get word out are how Xilonen and the Traveler came to be involved.

Dangers: As a quest domain it is a combat challenge with a Geo trial Xilonen: Forged Sand Interrogators, Shieldbreakers and Javelineers in the outer areas, then a final wave including Tepetlisaurus Warriors before the confrontation with Tlazolli. Solid Phlogiston and Molten Fissures are used to cross the layout. The domain is part of the quest and not open-world content.

Quests: Wailing Cacophony, part three of the Melodious Chant act in the Tribal Chronicles "A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks", centred on Xilonen. It follows A Faint Signal Lingers and leads to Serenity's Reprise.

Atmosphere: A cold, shut-up place that should be empty: stale furnace heat, the creak of carts on their rails, rows of glowing inscriptions that hum with something unwholesome. Beneath the machinery sits the sound of a mother whispering reassurance to a child who is not hers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forge is closed by the Children of Echoes, its inscriptions neutralised, and Tlazolli is in tribal custody pending a judgement the sources do not give.

217.content: The Tribal Chronicles quest in which Xilonen and the Traveler confront Tlazolli in her workshop, stop the ritual and rescue Nepecha. It ends with Nechca's blessing and with Tlazolli taken into custody.

218.content: Decorative pieces forged by Tlazolli using methods like Ancient Name forging. Sold in the tribe, they secretly absorbed their owners' memories of Nechca, along with the emotions attached to them, and were linked to a Central Inscription in the forge. After the ritual failed they were deactivated, owners regained their memories, and the remaining ones were destroyed.

219.content:
Tlazolli's Home (also: Tlazolli's house, Tlazolli's workshop): Tlazolli's Home is the dwelling and workshop of Tlazolli, an Ancient Name forger of the Children of Echoes, on the outskirts of the tribe's settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. Its interior can be entered only during the quest Melodious Chant. It is where Nechca's birthday party is held and where a mother's grief turned into a harmful deception.

In canon the house is tied to one story: Tlazolli, Xilonen's former mentor, hid a plan here to overwrite the memories of an orphaned girl, Nepecha, so that she would become her dead daughter Nechca. After the plan failed the workshop was officially closed off by the tribe.

Places: The house is a private dwelling at the edge of the Children of Echoes' settlement. The wiki lists an interior used only in the Melodious Chant quest and a separate workshop where Tlazolli worked on her Ancient Name forging; the nearby domain Tlazolli's Forge is a related site.

The quest-only interior is where Xilonen, the Traveler and Paimon bring a gift to Nechca's birthday, as set up in the act's first quest, Threadlike Whispers. The workshop later becomes the scene of the confrontation in which Tlazolli tries to finish a "Central Inscription" meant to imprint synthetic memories onto Nepecha.

People: Tlazolli, the owner, is an adult Ancient Name forger whose Ancient Name is Undugu. Nepecha lives with her as an adopted daughter; the tribe believes the girl is Nechca, Tlazolli's real daughter who died in an abyssal attack some years earlier. Xilonen, her former pupil, is a frequent visitor.

Tribe members who owned Blazegem Inscriptions unknowingly lost memories of Nechca to the scheme; the effect was reversed once the inscriptions were deactivated.

History: Several years before the Traveler's arrival Tlazolli's daughter Nechca died in an abyssal attack. Nepecha, a girl of about the same age with the same birthday, was orphaned in the same attack and was taken in. Tlazolli told the tribe that Nechca had merely been wounded and that abyssal energy had erased her memories, and she kept Nepecha isolated and sedated with a "medicine" so the truth would not surface. She also made and sold Blazegem Inscriptions that quietly gathered memories of Nechca from their wearers.

In Wailing Cacophony Xilonen noticed the missing memories and the knowledge "Nechca" should not have had. Tlazolli fled with Nepecha to her workshop; Xilonen and the Traveler burned away the stolen memories before the transfer could finish, which also let Nechca's soul, held within Tlazolli's Ancient Name, speak to her mother a last time. Tlazolli was taken into tribal custody and the workshop was closed. In Serenity's Reprise the inscriptions were gathered and destroyed. Later, in a dream, Tlazolli agreed to lend her power to the Traveler's fight against the Abyss.

Atmosphere: A modest craftsperson's home that looks warm and ordinary from outside, which is what makes the hidden strain inside it feel unsettling. Before the truth is exposed, the household is polite, watchful and a little too attentive to what Nepecha says.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the home is closed off by the tribe after Tlazolli's crimes; she is in custody and Nepecha stays with Xilonen.

Nobody lives here now. Do not stage new scenes inside as an open, welcoming house unless setting them before the events of Melodious Chant.

220.content:
Toyac Springs: Toyac Springs is the hot-spring coast of Natlan and the home of the People of the Springs (Meztli), a tribe of guides, cartographers, musicians and spa-keepers who live with their water-loving Koholasaurs. Official text calls it the most popular tribe region with outside visitors. Its name resembles the Nahuatl atoyac, 'on the river'.

An underground river of lava here is the real site behind the tribe's legend of a mysterious island. The playable hero Mualani is one of its people.

Geography: Springs, warm pools and beaches along Natlan's shore, with sub-areas Ameyalco Waters (Spiritways and eddies for Koholasaurs), the floating islands of the Upper Sanctum, Spiritwall Cave and the tribe's settlement. The only local specialty is sprayfeather gill.

The Underground Lava River is a cavern filled with Liquid Phlogiston and shows periodic volcanic activity. The Upper Sanctum is a ring of floating islands held up by Phlogiston and only reachable via a Spiritway.

Places: The People of the Springs' settlement, with Colomche Plaza (an open space where musicians and street artists perform), Golden Dusk (a restaurant and lodge by the beach), Leisurely Puffer (a watersports shop owned by Mualani's family, known for custom surfboards), Djembe Studios (an instrument shop run by Anchieta), Xochicuicatl Records (a record store owned by Pakaa Nui that also composes, records and markets music), Atlahua's Net (a fishing-gear store owned by Yelafath) and Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner, a small psychotherapy shop staffed by a dream-eating baku called Mint Daifuku and presumably owned by Yumemizuki Mizuki; Ameyalco Waters; the Upper Sanctum; the Underground Lava River; and Spiritwall Cave.

Golden Dusk is an old home of the Nui family, turned into a restaurant at Chief Amina's suggestion; its matriarch Kupo Nui owns it and Tirda sings there. It has held 242 rounds of the Inferno Stomach Supremo eating contest, whose current champion is Varesa of the Collective of Plenty. The tribe uses natural springs for locals and vetted guests and artificial springs for foreigners who cannot tolerate the heat of natural ones.

Spiritwall Cave contains the notes of a graffiti maker who was trapped by a rockfall and kept drawing. He wrote that he had devised an art of pictures from Phlogiston Engraving, hoped it would one day be appreciated, and left without giving his name.

People: Amina is chief. Mualani, the 'swellrider' of the hot springs, is a hero from the tribe, and her family owns the Leisurely Puffer. The Nui family run Golden Dusk.

Past members include Atawallpa, the giant Tupac, the former chief Paio and, by the wiki's inference, the ancient Pyro Archon Cochanina. Cochanina drove the Volcano Lord out of the People of the Springs over a thousand years ago, according to Natlan/History.

Culture: The tribe has long served as guides and cartographers. Its people like to bathe in hot springs with their Koholasaurs, fish together, listen to music and relax; the region is regarded as a vacation spot.

The first chief, in legend, set out for a mysterious island, gave up the 'outcome' to save his companions, came home empty-handed and realised he had already found the treasure; with his companions he founded Meztli. Surfing runs through the tribe's image: the ancient Pyro Archon Cochanina is remembered as a surfing champion (the weapon text Surf's Up), which is why the wiki assumes she was one of the springs' people.

History: The People of the Springs are one of Natlan's six tribes. Natlan/History says Cochanina drove the Volcano Lord out of their land over a thousand years ago. Tupac, a giant of the tribe, fought beside Tenoch against the Abyss five hundred years ago and later died of its taint or his wounds.

The quest The Mysterious Island's Truth, part of Mualani's story, takes the Traveler into the Underground Lava River, the true location of the legendary island; there Vulcanite, a rare golden crystal formed by rapidly cooled Liquid Phlogiston, appears only when volcanic activity begins and is swallowed by the lava almost immediately.

According to legend the Upper Sanctum (Hanan Pacha) was raised by Waxaklahun Ubah Kan and his disciple Chaac so that those who passed their trials could be taught Phlogiston, and those people became the first human tribe. In the world quest Seeker No Finding the Traveler completes the trials and finds a hidden island with a Phlogiston hot spring; the NPC Chikya says a hero accepted by the trials can gain the power to wield Phlogiston by bathing in it.

Atmosphere: Steam over warm pools, music in the plaza, holidaymakers and the glow of lava below the cave floors. Official text sums up the tribe as renowned for hot springs and relaxing music.

Dangers: Hostile Koholasaurs and Yumkasaurs, wild fighters of the Flowing Blade and Swiftstep bands, and lava or Liquid Phlogiston which rapidly drains HP. The boss is the Secret Source Automaton: Configuration Device.

The Underground Lava River periodically fills with lava, and it is unclear how the Koholasaurs that live there cope. Flow-Inverted Wayob Manifestations are elite enemies in Ameyalco Waters.

Travel: Koholasaurs swim in water and liquid Phlogiston, leap from eddies and ride Spiritways; Mualani can do the same (a gameplay mechanic). The Upper Sanctum is reached by activating a Spiritway.

Quests: Tribal Chronicles: Where the Springs Return (Mualani's story), including The Mysterious Island's Truth. World quest series: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire (Tracer No Tracing and Seeker No Finding), which opens the Upper Sanctum.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and Toyac Springs is the most popular holiday stop in Natlan.

The Abyss assault on Natlan ended in 5.3. The tribe lost Atea, who died of Abyssal poisoning in Chapter V, as well as Inna and Kwame in the invasion; Awhina, Haronga and Uturunku survive or die depending on a player choice.

Atea had been stabbed by an Abyssal monster; doctors saved her life but could no longer let her bathe in hot water because Abyssal power remained in her body. The wiki lists no changes at Toyac Springs in 6.x or 7.x.

221.comment: Toyac Springs: People of the Springs
221.content: The People of the Springs (Meztli) are one of Natlan's six tribes. Their chief is Amina. They live along Toyac Springs with Koholasaurs and are known as guides and cartographers.

222.comment: Toyac Springs: The Upper Sanctum (Hanan Pacha)
222.content: Hanan Pacha, the Upper Sanctum, is a group of floating islands in the sky above Ameyalco Waters, held together by Phlogiston. Legend says Waxaklahun Ubah Kan created it as a site to share Phlogiston with humanity. Today it is a ring of smaller islands, accessible only by activating a Spiritway; its ancient trials are made of Spiritways and Iridescent Inscriptions. The name is also an Inca term for the upper world.

223.content: An underground cavern full of Liquid Phlogiston that shows periodic volcanic activity. It is the real location of the 'Mysterious Island' from the People of the Springs' legends, as revealed in The Mysterious Island's Truth. Koholasaurs live in the cave.

224.content:
Underground Lava River (also: Lava River, Underground Lava River: Upper Level, Underground Lava River: Lower Level): The Underground Lava River is a cavern under Ameyalco Waters in Toyac Springs, Natlan, filled with liquid Phlogiston and subject to periodic eruptions. It is the only known source of Vulcanite, a rare golden crystal formed when liquid phlogiston cools quickly; this glow is what the People of the Springs' legend of the 'Mysterious Island' points toward. Koholasaurs live here, and an old trial door in its ruins opens a Spiritway to the Upper Sanctum.

The cave is the setting for two 5.0 quests: Mualani's Journey to the Mysterious Island and Chikya's Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire.

Geography: The cavern has an upper and a lower level and a hot, lava-filled maze. It begins with a cave south of the Ameyalco Waters Statue of the Seven, where a trial ruin sits with its Phlogiston Engravings, a half-opened Spiritdoor and a Spiritway on the edge of reality. Deeper in the lava pools, Spinel Fruit grows, a plant said to flourish near lava.

In The Mysterious Island's Truth the way down is a giant whirlpool that is switched on by Phlogiston nodes and returns at dawn; underneath the water, Viramdra theorises that the Spiritways affected the lava deep underground, creating temporary holes through which the water's current carried the party into the cave.

History: The People of the Springs' legend tells of a first chief who sought a 'mysterious island' that shone like gold. Viramdra, a researcher, recognises the description: the shine is Vulcanite, a mineral formed when large amounts of lava are cooled quickly, which appears only as fierce volcanic activity begins and is promptly swallowed by the flow. The golden glow is a warning of an impending eruption.

The first chief's hidden message on a statue explains that he chased the 'result' for years and reached the glow with his friends, but turned back at the final peril. He returned empty-handed and realised the treasure he most wanted was his friends' safety; he called this, and the tribe's present home, his real 'mysterious island'.

Mualani tells the party the map says: when you see the golden light, go the opposite way. Viramdra ignores that and runs in for the ore just as the lava becomes active again; Mualani crosses the lava on her surfboard to bring him back, and when the flow nears the party she whistles for Koholasaurs that carry everyone out. Mualani's lesson from the trip is to value companions over results, and Nuu says that those who understood the chief's intent have chosen not to boast.

People: Mualani, the People of the Springs' young guide, leads the Journey to the Mysterious Island with Viramdra, Karya and the Traveler; her teacher Nuu appears at the end. Chikya enters the lava ruin in Tracer No Tracing. The cavern's only residents are creatures: Koholasaurs and Koholasaur Whelps, with Fluid Avatars of Lava as hazards.

Quests: Where the Springs Return, Act III (The Mysterious Island's Truth, story quest, 5.0): the party reaches the cave, argues over Vulcanite and the chief's message. Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire (world quest, 5.0): Tracer No Tracing starts here, Seeker No Finding follows in the Upper Sanctum.

In Tracer No Tracing the party finds Unveiling Scripts, using an indwelling Koholasaurus and Aquadash to fetch one, and fights a Fluid Avatar of Lava. The Spiritdoor then half-opens and the party rides a Spiritway out of the lava. Chikya remembers an old scroll of ancestors swimming in lava and thinks it might have been a warning to trial-takers.

Atmosphere: Hot, gold-lit, humid and unsteady: lava pools and glowing ore, a quiet stone ruin, and the constant risk that the flow is about to rise.

Dangers: Rising lava and eruptions, Large Pyro Slimes and Fluid Avatars of Lava, a Secret Source Automaton: Hunter-Seeker guarding the Tracer ruin, and falls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern remains hot and active, with Koholasaurs living in it. Vulcanite still cannot be brought back, and the Spiritway trial is solved.

No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here.

225.content: Vulcanite is a rare, glowing golden crystal formed when liquid Phlogiston cools quickly. It forms at the start of fierce volcanic activity and is almost at once swallowed by the lava, so it appears impossible to obtain. The cavern under Ameyalco Waters is its only known site. Viramdra had hoped the ore would prove his theory, but concluded in the end that it can never be taken out.

key: first chief of the People of the Springs
226.comment: Underground Lava River: The People of the Springs' Mysterious Island
226.content: The legend of the Mysterious Island is the rite of passage of the People of the Springs' guides: a map says the island shines like gold and warns to go the opposite way from the golden light. Mualani's story quest shows that the golden light comes from Vulcanite in a lava cave and that the first chief's true 'island' was the tribe's home, the small island on which it was founded, which later coastlines turned into what it is today. Nuu says guides who understand this choose whether to share it or keep the legend for future guides.

227.content:
Varesa's Orchard: Varesa's Orchard is a family orchard just outside the "Collective of Plenty" tribe's settlement in Atocpan, Natlan. It belongs to Varesa and is guarded by her Tatankasaur companion, Vanana.

It grows apples, cacahuatl, grainfruit and quenepa berries, and is the only place where red berryshrooms can be found.

Places: The orchard lies right outside the Collective of Plenty. Varesa's house is behind a fruit stand in front, near the tribe's main entrance. On the southern side stands a "Fruits Aplenty" machine.

In the quest "Orchard Repose", Varesa says her family runs a huge orchard and that they live close to the tribe's entrance. The machine prepares a dish when ingredients are submitted and it is struck by a Tatankasaur or a Collective of Plenty character.

People: Varesa owns the orchard; her father is a skilled cook and her Tatankasaur companion Vanana keeps guard and stops visitors from entering until the quest allows it. Her uncle Acatl is the tribe's chief, as she mentions in the quest.

For Varesa's own background, see her character entry rather than repeating it here.

Quests: In "Orchard Repose" the Traveler goes to the orchard with Varesa and picks fruit and vegetables, including the specialty mushroom, for a meal. The quest is part of the "Mushroom Realm Mystery" chain.

The quest follows "Ardent Land of Plenty" and precedes "Sage Supreme". The pick-up objective lists apples, grainfruit, cacahuatl, quenepa berries and the red berryshroom, matching what the orchard grows.

Atmosphere: Fragrant and sunny, with fruit-laden trees, a stand by the road and a large, watchful Tatankasaur at the gate; homely and abundant.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a working orchard, open to the player after the relevant step of Orchard Repose.

228.content: Varesa's Orchard sits outside the Collective of Plenty settlement in Atocpan. Varesa's family grows apples, grainfruit, cacahuatl and quenepa berries there, and her companion Vanana guards it.

229.content:
Villa Guiztli (also: The Town in the Rock): Villa Guiztli is an underground town beneath Guiztli Ridge, a small rocky island in Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It is inhabited by cardboard cutouts and Nochtlins, and offers an immersive experience in which visitors play heroes defending the town from the villain "El Capoctus Joquiratto".

It is unlocked fully by progressing through To Guiztli Ridge!, part of Sunspray Summer Resort Part II. Its viewpoint is titled "The Town in the Rock".

People: Residents seen in idle dialogue are capybaras and alpacas, plus Nochtli lackeys in the villain's service. Before the quest is completed the streets are empty because the lackeys keep robbing the place; the villagers advise lying low.

After completion the capybaras greet guests, remark how lively and beautiful the town is, and an alpaca says peace has been restored. A capybara offers to change the colour of the town, turning buildings into Graffiti Zones or clearing them again.

Atmosphere: A staged, playful theatre-town: wanted signs, bandit lackeys and shouting about an invented outlaw, all set in a cavern. Treat it as an attraction, not a real settlement under threat.

Dangers: Joquiratto Lackeys (Nochtlins) guard chests and attack. A sealed chest challenge, Master Musketeer's Accuracy, asks the player to defeat 14 lackeys across five waves without injuring more than four civilians such as hostage capybaras and alpacas.

History: Guiztli Ridge itself has local figures including a fruit farmer, a guard and Achu. How the town came to exist is not stated; the Joquiratto story is presented as the resort's immersive show.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a permanent explorable subarea of the resort, added in 5.8.

230.content:
Vision Serpent's Sanctum (also: Vision Serpent Sanctum): The Vision Serpent's Sanctum is a site in Ochkanatlan listed beneath the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams. It has a mural and a note written by the Holy Sovereign.

The mural is shown in a gallery before and after being revealed during the world quest Adventure in the Land of Mists.

History: Holy Sovereign's Notes (VII) lies to the right of the mural. The ruler writes that a hostile entity (named on the wiki as Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L) has been imprisoned in a statue but will not obey, and that only draconic blood can operate the ancient machines. He resolves to build a Core of Chu'ulel loyal to humanity alone, by enslaving the draconic part of himself so that it stays imprisoned after his human self dies. The rest is smeared and unreadable.

He writes that no power greater than humanity can be trusted, save one gentle person the wiki links to Xbalanque. This is the ruler's own view, not an objective account. Notes I to VI are in the Old Core of Chu'ulel.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and open for exploration as of 7.1.

The sanctum belongs to the same set of Holy Sovereign's Notes as the earlier ones in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, which together show the ruler's shift from reasoning about waterworks to fearing and confining draconic power; he is the sole named author.

231.content:
Vucub Caquix Tower (also: Fire Parrot Tower): The Vucub Caquix Tower stands in the middle of Ashflow Street in Ochkanatlan. Its lower level, reached by elevator, holds notes from different eras about an expedition into the city and the calamity that ended the old alliance.

The name comes from the Popol Vuh bird demon Vucub Caquix; the Chinese name means Fire Parrot Tower.

Places: There is a wall mural, a door beside which scrolls are kept, and a lower level with an elevator and desks. A hole at the east side of the lower level has a note on a desk near its edge.

People: Four notes can be read. A mountain ranger's journal tells of an expedition guided by Copan's claim that a mechanism in the city leads to the sky-vessel, and laments that a very young Spiritcaller of the Masters of the Night-Wind was allowed to come. A Spiritcaller's note (by the young prodigy Liriwu) says she expected to catch up with Uncle Taika and go on to Cinder City, and that even the Wayob's voices cannot be heard here. A priest's note describes the old alliance's last days. A scholar's note concerns an ancient scroll.

Liriwu names Grand Master Sanhaj as her teacher's teacher and finds no mystic art, healing included, works in the tower, so she doubts even Sanhaj could dispel the curse.

History: The Nameless Priest's note records the Recording Officer Tlamachtihquetl, the craftsman Chupicua avoiding waterway labour with three bags of obsidian, and Manqu taking his place. It then describes repairs halting after a dark calamity submerged the deep well and transformed nearby residents; the Cuauhtli Warriors sealing the entrance and burning the infected with flame borrowed from the Holy Sovereign; an old woman raving about the sun and the alliance's collapse; and commoners blaming the ban on sacrifices to the Lord of the Night. Chichiri tried to persuade them. The writer ends barricaded with sheltering children, holding a gate.

The Traveling Scholar's note reasons that an ancient scroll from the era of the One Entombed With the Primal Fire shows dragon artisans made a weapon able to annihilate the Abyss, and mentions a treasure ship moored above Cinder City. The scholar later writes that they were all deceived about the treasure's essence; the rest is torn away.

Dangers: The ranger's journal warns that Abyssal erosion has ruined roads, that earlier missing adventurers were found beyond help, and that the city must be entered to reach the sky-vessel. Liriwu considers the place cursed.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and silent as of 7.1; open for exploration.

The tower's notes span at least three periods: the alliance's final days, an ancient scroll's era, and the recent expedition. They share one theme, that hopes of salvation (a weapon, a treasure, a rescue) failed in Ochkanatlan.

232.content:
Wavey Bay: Wavey Bay is the seaside subarea of Easybreeze Holiday Resort in Natlan, known for sandy beaches, pristine waters and many aquatic attractions.

The main facilities are announced on info boards: The Twilight Cruise, Rainbow Beams, the Razzle-Dazzle Mega Slide and Asha Speedrun.

Places: The Twilight Cruise is a cooperative ship-guiding game requiring timing and teamwork. Rainbow Beams is a paint-ball matching shooter. The Razzle-Dazzle Mega Slide is a seaside glide along the Spiritway. Asha Speedrun is a challenging race across a chosen route, suited to sporty tourists.

Before the matching story quests (Time to Test the Twilight Cruise!, To Wavey Bay!, Time to Test the Asha Speedrun!) the info boards mark the facility as awaiting testing and ask visitors to find the staff for closed testing; afterwards they read "Operating". Five boards stand around the bay, one beside "Muchih" and one near each major attraction.

People: Listed residents are "Muchih", Aqo, Chatubaya, Hayaq, Hemaki, Jayubal, Kalane, Poteh, Quemitl, Tuksina, Tzapan and Wachana.

Quests: Story quests: Sunspray Summer Resort Part II (The World Is Your Canvas!, To Wavey Bay!, Time to Test the Twilight Cruise!, Time to Test the Asha Speedrun!). World quests: Shine On, Pipilpan Idol! and The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc.

History: A sung note found here, addressed to Tecuhtli, warns of three things: Black Boar Rekis probably sending men to grab Asha, Icahua possibly lurking nearby as a sharp, sneaky shot, and that the second warning is the most important. It ties into the pirate plot also seen on Tete Isle.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a permanent explorable subarea added in 5.8.

233.content:
Weary Inn (also: Inn of Lassitude): The Weary Inn is a restaurant and hotel in one, on the outskirts of the Chuwen Fair in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame (Warrior's Rest Area), Natlan. It offers free lodging and food to warriors taking part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame.

Its owner is Chanca, a former contestant who once stayed here for free herself. She also runs the food stall Zakan's Street Bites near the entrance.

Places: Located in the Warrior's Rest Area of the Stadium, beside the Chuwen Fair. Per the official map text, the name was chosen in the hope that warriors would leave their weariness at the inn and walk into the Stadium full of energy.

The stall at the entrance sells the inn's cooking to anyone, not only contestants, and teaches recipes such as Tatacos.

People: Chanca, owner. A guest, Vitusov, a visitor whose origin the wiki lists as Snezhnaya, is seen here musing about a half-hour clean-plate challenge on a triple portion of Surf, Turf and Perch.

Every manager of the inn is said to be selected and designated by the Speaker's Chamber, which ties it to the Pilgrimage's organisers. Chanca says that anyone who knows a contestant can stay with them and eat and sleep at the inn on the house.

Governance: The Speaker's Chamber appoints the inn's managers, per the in-game description. Contestants' costs are covered; others pay for food at the stall.

Atmosphere: Hearty, noisy and unpretentious: large high-calorie meals, tired fighters and old comrades trading stories.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1 under Chanca.

After the Pilgrimage's battles ended, Chanca says many old comrades come by for meals; because of her old injuries she cannot help them in other ways, so she feeds them. The remark becomes available after the quest No One Fights Alone.

Canon gives the inn no named founder or history beyond the map description. Chanca recalls staying here free of charge as a contestant, so the arrangement predates her ownership.

234.content:
Well of Seven Flames: The Well of Seven Flames is a point of interest on Ashflow Street in Ochkanatlan, Natlan. Canon read gives no description of it beyond its name and place on the map.

It was added in version 5.2 along with Ochkanatlan.

Places: It lies within Ochkanatlan, along Ashflow Street. The English name refers to a well and seven flames, but no source read explains either.

Other languages render the name similarly, as a well of seven flames or seven burning wells, so the number seven is part of the official name in several translations.

Atmosphere: Use only the setting: the fiery, ashen underground world of Ochkanatlan. Any specific look or ritual would be invention.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 there is no further information. Canon does not state its history, use or condition.

Treat questions about its origin as unknown in character rather than inventing an answer.

235.comment: Well of Seven Flames: Well of Seven Flames
235.content: The Well of Seven Flames is a named point of interest on Ashflow Street in Ochkanatlan with no description in canon read. Its purpose is unknown.

236.content:
Xalac Vale (also: Xalac Valley): Xalac Vale is a river valley in Natlan. It extends from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to the Flower-Feather Clan's lands, and on its north side it runs past the Masters of the Night-Wind. It is a travel corridor between the tribes rather than a settlement, and canon says little more about it.

It is a minor point of interest, added with Natlan in Version 5.2, within the Tezcatepetonco Range area.

Geography: The in-game description calls it a river valley. Its stretch links three known points: the Stadium of the Sacred Flame at one end, the Flower-Feather Clan at the other, and the Masters of the Night-Wind alongside its northern side. The name Xalac is of Nahuatl-style origin: roughly "sand" plus "water" with a locative ending, so something like "place of sand and water" (a wiki etymology, not an in-game explanation).

Its location between the Stadium and the Flower-Feather Clan makes it a natural line of travel between two of Natlan's tribal territories. Exact boundaries, the river's name and its course are not given in canon read.

Travel: A notice posted in the vale advertises the Pakpaka Flying School and invites passers-by to sign up for flying lessons now rather than waiting for the next flying contest, which are held from time to time. This suggests gliding and flight training are part of local life, but the notice is the only detail given.

Atmosphere: For a scene, treat it as open Natlan river country: a waterway winding between tribal territories, with travellers heading to or from the Stadium and the Flower-Feather Clan, and the Night-Wind lands visible to the north. Anything beyond that (specific residents, ruins, wildlife) would be invention; use sparingly and do not present it as canon.

237.comment: Xalac Vale: Pakpaka Flying School Notice
237.content: An in-game notice in Xalac Vale urges readers to earn their wings at the Pakpaka Flying School and notes that flying contests are held now and then, so there is no need to wait to sign up. No other facts about the school are given in this notice.

238.content:
Xocolatl Beverages: Xocolatl Beverages is a juice bar in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan, run by Yantasar of the Masters of the Night-Wind. It specialises in unconventional drinks made from fresh fruit and spices, which locals enjoy.

Yantasar sells the idea as much as the drink: she advertises blessings of the Wayob and a taste as light as a Qucusaurus feather floating into the clouds.

People: Yantasar is the owner. Asked about it, she admits there is nothing special in the drinks beyond good, healthy ingredients; the draw is that they sound strange and people leave feeling elated. Natlan natives, she says, like that kind of thing.

When the Traveler asks for something ordinary she falls silent for a long time, unable to picture an ordinary drink, and offers Grainfruit Meat Soup as a compromise.

Culture: The shop is an example of Natlan's playful food culture, where the novelty of a dish is part of its charm. The name comes from xocolatl, a Nahuatl word for a cacao drink, per the wiki's trivia note.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1; nothing about it has changed in canon.

The stall sits within the Stadium near the Temple of Pax. Scenes should keep it light and visitor-facing.

Yantasar is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. Her idle remark that the drinks "can't taste that bad" and her admission that nothing special is in them make her salesmanship self-aware; she is sincere about ingredient quality. Whether alcohol is served is only implied by another NPC's remark and stays unconfirmed.

239.content:
Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner (also: Cozy Corner): Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner is a small store in the People of the Springs' area of Toyac Springs, Natlan, that offers psychotherapy through dream-eating yumekui-baku. It is presumably owned by Yumemizuki Mizuki, the Inazuman clinical psychologist and Aisa Bathhouse shareholder, and is currently staffed by a baku named Mint Daifuku.

A message board outside advertises that negative emotions can seep into dreams and that visitors on holiday can soothe lingering worries here. It also announces that the Natlan branch of Aisa Bathhouse was already under construction.

People: Mint Daifuku, a small floating mint-green baku with a white stripe on its belly, keeps the shop while its owner is away. It communicates only in squeaks, which the narration interprets: it greets the Traveler warmly, seems to treat them as a close partner of the owner, and is shy when patted.

Yumemizuki Mizuki is not on site; she has her own entry.

Culture: The shop brings Mizuki's Inazuman therapeutic practice to Natlan, as part of the same wellness venture as Aisa Bathhouse. Its services depend on baku devouring nightmares.

Atmosphere: Quiet, soft and slightly whimsical, with a restful, spa-like mood.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, minded by Mint Daifuku. The owner is not present.

The Natlan Aisa Bathhouse branch was only "under construction" in the board text; its later status is not covered here.

The message board texts cycle through several short notices when read; only the introduction was read here. Mint Daifuku shares its model with the Dough King, a wiki observation rather than lore, and the name is a pun on the Japanese sweet daifuku.

240.content:
Zakan's Street Bites (also: Zakan's Food Stall): Zakan's Street Bites is a food stall near the Weary Inn's entrance in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Natlan. Run by Chanca, it is described as Natlan's main restaurant and sells hearty meals, ingredients and recipes.

Chanca's personal specialty is Tatacos, a dish she says almost everyone in Natlan knows how to make.

People: Chanca, a former Pilgrimage contestant affiliated with the Scions of the Canopy, runs the stall and the Weary Inn. She is friendly and generous, and would rather teach a recipe than hand over a finished dish.

She says injuries from her fighting days limit what she can do now, so feeding old comrades is how she helps.

Economy: Gameplay detail: the stall is open at all hours and sells daily-stocked dishes such as Cup O' Grainfruit, Grainfruit Meat Soup, Tatacos and Blazed Meat Stew, weekly cooking ingredients, and recipes including Cup O' Grainfruit, Grainfruit Meat Soup, Xocoatl and Magmic Ode. Reaching top reputation with two of the six Natlan tribes earns a permanent 10% discount.

Atmosphere: Busy and cheerful, serving the Stadium's crowd of contestants, spectators and visitors.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1 under Chanca.

Zakan's identity is unexplained in the canon read.

Chanca also says she left fighting after old injuries, and that Tatacos is easy enough that she teaches it rather than serving it. The stall's Natlan-wide status as the main restaurant comes from the wiki's description, not from in-game text read here.
